# Typography

Type is a closed vocabulary of paired utilities. Each one bundles size, weight, line-height and tracking, and is picked by role rather than by size.

**6 families · 8 everyday tiers · 2 text colors · 1 utility per text node**

## The everyday set

Product UI is built almost entirely from these eight. Reach outside them on purpose.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `text-heading-1` | 36px · 600 | The page title. Exactly one per route. |
| `text-heading-2` | 28px · 600 | A major section of the page. |
| `text-title-lg` | 16px · 600 | Names a component: card, dialog, sheet, list row. |
| `text-title-sm` | 14px · 600 | Names a dense component: compact card, table section. |
| `text-body-md` | 15px · 400 | The default paragraph, description and help text. |
| `text-body-sm` | 13px · 400 | Secondary copy and table cells. |
| `text-label-lg` | 14px · 600 | Buttons, field labels, tabs. |
| `text-caption` | 12px · 400 | Timestamps, footnotes, meta rows. |

## The six families

Every tier belongs to one family, and the family is the decision. Size follows from it.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `Display  display-lg…4xl` | 48–120px · 700–800 | Type as image: landing heroes, campaign numbers. Never in product chrome; never two per view. |
| `Heading  heading-1…4` | 36 / 28 / 22 / 18px · 600 | The document outline (h1–h4). Keep the order; never skip a level to get a size. |
| `Title  title-lg · title-sm` | 16 / 14px · 600 | Names a UI part without claiming a document heading. |
| `Body  body-lg/md/sm/xs` | 17 / 15 / 13 / 12px · 400 | Reading text. -lg is the lede (carries text-wrap: pretty); -xs is a dense-UI floor, not a prose size. |
| `Label  label-lg/md/sm · caption` | 14 / 12 / 11px · 600; caption 12 · 400 | Functional, scannable text of one to three words. Caption is also the group-label tier: nav sections, menu groups. |
| `Mono  mono-xl/lg/md/caption/sm` | 28 / 20 / 13 / 12 / 11px · tabular | Numbers that are the content, IDs, hashes, code, aligned figures. |

## Text color

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `text-foreground` | full contrast | Primary text: headings, body, values. |
| `text-muted-foreground` | secondary contrast (AA on every surface) | Supporting text: descriptions, captions, meta, placeholders. |

## Rules

1. **One paired utility per text node. Compose it with a color and margin only.** Each utility is a tuned set of size, weight, leading and tracking. Splitting it into text-* + font-* + tracking-* breaks the tuning and every theme override of it. *Enforced by sable-lint: decomposed-type.*
2. **Pick the tier by role, not by the size it renders at.** A card title is title-lg even when body-lg is the same size: role fixes the weight (600 vs 400) and the rhythm around it.
3. **Two text colors: foreground and muted-foreground.** Both are contrast-tested against every surface in every theme. A third grey, or an opacity step, is untested contrast.
4. **One heading-1 per route; headings descend without skipping levels.** The heading outline is how screen-reader users navigate a page. Restyle with a tier rather than jumping a level for its size.
5. **Hierarchy comes from a clear jump (heading → title → body), then weight and space, before size.** Two sizes one step apart read as the same level. Space and weight separate levels more cheaply than another size.
6. **Cap reading text at --measure-prose (65ch).** Past roughly 75 characters the eye loses the line return. A wide region can still hold a 65ch column.
7. **Numbers that must align use a mono tier (tabular figures).** Proportional digits change width as values update, so totals and columns shimmy.
8. **text-wrap: balance on headings, pretty on ledes, neither on long prose.** balance evens short headlines; pretty only refuses a one-word last line. Both cost layout work that long prose does not repay.
9. **A mark attached to a line of type (a dot, a bullet, a timeline marker, a leading icon) sits in a box one line tall (h-[1lh] items-center) and is sized in em.** 1lh is the line-height of the text beside it, so the mark centres on that line in every tier, density and theme. A px size with a mt-[3px] nudge is right for one font at one size and wrong everywhere else.

## Never

- **Never:** Opacity on text (text-foreground/60, opacity-70 on a paragraph). **Instead:** text-muted-foreground. An alpha step over an unknown surface has unknown contrast, and it shifts per theme. *Enforced by sable-lint: text-opacity.*
- **Never:** A hand-picked size, weight or tracking (text-[15px], font-medium, tracking-wide). **Instead:** The paired utility for the role. Off-vocabulary type cannot be retuned by a theme or the customizer, so it drifts the moment either changes. *Enforced by sable-lint: decomposed-type.*
- **Never:** Uppercase in product chrome: nav and menu group labels, page eyebrows, table headers, section titles. **Instead:** Sentence-case text-caption or text-label-md in muted-foreground; hierarchy from size, weight and space. Tracked capitals spread across a UI read as shouting and slow word recognition. The eyebrow tier (label-xs / overline) is an editorial accent: at most one per marketing view.
- **Never:** Display tiers inside product UI, or two display sizes in one view. **Instead:** heading-1 for a page title; mono-xl for a metric. Display is type as image. In chrome it competes with the content it is supposed to frame.
- **Never:** Justified text, or reading copy below body-sm. **Instead:** Ragged-right at body-md; body-xs only for dense data. Justification opens rivers on the web, which has no hyphenation control; 12px prose fails people with low vision.
- **Never:** A new font family, or raw font-feature-settings / font-variation-settings. **Instead:** The theme's sans, mono and optional display; font-variant-numeric and font-weight. Raw axis tags silently do nothing on a fallback font, and every theme declares a fallback stack.

## Details

### Steady numbers

```tsx
// before
<span className="text-body-md">{price}</span>
// after
<span className="text-mono-md">{price}</span>
```

Mono tiers set tabular-nums, so a ticking value stops nudging its neighbors sideways.

### Optically centred labels

```tsx
// before
<button className="h-(--control-md) px-4 items-center">Save</button>
// after
<Button>Save</Button>  {/* label wrapped in .sable-label-trim */}
```

text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic centres the cap-height band the eye reads, not the line box. Measured: Helvetica otherwise sits a full 1px high on a 40px control.

### A marker centred on its line

```tsx
// before
<span className="mt-[5px] size-2 rounded-full bg-primary" />
// after
<span className="flex h-[1lh] items-center"><span className="size-[0.5em] rounded-full bg-primary" /></span>
```

The wrapper is exactly one line of the adjacent text tall, so the dot centres on the first line whatever the tier; em sizing keeps it in proportion when the type scales. Stepper indicator="dot" is built this way.

### Balanced headings

```tsx
// before
<h2 className="text-heading-2">Ship faster with fewer review rounds</h2>
// after
<h2 className="text-heading-2 text-balance">Ship faster with fewer review rounds</h2>
```

Evens line lengths so a two-line heading does not end on a single orphaned word.

### Secondary text without opacity

```tsx
// before
<p className="text-foreground/60">Updated 2m ago</p>
// after
<p className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">Updated 2m ago</p>
```

muted-foreground is contrast-tested on every surface; a 60% alpha is not.

**Related:** `sable docs spacing` · `sable docs accessibility` · `sable token typography` · `sable token typographyOverrides`

---

# Spacing & sizing

One 4px scale governs every gap, inset and size, and space is assigned by role. Controls read a height ladder that a density scope can retune all at once.

**4px base · 8px rhythm · 3 roles · 1 control ladder**

## Spacing by role

Steps below 2 (8px) are optical correction only.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `Inset  p-4` | 16px | Padding inside a surface. p-3 for a dense card, px-3 py-2 for a row. |
| `Stack, within a group  gap-1.5 – gap-2` | 6–8px | Label to field, title to description. |
| `Stack, between groups  gap-4 – gap-6` | 16–24px | Field to field, card to card. |
| `Stack, between sections  gap-12+` | 48px+ | Major regions of a page. |
| `Inline  gap-2 – gap-3` | 8–12px | Icon to label, control to control. |

## The control ladder

Comfortable values; data-density="compact" (or <Density>) redefines every step for a region.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `h-(--control-xs)` | 28px · compact 24 | Inline chips, tree rows. |
| `h-(--control-sm)` | 32px · compact 28 | Compact buttons, toolbar controls. |
| `h-(--control-md)` | 40px · compact 32 | The default: inputs, buttons, selects, menu triggers. |
| `h-(--control-cta)` | 44px · compact 36 | The primary call to action; clears the touch floor on its own. |
| `h-(--control-lg)` | 48px · compact 40 | Prominent or touch-first actions. |

## Icons and touch

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `text-base (16px)` | sm | Inline with label-md / body-sm. |
| `text-xl (20px)` | md · default | The default UI glyph beside label-lg. |
| `hit-target` | 44×44px | Keeps a visually small control's hit area at the WCAG floor without moving layout. |

## Rules

1. **Every margin, padding and gap is a step on the 4px scale.** Off-scale values break the rhythm that lets adjacent components line up without coordination.
2. **Padding, gaps and insets in a component sit on the spacing scale: a step (p-4, gap-2) or --spacing(n) inside an arbitrary value (p-[var(--card-p,--spacing(6))]).** The density (Character) control works by retuning --spacing, so anything on the scale moves with it. A literal p-[1.5rem] or padding: "12px" stays put while everything around it tightens. Keep fixed rem/px for what must not scale: a 1px hairline, a ring width. *Enforced by design-lint: fixed-spacing (library source).*
3. **Related things sit closer than unrelated things.** Proximity groups content without a divider line. Use space first; reach for a border only when space is not enough.
4. **Space lives on the container (gap), not on children (margins).** gap survives reordering, conditional children and RTL; per-child margins do not.
5. **Control heights read the --control-* ladder.** A density scope retunes every control at once. A hardcoded height has to be found and overridden by hand. *Enforced by sable-lint: raw-control-height.*
6. **Single-column content inside a card stacks with flex flex-col and a gap, not CSS grid.** A grid track sizes to its widest min-content child, so one long unbreakable string (a URL, a code line, a table) blows the column out past the card. A flex column lets children shrink to the card.
7. **A compact surface drops one whole step; a spacious one adds one.** Moving in whole steps keeps density changes proportional.
8. **Every interactive element clears a 44×44px hit area.** WCAG 2.5.5. Use padding or hit-target to grow the hit area; never a bigger glyph.
9. **Borderless controls get roughly twice the gap of bordered ones.** A border declares where a control ends. Two ghost buttons 12px apart read as one target.

## Never

- **Never:** Arbitrary values: p-[15px], gap-[7px], mt-[13px]. **Instead:** The nearest scale step. Arbitrary values cannot follow density or a customized scale.
- **Never:** h-[40px] on a control. **Instead:** h-(--control-md). It will not follow <Density>. *Enforced by sable-lint: raw-control-height.*
- **Never:** Icons sized with type utilities (text-body-md on an <Icon>). **Instead:** text-{size} scale classes. Type utilities carry line-height and tracking that misalign glyphs.
- **Never:** A fixed width sized to an English label. **Instead:** padding-inline and max-width with wrapping. German and Finnish run 30–50% longer.

## Details

### A dense region in one attribute

```tsx
// before
<div className="[&_button]:h-8 [&_input]:h-8">…</div>
// after
<Density value="compact">…</Density>
```

Every control, menu and popup inside retunes, including portaled overlays.

### Grouping by space

```tsx
// before
<Separator /> between every field
// after
<Stack gap={3}> between groups (24px), <Stack gap={1}> inside a group (8px)
```

Two spacing steps do the work of every divider, with less ink. Stack's numeric gap counts --rhythm-unit — two spacing steps — so it follows the density control like every other spacing value.

**Related:** `sable docs shape` · `sable docs typography` · `sable docs building-a-tool` · `sable token layout`

---

# Shape

Radius signals what something is: tight on containers, full on actions. Nested corners stay concentric, and one edge treatment marks a boundary.

**7 radius steps · concentric nesting · 1 edge treatment per boundary**

## The radius ladder

Each step is 4px apart, so common insets land on a real step. Themes and the customizer retune every step together.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `rounded-none` | 0 | Full-bleed media. |
| `rounded-xs` | 4px | Tags, kbd, small inline marks. |
| `rounded-sm` | 8px | Inputs, menu items, list rows. |
| `rounded-md` | 12px | Popovers, menus, toasts. |
| `rounded-lg` | 16px | Cards, dialogs, sheets. |
| `rounded-xl` | 20px | Hero surfaces. |
| `rounded-full` | pill | Buttons (via --button-radius), avatars, pills, dots. |

## Edges

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `border-border` | hairline | The default edge: inputs, cards, badges. |
| `border-border-strong` | hairline, higher contrast | Structural rules: table grids, section separators. |
| `border-border-floating` | faint, alpha | Every floating surface: popovers, menus, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets, toasts. Lighter than border; the shadow carries the elevation. |
| `ring-2 ring-ring` | 2px focus ring | Focus only. Never a thick border. |

## Rules

1. **Nested corners are concentric: inner radius = outer radius − inset. Write it as rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset>, not a hardcoded step.** A 12px popover with 4px padding takes 8px items. The utility computes the subtraction from the live tokens, so the pair stays concentric when a theme or the customizer rescales the radius ladder; a hardcoded rounded-sm drifts.
2. **A list of rows inside a rounded popup uses popup-inset on the popup, rounded-popup-item on the rows and popup-bleed on a separator.** All three derive from the popup's radius: the inset grows to a third of it (never below --spacing(1), so density moves it too), the rows take what is left after the inset and the 1px border, and a separator bleeds by exactly the inset. A rounder look gets more room instead of rows that round into pills; the default ladder lands on a 4px inset and 7px rows. *Enforced by sable-lint: popup-separator-bleed.*
3. **A Button, Pill or Badge gets its look from a variant, never from override classes.** border, bg, rounded, ring and shadow classes on a component fight the variant's own hover, selected and focus states, and give one call site a look no other site can ask for. Use the variant that exists (Button variant="floating" over content, "on-color" on a fill; Pill appearance="outline"; Badge appearance and tone) or add one to the component. *Enforced by sable-lint: component-restyle.*
4. **The outer radius is always at least the inner radius.** If the inset is larger than the outer radius, square the inner element or step the container up.
5. **Never mix radii within one component.** A component reads as one object when its corners agree.
6. **Actions are full; containers are tight.** The contrast itself says 'this is a control'. A theme flattens buttons through --button-radius, not by editing each one.
7. **High-contrast outlines (selection, emphasis) are inset rings; hairline chrome is a border.** Rings anti-alias on rounded corners at any display scale; a 1px light border on dark snaps to the pixel grid and looks jagged.
8. **One edge treatment per boundary: a border, a ring or a shadow.** Stacking all three makes an edge heavier than the content it holds.
9. **Prefer a tonal step or space over a divider line.** The flattest thing that reads is best.

## Never

- **Never:** rounded-[10px] or any off-ladder radius. **Instead:** The ladder step for the role. Off-ladder radii cannot follow a theme or the customizer's radius control.
- **Never:** A card inside a card with the same radius. **Instead:** Flatten the inner one, or use rounded-concentric-*. Nested surfaces with equal corners look misaligned at every corner.
- **Never:** <Button className="rounded-full">, <Pill className="border bg-card">, a -mx-1 separator in a popup. **Instead:** The component's variant (add one if it is missing); popup-bleed for the separator. An override fights the component's own states and does not follow the radius ladder, the density or a theme. *Enforced by sable-lint: component-restyle, popup-separator-bleed.*
- **Never:** border-2 for emphasis or focus. **Instead:** ring-2 ring-ring for focus; a tonal fill for emphasis. A thick border shifts layout and competes with the focus ring.

## Details

### Crisp selected outlines on dark surfaces

```tsx
// before
<button className="rounded-lg border border-foreground">
// after
<button className="rounded-lg ring-[1.5px] ring-foreground ring-inset">
```

A 1px high-contrast border on a rounded corner snaps unevenly at fractional device-pixel ratios (Windows 125%/150%) and reads as jagged, worst light-on-dark. A box-shadow ring is anti-aliased instead, and inset keeps it from changing the element's size. Keep hairline borders for low-contrast chrome, where the snapping is invisible.

### Concentric menu items

```tsx
// before
<div className="rounded-md p-1"><div className="rounded-md">Item</div></div>
// after
<div className="rounded-md popup-inset"><div className="rounded-popup-item">Item</div></div>
```

12px outer − 4px inset = 8px inner at the default ladder, and the utilities keep the subtraction right when a preset or the customizer rescales the radius or the density.

**Related:** `sable docs surfaces` · `sable docs spacing` · `sable token radii`

---

# Surfaces & elevation

Depth is a step up the surface ladder, chosen by how transient a surface is. Dark mode lifts with lighter tones and edge light; light mode adds soft shadows.

**4 surface tokens · 5 elevation roles · 1 shadow per surface · 1 layer scale**

## The surface ladder

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `bg-background` | the page | The document body; the furthest-back surface. |
| `bg-card` | +1 step | Resting containers: cards, panels, dialogs. |
| `bg-muted` | +1 step, quieter | Wells, code blocks, inactive fills inside a card. |
| `bg-popover` | +2 steps | Anything that floats: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips. Always distinct from card, so a menu in a dialog never melts into it. |
| `bg-overlay` | scrim | Behind modals, and pills over imagery. |

## Elevation by role

Raise by transience — how much a surface floats over content — not by importance.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `Resting` | no shadow | Page content and flat cards. A hairline border if it needs an edge. |
| `Raised  shadow-sm` | subtle | A draggable card, a sticky header over scrolled content. |
| `Floating  shadow-md` | anchored | Menus, popovers, selects, dropdowns. |
| `Modal  shadow-lg` | with scrim | Dialogs, sheets, the command menu. |
| `Top  shadow-xl` | rare | The toast stack. |

## Layers

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `z-(--z-sticky)` | 30 | Sticky in-content chrome: table headers. |
| `z-(--z-nav)` | 40 | App chrome: header, sidebar, bottom nav. |
| `z-(--z-overlay)` | 50 | Every portaled transient surface. |
| `z-(--z-toast)` | 60 | Toasts, above modals. |
| `z-(--z-skip-link)` | 100 | The skip link, above everything. |

## Rules

1. **Pick the elevation role, not a shadow value.** Elevation is a five-step system. A custom box-shadow cannot follow a theme or the light/dark split.
2. **Floating surfaces use bg-popover, resting ones bg-card. Anything with shadow-md or above floats: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets, toasts, a floating panel.** In dark mode popover is guaranteed lighter than card, so a menu opened inside a dialog always reads as on top of it. In light mode several presets make background, card and popover the same colour, so the fill alone never carries elevation. *Enforced by themes.test.ts + sable-lint: floating-surface.*
3. **A floating surface's edge is border-border-floating (or ring-border-floating), never the full border-border. The shadow carries the elevation.** A full hairline plus a shadow stacks into a heavy dark outline. border-floating is a faint alpha edge: it defines the shape against a same-coloured page in light mode and reads as a lit edge in dark mode, where shadows barely show. *Enforced by sable-lint: floating-surface.*
4. **A recessed area inside a surface (a segmented-control track, a pad, a preview well) is sable-well, and it takes no outline. Whatever sits on the well takes the surface's own colour back (bg-popover inside a popover).** sable-well mixes a fixed amount of ink into the surface it sits in, so it is the same visible step on the page, in a card or in a floating panel, in every theme and mode. A fixed bg-muted can nearly vanish inside a popover in dark mode, and adding an outline to every well to compensate stacks a panel into boxes.
5. **One shadow per surface; never a heavy shadow with a heavy border.** Stacked depth cues read as decoration rather than position.
6. **Do not elevate a static section to make it stand out.** Elevation means 'this floats'. Use a tonal step or space for emphasis.
7. **For modals, the scrim is the primary depth cue.** The scrim is what tells the user the page behind is inert; the shadow is secondary.
8. **Stack with the named layer scale.** Overlays portal to the end of body and order themselves by open order; the layer only has to clear in-flow chrome.

## Never

- **Never:** z-[9999] or any raw z-index. **Instead:** z-(--z-overlay) and the other named layers. Raw z-indexes become a bidding war that a future overlay always loses. *Enforced by sable-lint: raw-z-index.*
- **Never:** shadow-[0_8px_30px_rgba(0,0,0,.2)] or any custom shadow. **Instead:** shadow-sm … shadow-xl by role. Custom shadows ignore the theme's light/dark elevation recipes.
- **Never:** bg-card on a popover, or bg-popover on a resting card. **Instead:** Match the token to the role. Swapping them is how floating surfaces melt into the surface beneath.

## Details

### A menu inside a dialog

```tsx
// before
Dialog bg-card · Menu bg-card — identical in dark mode
// after
Dialog bg-card · Menu bg-popover — one step lighter, plus edge light
```

The menu reads as above the dialog without any prop.

**Related:** `sable docs shape` · `sable docs token-intent`

# Motion

Motion explains a change: where something came from, what responded, and that work is happening. It is subtle by default, built from named recipes, and one switch turns it off.

**4 slots · 3 speeds · enter-only overshoot · 1 kill switch**

## Three speeds

Match duration to the distance and size of what moves. Each value is multiplied by --motion-scale. Two edge steps sit outside the three: --motion-duration-instant (75ms) for a checkbox tick or tab swap, and --motion-duration-slower (500ms) for progress and value changes.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `fast  --motion-duration-fast` | 150ms | Hover, press, focus, tooltips, small toggles. Also every exit. |
| `base  --motion-duration-base` | 200ms | Menus, popovers, tabs, disclosure. The default enter. |
| `slow  --motion-duration-slow` | 300ms | Dialogs, sheets, page-level transitions. |

## Recipes

Reach for one named class before writing a transition.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `motion-interactive` | fast · standard | Hover/focus/press chrome on anything clickable. Replaces transition-colors. |
| `motion-press` | fast · scale settle | Tactile press. Always paired with motion-interactive. |
| `motion-fade` | enter base / exit fast | Scrims and backdrops. |
| `motion-pop` | enter base · spring | Anchored or centred surfaces: popovers, menus, dialogs. |
| `motion-slide-{up,down,left,right}` | enter base / exit fast | Directional surfaces: sheets, toasts. |
| `motion-disclosure` | base · standard | Height changes: accordion, collapsible. |
| `motion-icon-swap` | enter · emphasized cross-fade | Two icons of one control trading places: play/pause, outline/fill. |
| `motion-draw` | slower · decelerate | SVG line art drawing on when a <Reveal> scrolls in. The path needs pathLength="1"; stagger siblings with --motion-draw-delay. |
| `motion-spin · pulse · shimmer · dot-bounce · ping` | loops | Activity. Scale-aware, so reduced motion freezes them. |

## Easings

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `ease-standard` | cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) | The default for state changes. |
| `ease-decelerate` | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) | Entrances: arrive fast, settle slowly. |
| `ease-emphasized` | cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) | Large surfaces covering a lot of distance. |
| `ease-spring` | ~4% overshoot | A gentle pop on enter. Never on exit. |
| `ease-bounce` | ~10% overshoot | A playful pop, opt-in only. Enter only, never on exit. |

## The four slots

Every interactive component answers all four, by filling the slot or declining it with a reason in meta.motion.

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `arrival` | fade · slide · pop · Reveal | How does it enter? |
| `response` | motion-interactive · motion-press | What happens under the pointer? |
| `transition` | motion-disclosure · eased transform | How does it move between its own states? |
| `activity` | spin · pulse · shimmer | How do you tell working from frozen? |

## Rules

1. **Every motion has a reason: orientation, feedback, continuity or activity.** Motion with no reason is latency. If you cannot say which of the four it serves, remove it.
2. **Reach for a recipe first; drop to tokens only when none fits.** Recipes are reviewed once and respect the kill switch. A bespoke transition string is reviewed never. *Enforced by sable-lint: transition-colors, transition-all.*
3. **Exits are one step faster than entrances, and never overshoot.** Something leaving should get out of the way. A bounce on exit draws the eye to what the user just dismissed.
4. **Animate opacity and transform only.** They run on the compositor. Width, height, top and left cause layout on every frame. motion-disclosure is the one sanctioned exception.
5. **Durations come from tokens, so --motion-scale can stop them.** prefers-reduced-motion and <MotionProvider> off both set --motion-scale to 0. A raw duration ignores that. *Enforced by sable-lint: raw-duration, builtin-animate.*
6. **Interactive elements always respond. Something styled for hover with no motion recipe snaps.** A snap between states reads as broken. The four prohibitive rules could not catch missing motion, so this one does. *Enforced by sable-lint: static-interactive.*
7. **JS motion reads useMotion().enabled and does nothing when it is false.** Reduced motion is an accessibility setting, not a style preference.

## Never

- **Never:** Tailwind's animate-spin / animate-pulse / animate-ping / animate-bounce. **Instead:** motion-spin, motion-pulse, motion-ping, motion-dot-bounce. The built-ins ignore --motion-scale, so reduced motion cannot freeze them. *Enforced by sable-lint: builtin-animate.*
- **Never:** duration-150, duration-300, or any raw duration utility. **Instead:** duration-(--motion-duration-fast) and siblings. Raw durations bypass the kill switch. *Enforced by sable-lint: raw-duration.*
- **Never:** transition-all, or transition-colors on its own. **Instead:** motion-interactive, or name the properties you animate. transition-all animates unrelated layout changes and defeats the browser's pre-computation. *Enforced by sable-lint: transition-all, transition-colors.*
- **Never:** Motion on first paint of static content, or staggered entrances on every list. **Instead:** Reveal for one deliberate moment per view. Entrance choreography repeated everywhere becomes a loading delay.
- **Never:** The motion library in the core package. **Instead:** src/motion (WAAPI, IntersectionObserver, View Transitions). Sable's motion layer is zero-dependency; drag, FLIP and velocity springs belong in an optional adapter.

## Details

### Hover that respects the kill switch

```tsx
// before
<button className="transition-colors duration-150 sable-surface-interactive">
// after
<button className="motion-interactive sable-surface-interactive">
```

Same feel, but reduced motion now resolves it instantly.

### Faster exits

```tsx
// before
transition: opacity 200ms ease-in-out;  /* in and out */
// after
data-[starting-style]: enter 200ms decelerate · data-[ending-style]: exit 150ms standard
```

motion-pop and motion-slide-* already do this; dismissing feels responsive instead of sluggish.

**Related:** `sable docs accessibility` · `sable docs reviewing-motion` · `sable token motion`

# Scrolling

Every scroll container declares a policy. Vertical regions get a quiet bar that appears only while you are in them; horizontal strips get edge fades instead of a rail.

**2 policies · vertical gets a bar · horizontal gets a fade**

## Policies

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `scrollbar-quiet` | 4px thumb · hidden at rest → 12% active → 16% hovered → 20% dragging | The default for vertical scrolling. Grows to 6px under the pointer. |
| `scrollbar-hidden` | no bar | Only when something else carries the affordance — and you can name it (an edge fade, paging controls). |
| `<Scroller>` | edge fades + wheel mapping | Horizontal strips: media rows, chip rows, tab overflow. |
| `useScrollActivity` | data-scrolling for ~600ms | Lets the bar respond to touch drags and programmatic scrolls, which hover cannot see. |

## Rules

1. **Every overflow-*-auto|scroll declares scrollbar-quiet or scrollbar-hidden.** Left bare, the platform draws its own: on Windows, stepper arrows hard against the padding edge that poke out of rounded corners. *Enforced by sable-lint: unmanaged-overflow (also checked over every registry example).*
2. **Vertical regions get a bar; horizontal regions get an edge fade.** A vertical list needs position feedback. A horizontal strip needs 'there is more this way', which a fade says better than a 4px rail.
3. **A horizontal region must work without a horizontal input.** Most mice have no horizontal wheel. Scroller maps the vertical wheel sideways and handles arrow keys, Home and End.
4. **Reveal on scrolling, not only on hover.** Touch drags and programmatic scrolls (a chat following a reply) hover nothing, and those are the moments a reader needs to see where they are.

## Never

- **Never:** scrollbar-hidden on a vertical list with no fade or paging. **Instead:** scrollbar-quiet. It leaves the reader with no sense of position and nothing to discover.
- **Never:** A styled ::-webkit-scrollbar written per component. **Instead:** The scrollbar-quiet utility. Chromium ignores ::-webkit-scrollbar once scrollbar-width is set; the utility handles both engines.

## Details

### A scrolling panel

```tsx
// before
<div className="overflow-y-auto">
// after
<div className="overflow-y-auto scrollbar-quiet" ref={useScrollActivity()}>
```

No bar at rest; it appears while scrolling, hovered or focused, and fades a beat after. Content cut off at the edge is what says the region scrolls.

**Related:** `sable docs surfaces` · `sable docs accessibility` · `sable component Scroller`

# Accessibility

Sable's components ship accessible behavior from Base UI. These rules cover what an app composing them still has to get right.

**WCAG AA · 44px targets · visible focus · reduced motion · logical properties**

## Floors

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `Contrast` | 4.5:1 text · 3:1 UI and large text | Every semantic text/surface pair is checked per theme by contrast.test.ts. |
| `Hit area` | 44×44px | hit-target keeps a small control at the floor without moving layout. |
| `Focus` | ring-2 ring-ring, full opacity | Visible on every interactive element, in light, dark and forced-colors. |
| `Mobile input text` | ≥ 16px | iOS Safari zooms the page on focus below it. |
| `Reduced motion` | --motion-scale: 0 | Transitions resolve instantly; loaders hold their first frame. |

## Rules

1. **Use the component, not a div with a click handler.** Base UI supplies roles, keyboard handling and focus management. A clickable div has none of them.
2. **Every control has an accessible name.** Icon-only buttons take aria-label. Fields take a <Label> through <Field>, which also wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
3. **A live region exists before it has anything to say.** Render role="status" empty from the start and swap its text. A region inserted together with its content is announced inconsistently.
4. **On client-side navigation, update document.title and move focus to the new view's h1.** Route changes are silent to assistive technology unless the app announces them. AppShell supplies the skip link and landmarks; the app does the rest.
5. **Keep submit enabled; validate on submit and focus the first invalid field.** A disabled submit hides why it is disabled. Focus is the only way a screen-reader user finds the error.
6. **Use logical properties: ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/text-start/inset-inline-*.** Flex and grid mirror for free under dir="rtl"; hand-positioned elements do not. *Enforced by design-lint: physical-direction (ratchet).*
7. **Decorative layers over content take pointer-events-none and aria-hidden.** Scrims, glows and fades otherwise swallow clicks on the controls beneath.
8. **Check focus and disabled states under forced-colors: active.** Windows High Contrast overrides ring colors and erases opacity-based disabled styling.

## Never

- **Never:** Color as the only signal (a red border with no message). **Instead:** Color plus text or an icon. Roughly 1 in 12 men cannot tell red from green.
- **Never:** Opacity on the focus ring. **Instead:** ring-ring at full opacity; tune the token in the theme. A faded ring loses the contrast the theme tested. *Enforced by sable-lint: faded-focus-ring.*
- **Never:** A brand or status fill retuned under its old label — dark ink on a bright red that passes 4.5:1 at APCA Lc 42. **Instead:** A label that clears 4.5:1 and APCA Lc 60 in both modes. Move the fill's lightness, not its hue, keeping the ink its colour takes. A status colour on a surface is its own token (`--destructive-text`), so the fill can move freely. The ratio alone passes labels that read muddy. A deliberate brand pair is allowed with a recorded reason (lint disable or preset exceptions). *Enforced by sable-lint: label-contrast.*
- **Never:** Blocking paste, or type="number" for codes and card numbers. **Instead:** type="text" inputMode="numeric" with the right autocomplete. Blocking paste breaks password managers; number inputs scroll-change identifiers.
- **Never:** forced-color-adjust: none to 'fix' high-contrast mode. **Instead:** Let the system colors apply; verify the result. It removes the user's chosen colors exactly where they need them.
- **Never:** outline: none without a replacement. **Instead:** focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring. Keyboard users lose their place.

## Details

### An icon-only button

```tsx
// before
<Button size="icon"><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>
// after
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close"><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>
```

Without a name, a screen reader announces only 'button'.

### A status that announces

```tsx
// before
{saved && <p role="status">Saved</p>}
// after
<p role="status">{saved ? "Saved" : ""}</p>
```

The region is in the accessibility tree before its text changes, so the change is announced.

**Related:** `sable docs typography` · `sable docs motion` · `sable component <Name> --a11y`

# AuthPage

Split sign-in page: a form column (brand mark, heading, email + password, primary sign-in, passkey and wallet alternatives, sign-up switch, terms) beside a brand panel painted from the theme's tones with a featured release card. Below lg the panel drops away and the form is the whole screen.

**Intent:** Reach for this for sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, and any single-purpose one-column form route (invite accept, unsubscribe). Not for multi-section forms (use SettingsPage).

## Notes

- The form column is a `form`-capped Region (480px), so the controls keep the same measure whether the panel is present or not.
- No card around the form: the page itself is the surface, and the brand panel carries the identity. A card on a blank page reads as a template.
- The heading is `text-heading-1` in an h1 — it is the page outline, so it takes a heading tier, not a card title.
- Brand mark, form and terms are a three-part column: mark pinned to the top, form vertically centred in the remaining space, terms pinned to the bottom.
- Forgot password sits under the password field, right-aligned, before the submit button — so it comes right after the field in tab order. Field has no label-row action slot yet.
- One primary action. Passkey and wallet are outline buttons under an `or` Separator; switching to sign-up is a quiet `link-underline` link.
- Validation uses Field `validate` for product copy instead of the browser's generic required message. A rejected sign-in comes back through Form `errors` on the password field; the submit Button shows `loading` while the request is in flight.
- The brand panel artwork is a mesh of the theme's decorative tones over `--primary`, so it re-paints for every theme and mode. The relative-colour `oklch(from var(--tone-*) …)` lift needs an `inline-color` disable with a reason.
- The panel is `hidden lg:flex`: on a phone the form is the whole screen, with no decorative scroll above it.

## Accessibility

- The route renders inside <main> with one h1; the brand panel is an <aside> labelled "Featured release".
- Field auto-wires labels, describedby, and invalid state onto the inputs; on submit, the first invalid field is focused.
- Autocomplete attributes (`email webauthn`, `current-password`) keep password managers and passkey autofill working.
- The Forgot password and Create one links use `hit-target` to meet the 44px touch floor without changing layout.
- The artwork swatches are aria-hidden decoration; the brand link's accessible name is the wordmark.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, Entity, Field, Form, GradientArt, Icon, Input, Region, Separator, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

export function AuthPage() {
	const [pending, setPending] = useState(false)
	const [errors, setErrors] = useState<Record<string, string>>({})

	return (
		<main className="grid min-h-dvh bg-background lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.1fr)]">
			<Region max="form" safeArea={["top", "bottom"]} className="flex flex-col">
				{/* safeArea owns the region's own padding, so the breathing room sits one level in. */}
				<Stack gap={0} className="flex-1 py-8 sm:py-10">
					<a href="/" className="flex items-center gap-2.5 self-start rounded-sm motion-interactive motion-press">
						{/* The same mark the app shell's sidebar and header carry. */}
						<Icon name="gem" variant="solid" className="text-2xl" />
						<span className="text-title-lg">Atelier</span>
					</a>

					<Stack gap={4} justify="center" className="flex-1 py-12">
						<Stack gap={1.5}>
							<h1 className="text-heading-1">Welcome back</h1>
							<p className="text-body-lg text-muted-foreground">
								Sign in to collect new releases and manage your editions.
							</p>
						</Stack>

						<Form
							className="gap-5"
							errors={errors}
							onFormSubmit={() => {
								setPending(true)
								// Replace with your auth call; a rejected sign-in comes back as a field error.
								setTimeout(() => {
									setPending(false)
									setErrors({ password: "That email and password don’t match. Try again or reset your password." })
								}, 900)
							}}
						>
							<Field label="Email" name="email" validate={(value) => (value ? null : "Enter your email address.")}>
								<Input type="email" autoComplete="email webauthn" placeholder="you@example.com" />
							</Field>
							<Stack gap={1.5}>
								<Field label="Password" name="password" validate={(value) => (value ? null : "Enter your password.")}>
									<Input type="password" autoComplete="current-password" />
								</Field>
								<a href="/forgot-password" className="hit-target self-end text-body-sm text-muted-foreground link-underline motion-interactive">
									Forgot password?
								</a>
							</Stack>
							<Button type="submit" size="cta" loading={pending} loadingLabel="Signing in" className="w-full">
								Sign in
							</Button>
						</Form>

						<Separator label="or" />

						<Stack gap={1.5}>
							<Button variant="outline" size="cta" className="w-full" iconStart={<Icon name="key" />}>
								Sign in with a passkey
							</Button>
							<Button variant="outline" size="cta" className="w-full" iconStart={<Icon name="wallet" />}>
								Connect a wallet
							</Button>
						</Stack>

						<p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">
							No account?{" "}
							<a href="/signup" className="hit-target link-underline motion-interactive text-foreground">
								Create one
							</a>
						</p>
					</Stack>

					<p className="text-body-xs text-muted-foreground">
						By signing in you agree to the{" "}
						<a href="/terms" className="link-underline motion-interactive">
							Terms
						</a>{" "}
						and{" "}
						<a href="/privacy" className="link-underline motion-interactive">
							Privacy Policy
						</a>
						.
					</p>
				</Stack>
			</Region>

			{/* The brand panel is decoration: on a phone the form is the whole screen. */}
			<aside aria-label="Featured release" className="hidden p-3 lg:flex">
				{/* Art painted from the theme's tones over its brand, so it follows every look. */}
				<GradientArt seed="Untitled (gold rush)" className="flex flex-1 flex-col justify-end rounded-xl p-8">
					<Card className="max-w-md">
						<CardContent>
							<Stack gap={3}>
								<Badge tone="edition" className="self-start">
									Edition of 50
								</Badge>
								<p className="text-title-lg">
									“Every edition is a conversation with whoever holds it next.”
								</p>
								<Entity
									className="p-0"
									leading={<Avatar variant="art" fallback="MO" />}
									title="Mara Okafor"
									subtitle="Untitled (gold rush), 2026"
								/>
							</Stack>
						</CardContent>
					</Card>
				</GradientArt>
			</aside>
		</main>
	)
}
```

# BrandLandingPage

High-fidelity brand/product landing page: pill navigation, editorial hero type, a dark product scene, a value section, a how-it-works sequence, a customer story with outcomes, a closing CTA band, and a complete branded footer.

**Intent:** Use this for a polished product marketing route that still needs to show a credible app surface. It is warmer and more tactile than the canonical LandingPage, but avoids trend-driven neon and generic hype cues.

## Notes

- The story runs promise → product → value → process → proof → ask: hero, product scene, 'Why Cove' value cards, a three-step how-it-works list, a customer story with outcome figures, then one closing CTA. Each section adds new evidence; no number is repeated from the product scene.
- One display headline owns the first viewport; supporting copy stays in body-lg at prose measure. Section headings are heading-1 under a `text-overline` eyebrow.
- The nav spends one compact pill surface, with a clear brand signal and two primary paths: sign in and request access.
- The product scene and the closing CTA band are dark islands: a `dark` class on the wrapper re-scopes every semantic token, so surfaces, muted ink, Badge tones and Buttons take the theme's own dark values in either page mode. Never fake a dark panel with overlay ink at reduced opacity — status tones tuned for a light page vanish on it.
- The scene is a picture of the product: `aria-hidden` + `inert` keep its sample button and figures out of the tab order and the outline. On narrow screens it drops the side column and keeps the signal map, so it scales instead of stacking into a second page.
- The chart keeps past weeks on the quiet `secondary` fill and gives the current week the one accent, so the signal reads at a glance.
- Value cards are real Cards with a neutral `sable-well` icon tile; the customer story is a Card rendered as a figure, with outcome figures split by Separator. The scene's nested panels take `rounded-concentric-xl/<inset>` from the shell's radius, so the corners stay parallel at any radius preset.
- The footer closes the page with brand reassurance, a plain status Badge, a three-column sitemap (three columns at every width), a digest signup, and legal links.
- All figures, names and the testimonial are sample content; replace them with real, verifiable claims.

## Accessibility

- The brand nav is a labeled nav landmark with real links and visible text.
- Each content section is a labelled region (by its h2, or aria-label for the customer story); the decorative product scene is hidden from assistive tech and inert.
- The how-it-works steps are an ordered list; the testimonial is a figure with a blockquote and a figcaption naming the speaker.
- The footer is a real footer landmark with a labeled footer nav, visible link text, and a labeled email field.
- TextReveal preserves the full headline as one accessible label and honors reduced-motion policy; Reveal shows the value cards immediately when motion is off.
- Status dots and the status Badge are paired with visible text labels so color is never the only signal.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid, Icon, Input, Region, Reveal, Row, Separator, Stack, StatusDot, TextReveal } from "@sableui/react"

const navItems = [
	{ label: "Platform", href: "#platform" },
	{ label: "How it works", href: "#how-it-works" },
	{ label: "Customers", href: "#customers" },
	{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" },
]

const spaces = [
	{ name: "Waypoint", value: "98.4%", label: "clear routes" },
	{ name: "Fielddesk", value: "12", label: "open holds" },
	{ name: "Archive", value: "4.8k", label: "sealed records" },
]

const routes = [
	{ label: "Intake", state: "Open", tone: "info" as const },
	{ label: "Review", state: "Live", tone: "edition" as const },
	{ label: "Archive", state: "Safe", tone: "success" as const },
]

// Weekly approvals: past weeks recede, the current week carries the signal.
const bars = [
	{ week: "w1", height: "38%", current: false },
	{ week: "w2", height: "56%", current: false },
	{ week: "w3", height: "44%", current: false },
	{ week: "w4", height: "68%", current: false },
	{ week: "w5", height: "52%", current: false },
	{ week: "w6", height: "78%", current: false },
	{ week: "w7", height: "60%", current: false },
	{ week: "w8", height: "72%", current: false },
	{ week: "w9", height: "88%", current: true },
```

---

# ChatPanel

A full-height conversation surface: titled header, scrolling transcript, and a composer pinned to the bottom — the assembled shape of an AI assistant, a support thread, or a DM.

**Intent:** Reach for this for any conversation that owns its screen — an assistant, a support inbox thread, a DM. Not for a chat docked beside other work (compose the same three parts inside a Sheet or a PanelGroup instead), and not for a comment thread under an article, which is a FeedPage concern.

## Notes

- The panel is a fixed-height column, not a growing page. `h-[calc(100dvh_-_--spacing(12))]` on the Card (the viewport minus the Page's py-6, in spacing units so density moves both together — a fixed `3rem` drifts the moment density moves the padding) and `flex-1 min-h-0` on the MessageScroller are what make the transcript scroll instead of the document — the single most common thing to get wrong here, and it fails by pushing the composer off the bottom of the screen.
- The panel is a Card, not a hand-built bordered section: CardHeader (title, description, CardAction), the MessageScroller and a CardFooter all inset by the card's own `--card-p`, so the three regions share one edge at any card density.
- `dvh` rather than `vh`: on mobile the URL bar collapses, and a `vh`-sized panel puts the composer under it exactly when someone is trying to type.
- Region cap is `feed` (640px) — a conversation is a reading column, and the Bubble measure cap is tuned to the same assumption.
- The composer sits outside the scroll region, in a bordered CardFooter, so it stays put while the transcript moves.
- Grouping is derived from the data (`turns[i - 1].mine === turn.mine`) rather than hand-set, and the tail is dropped on continuations — that pairing is what makes a run read as one block.
- What the assistant did before answering — a doc it read, a tool it ran — is a `Marker variant="note"` in that message's `header`, so it reads as part of the turn rather than as an event between turns.
- The assistant's long-form answer uses `variant="plain"` and continues the same grouped run. A tinted box around a code block reads as a quote rather than as a turn. A plain Bubble sizes to its content with no measure cap, so it takes `max-w-full` here: bounded by the column, a wide code line scrolls inside the CodeBlock instead of pushing the transcript sideways on a phone.
- A settled answer carries its actions (copy, regenerate) in the Message `footer` as a `Toolbar` of icon `ToolbarButton`s with tooltips — one tab stop, arrow keys between them. The answer still streaming has none: there is nothing to copy or regenerate until it settles, and Stop lives in the composer.
- One turn, one Message: the reader's question and the file it refers to stack inside a single end-aligned Message rather than being sent as two.
- Assistant turns share one Avatar with a glyph fallback and `alt="Assistant"` — initials like "AI" read as a person, and a fallback-only avatar is otherwise unnamed.
- The answer in flight is a `StreamingText` in a `plain` Bubble, and ONE `pending` flag drives both it and the composer's `busy`. They are the same wait reported at the two ends of the panel; letting them drift gives you a composer still saying 'sending' under an answer that already finished.
- A spinner `Marker` (or `ThinkingOrb`) belongs BEFORE the first token and is replaced once tokens land, not kept alongside. Two indicators for one wait read as two things happening — which is also why `StreamingText` takes `caret={false}` when something adjacent already reports it.
- MessageScroller needs no configuring for this: it re-follows on "a message grew" (ResizeObserver) as well as "a message arrived", so the newest token stays pinned while a reader who has scrolled up is left alone.
- For a new thread, swap the transcript's children for an `<EmptyState>` inside the same MessageScroller — the panel, header and composer are unchanged, which is the point of keeping them separate.

## Accessibility

- The panel header's title is the page's <h1> (an h1 inside CardTitle, which carries the type); the transcript is a scroll region with native overflow, so keyboard scrolling works unchanged.
- The answer in flight carries `aria-busy` rather than sitting in a live region. That is deliberate: a live region around streamed text announces every token, which is unusable. Announce once when the turn settles, from whatever owns the turn — the incomplete state is still exposed, just not narrated.
- The composer is a real <form> whose Enter handling skips IME composition, and every icon-only control in the panel carries an accessible label — the answer actions also carry a tooltip, and the stop control is named for what it stops (`stopLabel="Stop answering"`).

## Source

```tsx
import { Attachment, Avatar, Bubble, Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, ChatComposer, CodeBlock, Icon, Marker, MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, Message, MessageScroller, Page, SettingsMenu, SettingsRow, SimpleTooltip, StreamingText, Toolbar, ToolbarButton } from "@sableui/react"

/**
 * The request is in flight. In an app this is your send state — from `useChat`,
 * a fetch, whatever owns the turn — and it is deliberately ONE flag driving two
 * places: the composer's `busy` and the answer's `streaming`. They are the same
 * wait reported at both ends of the panel, and letting them drift is how you get
 * a composer that still says "sending" under an answer that already finished.
 */
const pending = true

/** The answer so far. Append tokens to this; `StreamingText` assumes it only grows. */
const streamed =
	"Yes, appends are already safe: your layout effect measures before paint. The jump is on the prepend path, which reads scrollHeight after the new rows"

/**
 * The opening exchange. `step` is what the assistant did before answering — a
 * doc it read, a tool it ran — and it rides in that message's header, so it
 * reads as part of the turn rather than as an event between turns.
 */
const turns: { id: string; mine: boolean; step?: string; body: string }[] = [
	{
		id: "t_01",
		mine: true,
		body: "Our chat scroll jumps every time older messages load. What are we doing wrong?",
	},
	{
		id: "t_02",
		mine: false,
		step: "Read message-scroller.md",
		body: "Almost always the anchor. If you preserve the scroll position by measuring the container, prepending history moves everything under the reader.",
	},
	{
		id: "t_03",
		mine: false,
		body: "Anchor on the oldest rendered message instead and add back however far it moved. Appends leave it alone, so the same rule covers both.",
	},
]

export function ChatPanel() {
	// One identity for every assistant turn. A glyph rather than initials: "AI"
	// in a circle reads as a person called A. I. The glyph is sized to the
	// circle (the fallback's own size is tuned for two letters, and a lone icon
	// at that size reads as a speck); `alt` names it for a screen reader, which
	// otherwise gets nothing from a fallback-only avatar.
	const assistant = (
		<Avatar variant="art"
			size="sm"
			alt="Assistant"
			fallback={<Icon name="sparkles" className="text-base" />}
		/>
	)

	return (
		<Page as="main" max="feed" gap={0} className="py-6">
			{/* h-dvh minus the page's own padding (py-6 = 12 spacing units, in
			    spacing units so density moves both together): the panel owns the
			    viewport, and the transcript — not the page — is the thing that
			    scrolls. The panel is a Card; its parts inset by the card's own
			    --card-p, so header, transcript and composer share one edge. */}
			<Card
				render={<section aria-labelledby="chat-title" />}
				className="flex h-[calc(100dvh_-_--spacing(12))] flex-col overflow-hidden"
			>
				<CardHeader className="border-b border-border pb-(--card-p)">
					{/* CardTitle carries the type; the h1 inside it is the page heading. */}
					<CardTitle>
						<h1 id="chat-title">Scroll behaviour</h1>
					</CardTitle>
					<CardDescription>Assistant · answers from your team's docs</CardDescription>
					<CardAction>
						{/* Labelled, not a bare plus: the composer already has a plus
						    (attach), and two identical glyphs a panel apart that do
						    different things is a guessing game. */}
						<Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
							<Icon name="edit" />
							New chat
						</Button>
					</CardAction>
				</CardHeader>

				{/* flex-1 min-h-0 is the whole layout: it bounds the scroll region
				    against the panel instead of letting the transcript grow the page. */}
				<MessageScroller className="min-h-0 flex-1 p-(--card-p)">
					<Marker variant="separator">Today</Marker>

					{turns.map((turn, i) => {
						// Derived, not hand-set: a turn continues a run when the one
						// before it has the same author. A continuation drops its
						// avatar (Message keeps the column) AND its tail (Bubble keeps
						// the ear's space) — together, that makes the run one block.
						const continues = i > 0 && turns[i - 1].mine === turn.mine
						return (
							<Message
								key={turn.id}
								messageId={turn.id}
								align={turn.mine ? "end" : "start"}
								grouped={continues}
								avatar={turn.mine ? undefined : assistant}
								header={
									turn.step ? (
										<Marker variant="note" icon="book" className="justify-start">
											{turn.step}
										</Marker>
									) : undefined
								}
							>
								<Bubble
									variant={turn.mine ? "primary" : "muted"}
									align={turn.mine ? "end" : "start"}
									tail={!continues}
								>
									{turn.body}
								</Bubble>
							</Message>
						)
					})}

					{/* The same run, continued: long-form output with no bubble,
					    because a tinted box around a code block reads as a quote
					    rather than as a turn. Its footer carries what the reader does
					    WITH a settled answer, as a Toolbar: one tab stop, arrow keys
					    between the actions. */}
					<Message
						messageId="t_04"
						grouped
						avatar={assistant}
						footer={
							<Toolbar aria-label="Answer actions">
								<SimpleTooltip content="Copy answer">
									<ToolbarButton size="icon-sm" aria-label="Copy answer">
										<Icon name="copy" />
									</ToolbarButton>
								</SimpleTooltip>
								<SimpleTooltip content="Regenerate">
									<ToolbarButton size="icon-sm" aria-label="Regenerate answer">
										<Icon name="refresh" />
									</ToolbarButton>
								</SimpleTooltip>
							</Toolbar>
						}
					>
						{/* max-w-full: a plain Bubble sizes to its content with no
						    measure cap, and a code line is wider than a phone. Bounded
						    by the column, the CodeBlock scrolls inside itself instead of
						    pushing the whole transcript sideways. */}
						<Bubble variant="plain" className="max-w-full">
							<p className="text-body-md text-foreground">
								Here is the shape of it:
							</p>
							<CodeBlock
								code={
									"const shift = anchor.offsetTop - lastTop\nif (shift !== 0) viewport.scrollTop += shift"
								}
								filename="preserve.ts"
							/>
						</Bubble>
					</Message>

					{/* The reader's follow-up is one turn: the question and the file
					    it refers to stack in a single Message, so they share a side, an
					    edge and a timestamp rather than reading as two sends. */}
					<Message messageId="t_05" align="end">
						<Bubble variant="primary" align="end">
							Here's ours. Does the same fix cover new messages arriving?
						</Bubble>
						<Attachment
							name="scroller.tsx"
							meta="4.2 KB · TSX"
							onOpen={() => undefined}
						/>
					</Message>

					{/* The answer arriving. A `Marker` with a spinner — or ThinkingOrb —
					    is what sits here BEFORE the first token; once tokens land it is
					    replaced rather than kept, because two indicators for one wait
					    read as two things happening. What stays is the step it took,
					    as a finished note in the header.

					    No bubble, same as the long-form answer above: a tinted box
					    around a growing paragraph makes the reflow look like the box
					    breathing. And no answer actions yet — there is nothing to copy
					    or regenerate until it settles; Stop lives in the composer.

					    MessageScroller needs no help with this — it already re-follows on
					    "a message grew" (ResizeObserver), not just on "a message arrived",
					    so the newest token stays pinned while the reader can still scroll
					    up without being yanked back. */}
					<Message
						messageId="t_06"
						avatar={assistant}
						header={
							<Marker variant="note" icon="file" className="justify-start">
								Read scroller.tsx
							</Marker>
						}
					>
						<Bubble variant="plain">
							<StreamingText text={streamed} streaming={pending} />
						</Bubble>
					</Message>
				</MessageScroller>

				<CardFooter className="border-t border-border pt-(--card-p)">
					<ChatComposer
						className="flex-1"
						placeholder="Ask a follow-up…"
						// Same flag as the answer's `streaming`, which is what turns Send
						// into Stop. A composer that stays sendable mid-answer invites a
						// second request on top of the one still running.
						busy={pending}
						onStop={() => undefined}
						stopLabel="Stop answering"
						onAttach={() => undefined}
						footer="Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line"
						// Model and effort sit in `actions`, at the send end of the row:
						// they qualify the message about to be sent, so they belong beside
						// the button that sends it rather than next to the attach control.
						actions={
							<SettingsMenu
								variant="subtle"
								size="xs"
								label="Change model and effort"
								summary={
									<>
										<span className="text-foreground">5.6 Sol</span>{" "}
										<span className="text-muted-foreground">High</span>
									</>
								}
							>
								<SettingsRow label="Model" value="5.6 Sol">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="sol">
										<MenuRadioItem value="sol">5.6 Sol</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="lite">5.6 Lite</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
								<SettingsRow label="Effort" value="High">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="high">
										<MenuRadioItem value="low">Low</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="standard">Standard</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="high">High</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
								<SettingsRow label="Speed" value="Standard">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
										<MenuRadioItem value="standard">Standard</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="priority">Priority</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
							</SettingsMenu>
						}
					/>
				</CardFooter>
			</Card>
		</Page>
	)
}
```

---

# DashboardPage

App-shell creator dashboard: a branded Sidebar with an account footer (AppHeader + BottomNav below lg), a KPI row, an edge-to-edge editions table with sell-through Meters, and supporting payout, collector, release and activity cards — the default shape for an operator or analytics home route.

**Intent:** Reach for this when a route's job is monitoring or managing many records (sales, orders, editions, posts) with a few headline numbers. Not for reading-focused routes (use FeedPage) or single-record routes (use ListDetailPage's detail side).

## Notes

- Region cap is `wide` (1280px): dashboards hold tables and multi-column grids, never a reading column.
- Hierarchy runs headline → records → context: KPI row, then the primary table beside its two closest companions (payout, top collectors), then the lower-priority lists (upcoming, activity). Every row of the grid is filled so the route ends on content, not empty canvas.
- Stat cards: CardHeader carries the label (CardDescription) and the value; KPI values are `text-mono-xl` — the metric mono tier, tabular figures — never a heading tier. The trend Badge sits with its comparison note in CardContent, so the value keeps the full card width when the row folds to 2×2 on a phone.
- Stat cards use an explicit cols map (2 → 4) — a 4-stat row must fold to 2×2, never strand an orphan the way auto-fit can.
- The table runs flush to the card edges with `<CardContent flush>`, which hands the card's padding to the table (`--table-edge-px`), so the first and last columns line up with the CardHeader at any card density — never hand-set pl-6/pr-6. Numeric columns align end in mono; Table scrolls horizontally inside the card on narrow screens.
- Sold / supply is a `Meter` (how full a known range is), not `Progress` (task progress). Status is `Badge appearance="plain" dot`, with the app's own states mapped to tones once at the top of the file.
- Lists are Entity rows in CardList, inset to the card padding and divided by hairlines — never CardContent with hand-tuned px. A card that shares a grid row with a taller one becomes `flex flex-col` and pins its CardFooter with `mt-auto`.
- Brand and account live in the Sidebar: SidebarHeader holds the mark + wordmark, SidebarFooter holds the signed-in Entity with an OverflowMenu. Sidebar rebinds the page ink tokens to its own, so the Entity and OverflowMenu read correctly even when a theme paints the rail dark on a light page.
- The page has exactly one heading-1 (PageHeader); card titles are Title tier, not headings.
- Chrome (Sidebar) is outside the content grid; the Page region caps only content.
- Sidebar hides below lg, so the shell's header carries an AppHeader (brand + account) and its footer a BottomNav with the same destinations — never strand mobile users without navigation.

## Accessibility

- AppShell provides the skip link and <main id="main-content"> landmark.
- The active SidebarItem and BottomNavItem carry aria-current via `active`.
- DataTable headers are real <th>; sortable columns are announced.
- Each sell-through Meter has an aria-label naming the edition and aria-valuetext reading "184 of 250 sold".
- Avatars beside a visible name use an empty alt so the name is not read twice.

```tsx
											<span className="text-body-sm whitespace-nowrap text-muted-foreground">{shortDate(row.released)}</span>
										),
									},
								]}
							/>
						</CardContent>
						<CardFooter className="justify-between">
							<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">
								Showing {editions.length} of {editionCount} editions

								View all editions

							</Button>
						</CardFooter>
					</Card>

								<CardAction>

										{shortDate(payout.date)}

								</CardAction>
							</CardHeader>
							<CardContent>
								<dl className="sable-list-dl text-body-sm">
									{payout.lines.map((line) => (
										<div key={line.label} className="contents">
											<dt>{line.label}</dt>
											<dd className={typeof line.value === "number" ? "text-end text-mono-sm" : "text-end"}>
												{typeof line.value === "number" ? usdCents.format(line.value) : line.value}
											</dd>
										</div>
									))}
								</dl>
							</CardContent>
						</Card>
						<Card>
							<CardHeader>
								<CardTitle>Top collectors</CardTitle>
								<CardDescription>By spend this month.</CardDescription>
								<CardAction>
									<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/collectors" />}>
										View all
									</Button>
								</CardAction>
							</CardHeader>
							<CardList>
								{collectors.map((person) => (
									<Entity
										key={person.id}
										leading={<Avatar variant="art" size="sm" fallback={person.initials} alt="" />}
										title={person.name}
										subtitle={`${person.handle} · ${person.pieces} pieces`}
										action={<span className="text-mono-sm">{usd.format(person.spent)}</span>}
									/>
								))}
							</CardList>
						</Card>
					</Stack>
				</Grid>

						<CardHeader>
							<CardTitle>Upcoming releases</CardTitle>
							<CardDescription>Scheduled to open to collectors.</CardDescription>
						</CardHeader>
						<CardList>
							{upcoming.map((release) => (
								<Entity
									key={release.id}
									title={release.title}
									subtitle={release.detail}
									action={<RelativeTime date={Date.now() + release.at} className="text-caption text-muted-foreground" />}
								/>
							))}
						</CardList>
						<CardFooter className="mt-auto">
							<Button variant="outline" size="sm" render={<a href="/editions/new" />}>
								<Icon name="calendar" />
								Schedule a release
							</Button>
						</CardFooter>
					</Card>
					<Card className="xl:col-span-2">
						<CardHeader>
							<CardTitle>Activity</CardTitle>
							<CardDescription>Collects, tips, and follows.</CardDescription>
							<CardAction>
								<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/activity" />}>
									View all
								</Button>
							</CardAction>
						</CardHeader>
						<CardList>
							{activity.map((item) => (
								<Entity
									key={item.id}
									leading={<Avatar variant="art" size="sm" fallback={item.initials} alt="" />}
									title={item.who}
									subtitle={item.what}
									action={<RelativeTime date={Date.now() - item.when} className="text-caption text-muted-foreground" />}
								/>
							))}
						</CardList>
					</Card>
				</Grid>
			</Page>
		</AppShell>
	)
}
```

# FeedPage

Social reading feed with a side rail: a feed-width main column (composer, For you / Following Tabs, one Card per post, an edition drop with price, supply Meter and Collect, a Skeleton for the next page) beside a sticky rail of who-to-follow and upcoming drops that drops away below lg.

**Intent:** Reach for this for timelines, activity streams, and any reverse-chronological reading surface where people also act on what they read. Not for record management (DashboardPage) or side-by-side browsing (ListDetailPage).

## Notes

- The main column is capped at `--region-feed` (640px) inside a `wide` page, so posts keep a reading measure while the rail fills the desktop width. The rail is a fixed `w-80` aside, `sticky` at lg and `hidden` below it — its content is supplementary, so nothing is lost on mobile.
- Feed scope is `Tabs` (underline, stretched to the column with `flex`): peer views of the same feed. The composer sits above them because posting applies to both.
- The composer is a Card holding `Textarea autoResize` plus ghost icon Buttons and a secondary `Post` — not ChatComposer, which submits on Enter and is for conversations.
- Each post is a Card: an Entity byline in a CardList (with an OverflowMenu for post actions), body copy, then media in an AspectBox at the asset's own ratio, inset with `rounded-concentric-lg/6` so its corners follow the card's in every theme.
- An edition drop adds a `Badge appearance="overlay"` on the artwork, title and price, the one primary Button on the page (`Collect`), and a `Meter` for supply — collected against a known maximum is a level, not task progress.
- Actions are ghost sm Buttons (icon + count) in a Row pulled out by the button's own padding (`-ms-3`) so the first icon sits on the text edge.
- Loading the next page shows a Skeleton post in the shape the post will land in, above the explicit load-more Button in its `loading` state — predictable for keyboard and AT users, unlike infinite scroll.

## Accessibility

- Each post is an <article>, so AT users can jump between posts; the rail is a labelled <aside> landmark.
- Rail card titles render as h2 (CardTitle `render={<h2 />}`) under the page's one h1.
- Icon-only buttons and every Follow / Remind button carry aria-labels naming their target; counts stay in the accessible name.
- The supply Meter is role=meter with a getAriaValueText reading ("62 of 100 collected").
- The Skeleton card is aria-busy; the loading Button keeps its label ("Loading posts").

# LandingPage

Product / open-source landing page: a centered hero with an eyebrow Badge, one display headline, lede, two CTAs and a copyable install command; a Browser-framed product preview composed from real components; a six-up feature grid; a setup section with tabbed code; an agent-workflow section with terminal output; a CTA card; and a link-column footer.

**Intent:** Reach for this for the marketing route of a developer product, library, or tool: the page where the product shows itself working and the reader installs or signs up. For a branded, editorial marketing site use BrandLandingPage. Not for product UI (display type and one-per-view rules forbid it inside the app).

## Notes

- Display type is the marketing voice: exactly one display headline per page (`text-display-lg` on phones, `text-display-2xl` from `sm`). Every section below uses `text-heading-1` with a `text-overline` kicker.
- The eyebrow is a small outline Badge (`size="sm"`): the badge's own size, never a type class forced onto its label. Hierarchy above the fold is eyebrow, display, lede, CTAs, install command.
- The lede is body-lg capped at the prose measure. The headline may be wide; reading text may not.
- Two CTAs max per row: one primary, one quiet outline. The install line is a `CodeBlock` with `prompt="$"`, so it truncates on one line and copy takes only the command.
- Show the product instead of describing it. The preview is real components (PageHeader, metric Cards, a Meter, a CardList of Entity rows, Message and Bubble, ChatComposer) inside `Browser`, wrapped in an `inert` div so the picture's controls never take focus. Secondary columns hide on small screens rather than stacking into a long mock.
- Features are Cards in a fixed `Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }}`, so six items always land as full rows (3 x 2, 2 x 3, 1 x 6) without an orphan.
- Multi-line code uses `CodeBlock` with a filename; switch related snippets with `Tabs`, defaulting to the most complete one. Terminal output passes `highlight={false}` so a code highlighter does not colour prose.
- Reveal wraps below-the-fold blocks only (features, code, CTA). It no-ops under reduced motion via the motion policy.
- Hide nav groups on narrow screens by wrapping them in a `max-md:hidden` div: a `Row` or `Button` sets its own display, which a `hidden` class on the same element does not reliably override.

## Accessibility

- The hero headline is the page h1; section titles are h2s and feature and step titles are h3s. Footer column labels are h2s inside the footer nav.
- The product preview is a `figure` with a visible figcaption. Its content is `inert`, which removes it from the tab order and the accessibility tree, so its headings and buttons do not pollute the outline.
- Reveal renders content immediately (no animation) when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
- CTA buttons are real links with visible text, with no icon-only CTAs. Footer links keep a 36px minimum row height for touch.
