---

# ListDetailPage

Searchable list beside the selected record's detail: interactive Entity rows in a CardList (5 of 12 columns) and a sticky detail pane (7) with an editable field, a label/value list, record actions with a destructive confirmation, and recent activity. Below lg it becomes a drill-in.

**Intent:** Reach for this when a route lists records AND works on one at a time (members + member, inbox + message, orders + order). For pure browsing with no selection, a single-column FeedPage or a DashboardPage table is simpler.

## Notes

- Region cap is `wide`; Columns 12 → Col 5 (list) + Col 7 (detail). Below lg the list and detail share one column as a drill-in: selecting a row shows the detail with an `All members` back button (lg:hidden), and the back button returns to the list. The panes swap with `max-lg:hidden`, so desktop always shows both.
- Rows are interactive Entity inside one Card + CardList. Selection is Entity `selected`; `sable-surface` on the list card makes its selected step 12% ink off the card, so a selected row stays distinct from its muted avatar.
- Search filters the list in place (name, email, role). No matches swap the CardList for an EmptyState with a Clear search action; the selected detail stays open.
- A pending invite lives in the same list: a mail glyph in the Avatar, an `Invited` Badge, and an invite-specific detail (role on joining, sent, expires, invited by; Resend and Revoke actions).
- The role Select edits the record in place; its Field description states what the role can do. The owner's role is read-only and the owner has no remove action.
- Read-only facts are a native `<dl className="sable-list-dl sable-list-dl-2">` inside an `@container`, so pairs go two-up only when the pane is wide enough.
- Remove / revoke run through DestructiveActionModal; on confirm the next row is selected. Page-level counts (members, pending, seats) live in the PageHeader description and update with the list.
- The detail pane is sticky (lg:top-6) so it stays in view while a long list scrolls.

## Accessibility

- Each row is a real button (Entity `interactive` + `onSelect`): Tab moves through rows, Enter/Space selects. The selected row is Entity `selected`, which paints the selected fill and sets aria-current; list avatars are aria-hidden so initials are not read before the name.
- The detail pane is a labelled region (`Member details`) whose title is a level-2 heading.
- On a phone, drilling in moves focus to the back button; going back returns focus to the row that was open. After a remove, focus lands on the newly selected row; after Clear search, on the search field.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from "react"
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, Col, Columns, DestructiveActionModal, EmptyState, Entity, Field, Icon, Page, PageHeader, Row, SearchInput, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, Stack, StatusDot } from "@sableui/react"

type Role = "owner" | "admin" | "editor" | "viewer"

const roles: { value: Role; label: string }[] = [
	{ value: "owner", label: "Owner" },
	{ value: "admin", label: "Admin" },
	{ value: "editor", label: "Editor" },
	{ value: "viewer", label: "Viewer" },
]

const roleLabel: Record<Role, string> = {
	owner: "Owner",
	admin: "Admin",
	editor: "Editor",
	viewer: "Viewer",
}

const roleSummary: Record<Role, string> = {
	owner: "Full access, including payouts and billing. Transfer ownership in studio settings.",
	admin: "Manages members, editions and payouts.",
	editor: "Drafts, prices and releases editions.",
	viewer: "Sees editions and sales, but can't change them.",
}

type Activity = { id: string; icon: string; text: string; when: string }

type Member = {
	id: string
	name: string
	email: string
	initials: string
	role: Role
	pending: boolean
	handle?: string
	joined?: string
	lastActive?: string
	editions?: number
	invitedBy?: string
	sent?: string
	expires?: string
	resent?: boolean
	activity: Activity[]
}

const seats = 10

const initialMembers: Member[] = [
	{
		id: "u_01", name: "Ada Lovelace", handle: "@ada", email: "ada@atelier.art", initials: "AL", role: "owner", pending: false,
		joined: "Mar 4, 2024", lastActive: "Online now", editions: 12,
		activity: [
			{ id: "a1", icon: "gem", text: "Released Analytical Engine No. 3 — edition of 50", when: "2 hours ago" },
			{ id: "a2", icon: "mail", text: "Invited louise@bourgeois.studio as Editor", when: "2 days ago" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "u_02", name: "Grace Hopper", handle: "@grace", email: "grace@atelier.art", initials: "GH", role: "admin", pending: false,
		joined: "Mar 9, 2024", lastActive: "20 minutes ago", editions: 4,
		activity: [
			{ id: "a1", icon: "user", text: "Changed Frida Kahlo's role to Viewer", when: "Yesterday" },
			{ id: "a2", icon: "edit", text: "Updated pricing on First Compiler — edition of 10", when: "3 days ago" },
			{ id: "a3", icon: "gem", text: "Released First Compiler — edition of 10", when: "Sep 28" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "u_03", name: "Mary Shelley", handle: "@mary", email: "mary@atelier.art", initials: "MS", role: "editor", pending: false,
		joined: "Jun 18, 2024", lastActive: "3 hours ago", editions: 7,
		activity: [
			{ id: "a1", icon: "calendar", text: "Scheduled Frankenstein Studies for Oct 14", when: "3 hours ago" },
			{ id: "a2", icon: "gem", text: "Released The Last Man — edition of 25", when: "Sep 21" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "u_04", name: "Nina Simone", handle: "@nina", email: "nina@atelier.art", initials: "NS", role: "editor", pending: false,
		joined: "Jan 12, 2025", lastActive: "Yesterday", editions: 3,
		activity: [
			{ id: "a1", icon: "upload", text: "Uploaded artwork for Little Girl Blue", when: "Yesterday" },
			{ id: "a2", icon: "gem", text: "Released Feeling Good — edition of 100", when: "Aug 30" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "u_05", name: "Frida Kahlo", handle: "@frida", email: "frida@atelier.art", initials: "FK", role: "viewer", pending: false,
		joined: "Jul 2, 2025", lastActive: "4 days ago", editions: 0,
		activity: [{ id: "a1", icon: "comment", text: "Commented on the Las Dos Fridas draft", when: "4 days ago" }],
	},
	{
		id: "i_01", name: "louise@bourgeois.studio", email: "louise@bourgeois.studio", initials: "", role: "editor", pending: true,
		invitedBy: "Ada Lovelace", sent: "2 days ago", expires: "In 5 days",
		activity: [],
	},
]

export function ListDetailPage() {
	const [members, setMembers] = useState(initialMembers)
	const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>("u_02")
	const [query, setQuery] = useState("")
	// Below lg the list and the detail share one column: selecting drills in.
	const [showDetail, setShowDetail] = useState(false)
	const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false)
	const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
	const backRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
	const searchRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

	const needle = query.trim().toLowerCase()
	const visible = members.filter((m) =>
		[m.name, m.email, m.handle ?? "", roleLabel[m.role]].some((v) => v.toLowerCase().includes(needle)),
	)
	const selected = members.find((m) => m.id === selectedId) ?? null
	const active = members.filter((m) => !m.pending).length
	const pending = members.length - active

	// Drilling in on a phone moves focus to the detail's back control; the
	// control is display:none at lg, so desktop focus stays on the list.
	useEffect(() => {
		if (showDetail && backRef.current?.offsetParent) backRef.current.focus()
	}, [showDetail, selectedId])

	function select(id: string) {
		setSelectedId(id)
		setShowDetail(true)
	}

	function focusRow(id: string | undefined) {
		requestAnimationFrame(() => {
			listRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-member-id="${id}"] button`)?.focus()
		})
	}

	function backToList() {
		setShowDetail(false)
		focusRow(selectedId ?? undefined)
	}

	function setRole(id: string, role: Role) {
		setMembers((list) => list.map((m) => (m.id === id ? { ...m, role } : m)))
	}

	function resend(id: string) {
		setMembers((list) =>
			list.map((m) => (m.id === id ? { ...m, sent: "Just now", expires: "In 7 days", resent: true } : m)),
		)
	}

	function remove(id: string) {
		const index = members.findIndex((m) => m.id === id)
		const rest = members.filter((m) => m.id !== id)
		setMembers(rest)
		const next = rest[Math.min(index, rest.length - 1)]?.id
		setSelectedId(next ?? null)
		setShowDetail(false)
		// The control that opened the confirmation is gone; land on the next row.
		focusRow(next)
	}

	return (
		<Page as="main" max="wide" gap={4} className="py-6">
			<PageHeader
				title="Members"
				description={`${active} members · ${pending} pending ${pending === 1 ? "invite" : "invites"} · ${members.length} of ${seats} seats used`}
				actions={<Button iconStart={<Icon name="plus" />}>Invite member</Button>}
			/>
			<Columns count={{ base: 1, lg: 12 }}>
				<Col span={{ base: 1, lg: 5 }} className={showDetail ? "max-lg:hidden" : undefined}>
					<Stack gap={3}>
						<SearchInput
							ref={searchRef}
							value={query}
							onValueChange={setQuery}
							placeholder="Search name, email or role"
							aria-label="Search members"
						/>
						{/* sable-surface derives the rows' selected step from the card (12% ink),
						    so a selected row stays distinct from its muted avatar. */}
						<Card ref={listRef} className="sable-surface">
							{visible.length > 0 ? (
								<CardList aria-label="Members">
									{visible.map((m) => {
										const isSelected = m.id === selectedId
										return (
											<Entity
												key={m.id}
												data-member-id={m.id}
												interactive
												selected={isSelected}
												onSelect={() => select(m.id)}
												leading={
													<Avatar variant="art"
														seed={m.name}
														fallback={m.pending ? <Icon name="mail" className="size-5" /> : m.initials}
														status={m.lastActive === "Online now" ? <StatusDot tone="success" /> : undefined}
														// The row's title already names it: keep the initials out of the row's name.
														aria-hidden
													/>
												}
												title={m.name}
												subtitle={
													m.pending
														? `${roleLabel[m.role]} · invite sent ${m.sent?.toLowerCase()}`
														: `${roleLabel[m.role]} · ${m.handle}`
												}
												action={m.pending ? <Badge tone="info">Invited</Badge> : undefined}
											/>
										)
									})}
								</CardList>
							) : (
								<CardContent>
									<EmptyState
										icon={<Icon name="search" />}
										title="No members found"
										description={`Nobody matches “${query.trim()}”. Try a name, email or role.`}
										action={
											<Button variant="secondary" size="sm" onClick={() => {
												setQuery("")
												searchRef.current?.focus()
											}}>
												Clear search
											</Button>
										}
									/>
								</CardContent>
							)}
						</Card>
					</Stack>
				</Col>
				<Col span={{ base: 1, lg: 7 }} className={showDetail ? undefined : "max-lg:hidden"}>
					<Stack role="region" aria-label="Member details" gap={3} className="lg:sticky lg:top-6">
						<Button
							ref={backRef}
							variant="ghost"
							size="sm"
							bleed="start"
							iconStart={<Icon name="chevron-left" />}
							onClick={backToList}
							className="self-start lg:hidden"
						>
							All members
						</Button>
						{selected === null ? (
							<EmptyState
								surface="card"
								icon={<Icon name="user" />}
								title="No member selected"
								description="Choose someone from the list to see their role and activity."
							/>
						) : (
							<>
								<Card>
									<CardHeader>
										<Row gap={2}>
											<Avatar variant="art"
												size="lg"
												fallback={selected.pending ? <Icon name="mail" className="size-6" /> : selected.initials}
												status={selected.lastActive === "Online now" ? <StatusDot tone="success" /> : undefined}
												alt={selected.pending ? "Pending invite" : selected.name}
											/>
											<Stack gap={0} className="min-w-0">
												<CardTitle render={<h2 />} className="truncate">
													{selected.name}
												</CardTitle>
												<CardDescription className="truncate">
													{selected.pending ? "Hasn't joined yet" : `${selected.handle} · ${selected.email}`}
												</CardDescription>
											</Stack>
										</Row>
										{selected.pending ? (
											<CardAction>
												<Badge tone="info">Invited</Badge>
											</CardAction>
										) : null}
									</CardHeader>
									<CardContent>
										<Stack gap={5}>
											<Field
												label={selected.pending ? "Role on joining" : "Role"}
												description={roleSummary[selected.role]}
											>
												<Select
													items={roles}
													value={selected.role}
													onValueChange={(value) => setRole(selected.id, value as Role)}
													disabled={selected.role === "owner"}
												>
													<SelectTrigger className="max-w-72" />
													<SelectContent>
														{roles
															.filter((r) => r.value !== "owner" || selected.role === "owner")
															.map((r) => (
																<SelectItem key={r.value} value={r.value}>
																	{r.label}
																</SelectItem>
															))}
													</SelectContent>
												</Select>
											</Field>
											<div className="@container">
												{selected.pending ? (
													<dl className="sable-list-dl sable-list-dl-2">
														<dt>Sent</dt>
														<dd>{selected.sent}</dd>
														<dt>Expires</dt>
														<dd>{selected.expires}</dd>
														<dt>Invited by</dt>
														<dd>{selected.invitedBy}</dd>
													</dl>
												) : (
													<dl className="sable-list-dl sable-list-dl-2">
														<dt>Email</dt>
														<dd>{selected.email}</dd>
														<dt>Joined</dt>
														<dd>{selected.joined}</dd>
														<dt>Last active</dt>
														<dd className={selected.lastActive === "Online now" ? "text-success" : undefined}>
															{selected.lastActive}
														</dd>
														<dt>Editions released</dt>
														<dd>{selected.editions}</dd>
													</dl>
												)}
											</div>
										</Stack>
									</CardContent>
									{selected.role !== "owner" ? (
										<CardFooter>
											<Row gap={2} wrap>
												{selected.pending ? (
													<Button
														variant="secondary"
														size="sm"
														iconStart={<Icon name={selected.resent ? "check" : "send"} />}
														disabled={selected.resent}
														onClick={() => resend(selected.id)}
													>
														{selected.resent ? "Invite resent" : "Resend invite"}
													</Button>
												) : null}
												<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setConfirming(true)}>
													{selected.pending ? "Revoke invite" : "Remove from studio"}
												</Button>
											</Row>
										</CardFooter>
									) : null}
								</Card>
								{selected.activity.length > 0 ? (
									<Card>
										<CardHeader>
											<CardTitle render={<h3 />}>
												Recent activity
											</CardTitle>
										</CardHeader>
										<CardList>
											{selected.activity.map((a) => (
												<Entity
													key={a.id}
													leading={<Icon name={a.icon} className="text-muted-foreground" />}
													title={a.text}
													subtitle={a.when}
												/>
											))}
										</CardList>
									</Card>
								) : null}
								<DestructiveActionModal
									open={confirming}
									onOpenChange={setConfirming}
									title={selected.pending ? "Revoke this invite?" : `Remove ${selected.name}?`}
									description={
										selected.pending
											? `${selected.email} won't be able to join with the link they were sent.`
											: "They lose access to the studio right away. Editions they released stay on sale."
									}
									confirmLabel={selected.pending ? "Revoke invite" : "Remove member"}
									onConfirm={() => remove(selected.id)}
								/>
							</>
						)}
					</Stack>
				</Col>
			</Columns>
		</Page>
	)
}
```

# SettingsPage

Account settings inside the app shell: a sticky SideNav section rail beside a column of section Cards — a Profile form with the page's one explicit save, Card + CardList + Entity rows with Switches that apply instantly, a read-only payouts summary, account rows, and a delete card confirmed through DestructiveActionModal.

**Intent:** Reach for this for account/profile/workspace settings and any 'edit a handful of grouped preferences' route. Not for a single short form (use AuthPage's centered form shape) or bulk record editing (use DashboardPage + DataTable).

## Notes

- Region cap is `wide`, split on a 12-column track: a 3-column SideNav rail and a 9-column section column. The rail fills the space a lone content-width column would leave empty and gives the page its table of contents.
- The rail is `SideNav` (the documented settings sub-nav), sticky, with in-page anchor items; it hides below lg, where the sections simply stack and the shell's BottomNav carries app navigation.
- One save model, stated in the copy: drafted text (the Profile form) commits through its single footer save; toggles apply the moment they change, and the Notifications description says so. Never pair a Switch with a Save button.
- Settings rows are Card + CardList + Entity with the Switch in `action` — the row owns its title and one-line description; keep descriptions short, because Entity truncates its subtitle.
- Each section is a Card whose CardTitle holds an h2, so the page has a real heading outline under PageHeader's h1; Cards carry the anchor id and `scroll-mt-*` so anchor jumps clear the top edge.
- Field wires label/description/error a11y automatically; never hand-roll <label> + <input> pairs. Pair fields side by side with Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }}.
- The destructive action is last and isolated in its own Card, and it never acts directly: it opens DestructiveActionModal with type-to-confirm on the handle.
- Lives in the same AppShell as DashboardPage: Sidebar from lg up, AppHeader + BottomNav below it, with Settings marked active in both.

## Accessibility

- AppShell provides the skip link and <main id="main-content"> landmark; the active SidebarItem and BottomNavItem carry aria-current.
- The section rail is a labelled <nav> ("Settings sections") distinct from the primary navigation; its active item carries aria-current.
- Every section has an h2, so screen-reader heading navigation mirrors the rail.
- Each Switch takes its row title as aria-label, since the Entity title is not a <label>.
- Field auto-wires htmlFor/id, aria-describedby (description + error), aria-invalid, and required.
- DestructiveActionModal is an alertdialog: focus opens on Cancel, the backdrop does not dismiss, and the confirm stays disabled until the handle is typed.

# ApiKeysBlock

An API keys card: each key's name with its masked hint in Code, when it was created and last used, and an OverflowMenu to rename, roll or revoke.

**Intent:** Reach for this for developer settings — API keys, access tokens, webhook secrets. Show a newly created key once, in a Dialog with a copy button; this list only ever shows the masked hint.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 20rem–42rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Only the last four characters are shown. A full key never appears in a list, so there is no copy action here.
- "Last used" sits in the detail line: it is what tells someone a key is safe to revoke.
- Revoke is the destructive item, last and after a separator; confirm it in your handler with DestructiveActionModal.

## Accessibility

- Each OverflowMenu is labelled with the key's name, so the triggers are distinguishable.
- The masked hint is a Code element inside the title, read after the key's name.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, cn, Code, Entity, Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

const keys = [
	{ id: "k1", name: "Production", hint: "sk_live_••••4f2a", detail: "Created Mar 2 · used 4 minutes ago" },
	{ id: "k2", name: "Staging", hint: "sk_test_••••91cd", detail: "Created Feb 11 · used yesterday" },
	{ id: "k3", name: "CI deploys", hint: "sk_live_••••0b7e", detail: "Created Jan 5 · never used" },
]

export interface ApiKeysBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	onCreate?: () => void
	/** Called with the key's id and the action chosen from its menu. */
	onKeyAction?: (id: string, action: "rename" | "roll" | "revoke") => void
}

export function ApiKeysBlock({ className, framed = true, onCreate, onKeyAction }: ApiKeysBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-2xl", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>API keys</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>A key is shown once, when you create it. Store it somewhere safe.</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Button size="sm" variant="outline" iconStart={<Icon name="key" />} onClick={onCreate}>
						Create key
					</Button>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardList>
				{keys.map((k) => (
					<Entity
						key={k.id}
						title={
							<span className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2">
								{k.name}
								<Code>{k.hint}</Code>
							</span>
						}
						subtitle={k.detail}
						action={
							<OverflowMenu label={`Manage the ${k.name} key`} size="icon-sm">
								<MenuItem onClick={() => onKeyAction?.(k.id, "rename")}>Rename</MenuItem>
								<MenuItem onClick={() => onKeyAction?.(k.id, "roll")}>Roll key</MenuItem>
								<MenuSeparator />
								<MenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => onKeyAction?.(k.id, "revoke")}>
									Revoke
								</MenuItem>
							</OverflowMenu>
						}
					/>
				))}
			</CardList>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# ChatThreadBlock

A short message thread on a card: Message rows with incoming muted Bubbles on the start side and your own primary Bubbles on the end.

**Intent:** Reach for this to show a conversation excerpt — a support preview, a comment thread on a dashboard, a recent-DM card. A working chat with a composer, streaming and history is the ChatPanel page shell.

**Block:** Social & messaging · card · designed for 16rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Sit it on a card, not straight on a muted page: incoming bubbles are the muted surface, and would vanish into it.
- Your own messages align to the end with the primary Bubble; everyone else's align to the start.

## Accessibility

- Each Message carries a messageId, so a thread can be addressed and announced item by item.
- Direction is shown by alignment and colour; when senders matter, add the sender's name to each Message.

## Source

```tsx
import { Bubble, Card, CardContent, cn, Message } from "@sableui/react"

const messages = [
	{ id: "m1", text: "Is the new cover ready?", mine: false },
	{ id: "m2", text: "Uploading it now 🎉", mine: true },
	{ id: "m3", text: "Perfect, thank you!", mine: false },
]

export interface ChatThreadBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border. Keep it framed on a muted page: incoming bubbles are the muted surface too. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function ChatThreadBlock({ className, framed = true }: ChatThreadBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-2">
				{messages.map((m) => (
					<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id} align={m.mine ? "end" : undefined}>
						<Bubble variant={m.mine ? "primary" : undefined} align={m.mine ? "end" : undefined}>
							{m.text}
						</Bubble>
					</Message>
				))}
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# CommandPaletteBlock

An inline command palette: CommandMenuPanel with a filter field and grouped actions, each with an icon and its keyboard shortcut.

**Intent:** Reach for this to show a command list in place — an empty state that teaches shortcuts, an onboarding step, a quick-actions card. The ⌘K palette that opens over the app is CommandMenu; this is its panel without the dialog.

**Block:** Navigation · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Each command shows its shortcut as a Kbd hint, so the palette also teaches the keys.
- `onCommand` receives the command's id; ids also key the rows, so two commands may share a label.
- No card around it: the panel is its own surface, lifted with `shadow-sm` when it sits on a muted section.

## Accessibility

- CommandMenuPanel wires the filter input to the list as a combobox, with arrow-key navigation and the active row announced.
- Shortcut hints are Kbd elements, read as keys.

## Source

```tsx
import { cn, CommandMenuPanel, Kbd, type CommandItem } from "@sableui/react"

const commands = [
	{ id: "new-project", icon: "plus", label: "New project", key: "N" },
	{ id: "invite", icon: "user", label: "Invite teammate", key: "I" },
	{ id: "settings", icon: "gear", label: "Open settings", key: "," },
]

export interface CommandPaletteBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** Called with the chosen command's id. */
	onCommand?: (id: string) => void
}

export function CommandPaletteBlock({ className, onCommand }: CommandPaletteBlockProps) {
	const items: CommandItem[] = commands.map((c) => ({
		id: c.id,
		group: "Actions",
		icon: c.icon,
		label: c.label,
		hint: <Kbd>{c.key}</Kbd>,
		onSelect: () => onCommand?.(c.id),
	}))
	return <CommandMenuPanel className={cn("w-full max-w-xs shadow-sm", className)} placeholder="Type a command…" items={items} />
}
```

# CtaBandBlock

A closing call to action: a centred h2 and one-line lede on a card, with a primary and an outline action.

**Intent:** Reach for this as the last section before the footer, repeating the hero's primary action once the reader has seen the case. Mid-page prompts to sign up belong inline, not in a band.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Copied from the LandingPage page shell's closing call to action.
- The primary action matches the hero's, so the page asks for one thing twice rather than two things once.
- Sitting on a Card lifts it from the page without a coloured band, so it follows any preset.

## Accessibility

- The section is labelled by its h2.
- Both actions are links styled as Buttons, because they navigate.

## Source

```tsx
import { useId } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardContent, cn, Region, Row, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const cta = {
```

# DangerZoneBlock

A delete-account card: what deleting removes and what survives, one destructive Button, and a DestructiveActionModal that asks for the handle to be typed before it acts.

**Intent:** Reach for this as the last section of account, workspace or project settings. Deleting a single record from a list is an OverflowMenu item that opens DestructiveActionModal directly, not a card.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 20rem–42rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Copied from the SettingsPage page shell's Delete account section.
- The button never acts directly: it opens the modal, whose confirm stays disabled until the handle is typed.
- The description says what is lost AND what is kept ("Collectors keep the editions they own"), which is what people want to know before they decide.

## Accessibility

- DestructiveActionModal is an alertdialog: focus opens on Cancel and the backdrop does not dismiss it.
- The CardTitle is an h2, so the section is reachable by heading.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, DestructiveActionModal } from "@sableui/react"

const account = { handle: "ada", editions: 12 }

export interface DangerZoneBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called once the person has typed the handle and confirmed. */
	onDelete?: () => void
}

export function DangerZoneBlock({ className, framed = true, onDelete }: DangerZoneBlockProps) {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
	return (
		<>
			<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-2xl", className)}>
				<CardHeader>
					<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Delete account</CardTitle>
					<CardDescription>
						Permanently remove your profile, editions, and sales history. Collectors keep the editions they own.
					</CardDescription>
				</CardHeader>
				<CardFooter actions className="justify-end">
					<Button variant="destructive" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
						Delete account
					</Button>
				</CardFooter>
			</Card>
			<DestructiveActionModal
				open={open}
				onOpenChange={setOpen}
				title="Delete your account?"
				description={`This permanently removes your profile, ${account.editions} editions, and sales history. Pending payouts are still sent. This can't be undone.`}
				confirmLabel="Delete account"
				confirmingLabel="Deleting…"
				confirmText={account.handle}
				onConfirm={() => {
					setOpen(false)
					onDelete?.()
				}}
			/>
		</>
	)
}
```

# DeviceComparisonBlock

A comparison card: each series' total sits in the header as a pressable tile, and the one pressed is plotted below as a daily BarChart.

**Intent:** Reach for this when two or three measures share a page and the reader looks at one at a time — devices, regions, plans. To see them together, plot both in one BarChart or LineChart instead.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 20rem–48rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The totals are the switch: Toggles in a labelled ToggleGroup, so the number and the control are one thing, with the group's own pressed and hover states.
- Switching eases every bar to its new height rather than redrawing.
- Below sm the tiles stack under the title and divide with a top rule instead of a side rule.

## Accessibility

- Each total is a Toggle (aria-pressed) named by its label and value, in a ToggleGroup labelled "Device" with arrow-key movement between tiles.
- The chart's name says which series is plotted, so the data table is unambiguous.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { BarChart, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@sableui/react"

/** 30 days of visitors — replace with your own rows ({ date, desktop, mobile }). */
const days = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => ({
	date: new Date(2026, 8, 1 + i).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
	desktop: Math.round(320 + Math.sin(i / 3) * 90 + (i % 5) * 14),
	mobile: Math.round(260 + Math.cos(i / 4) * 80 + (i % 4) * 18),
}))

const series = [
	{ key: "desktop", label: "Desktop" },
	{ key: "mobile", label: "Mobile" },
] as const

const shortDate = (iso: string) => new Date(`${iso}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })

export interface DeviceComparisonBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function DeviceComparisonBlock({ className, framed = true }: DeviceComparisonBlockProps) {
	const [active, setActive] = useState<string>("desktop")
	const totals = Object.fromEntries(series.map((s) => [s.key, days.reduce((sum, d) => sum + d[s.key], 0)]))
	const current = series.find((s) => s.key === active) ?? series[0]
	return (
		// overflow-hidden: the square tiles meet the card's rounded corner.
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-3xl overflow-hidden", className)}>
			<div className="flex flex-col border-b border-border sm:flex-row">
				<CardHeader className="flex-1 pb-[var(--card-p,--spacing(6))]">
					<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Visitors by device</CardTitle>
					<CardDescription>The last 30 days. Pick a device to plot it.</CardDescription>
				</CardHeader>
				{/* The totals ARE the switch: one pressed tile per series. */}
				<ToggleGroup
					value={[active]}
					onValueChange={(v: unknown[]) => v[0] && setActive(String(v[0]))}
					aria-label="Device"
					className="items-stretch gap-0"
				>
					{series.map((s) => (
						<Toggle
							key={s.key}
							value={s.key}
							className="h-auto flex-1 flex-col items-start justify-center gap-1 rounded-none border-border px-6 py-4 text-start text-foreground max-sm:border-t sm:border-s"
						>
							<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">{s.label}</span>
							<span className="text-mono-lg">{totals[s.key].toLocaleString("en-US")}</span>
						</Toggle>
					))}
				</ToggleGroup>
			</div>
			<CardContent>
				<BarChart
					label={`${current.label} visitors per day, last 30 days`}
					data={days}
					index="date"
					series={[current]}
					indexFormatter={shortDate}
					radius={3}
					className="h-64"
				/>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# EventCardBlock

An upcoming-event card: a DateTile beside the title and time, a "starts in" Badge, attendees as an AvatarGroup, and Decline / Join.

**Intent:** Reach for this for the next meeting, booking or live session on a dashboard or home screen. For a list of many upcoming events, use Entity rows with a DateTile as `leading`.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The DateTile names the day; the full weekday and time range sit in text beside it.
- The Badge is one title line tall and wraps under the title rather than squeezing it onto two lines.
- AvatarGroup `fit` trades avatars for the +N count before it pushes the actions to their own line.

## Accessibility

- DateTile is a <time> with a machine-readable date; the time range is plain text read in order after the title.
- The AvatarGroup's aria-label states the total attendee count.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardTitle, cn, DateTile } from "@sableui/react"

const event = {
	title: "Design review",
	date: new Date(2026, 9, 14),
	when: "Tuesday, 2:00 – 2:45 PM",
	starts: "In 10 min",
	attendees: ["MO", "SR", "JL"],
	total: 7,
}

export interface EventCardBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the person's answer. */
	onRespond?: (answer: "join" | "decline") => void
}

export function EventCardBlock({ className, framed = true, onRespond }: EventCardBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardContent className="flex gap-4">
				<DateTile date={event.date} />
				<div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1">
					{/* The row carries the title's type, so the badge's box is exactly
					    one title line (`h-[1lh]`): it centres on the title and never
					    makes the row taller than the title alone. When a bolder or
					    roomier look leaves no space beside the title, the badge wraps
					    to its own line instead of squeezing the title onto two. */}
					<div className="flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between gap-x-2 text-title-lg">
						<CardTitle>{event.title}</CardTitle>
						<span className="flex h-[1lh] shrink-0 items-center">
							<Badge tone="info" size="sm">
								{event.starts}
							</Badge>
						</span>
					</div>
					<CardDescription>{event.when}</CardDescription>
				</div>
			</CardContent>
			{/* `fit`: when a roomy look tightens the row, the stack gives up
			    avatars to the count instead of pushing the actions to a new line. */}
			<CardFooter className="flex-wrap justify-between gap-3">
				<AvatarGroup aria-label={`${event.total} attendees`} total={event.total} size="sm" surface={framed ? "card" : undefined} fit>
					{event.attendees.map((initials) => (
						<Avatar variant="art" key={initials} fallback={initials} alt={initials} />
					))}
				</AvatarGroup>
				<div className="flex gap-2">
					<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => onRespond?.("decline")}>
						Decline
					</Button>
					<Button size="sm" onClick={() => onRespond?.("join")}>
						Join
					</Button>
				</div>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# FaqBlock

A FAQ section: the heading and a way to ask beside an Accordion of questions, each answer one or two sentences.

**Intent:** Reach for this near pricing or at the end of a landing page, for the questions that block a decision. Long help content belongs in docs, not an accordion.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Every question starts closed: the list of questions is itself the useful summary.
- The way to ask a human sits beside the heading, so it is found before the reader scrolls the list.
- Capped at the `content` region width; questions wider than that are hard to scan.

## Accessibility

- Accordion triggers are buttons with aria-expanded, inside headings, so the questions are navigable by heading and operable by keyboard.
- The contact link is a real <a> inside the lede sentence.

## Source

```tsx
import { useId } from "react"
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger, cn, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const intro = {
	title: "Questions, answered",
	lede: "Can't find what you need?",
	contact: { label: "Write to us", href: "/contact" },
}

const questions = [
	{ q: "Is there a free plan?", a: "Yes. Starter is free forever for three live editions, with no fees on your first $1,000 in sales." },
	{ q: "Can I change plans later?", a: "Any time. Upgrades apply immediately and are prorated; downgrades take effect at the end of the billing period." },
	{ q: "Who owns the work I sell?", a: "You do. Collectors own the editions they buy, and you keep the rights to the work itself." },
	{ q: "How do payouts work?", a: "Sales clear after seven days and are paid out every Friday to the account you connect in settings." },
]

export interface FaqBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function FaqBlock({ className }: FaqBlockProps) {
	const titleId = useId()
	return (
		<Region as="section" aria-labelledby={titleId} max="content" className={cn("w-full py-16", className)}>
			<div className="grid gap-10 md:grid-cols-[1fr_2fr]">
				<Stack gap={2}>
					<h2 id={titleId} className="text-balance text-heading-2">
						{intro.title}
					</h2>
					<p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">
						{intro.lede}{" "}
						<a href={intro.contact.href} className="text-foreground underline underline-offset-4 motion-interactive hover:text-muted-foreground">
							{intro.contact.label}
						</a>
						.
					</p>
				</Stack>
				<Accordion>
					{questions.map((item) => (
						<AccordionItem key={item.q} value={item.q}>
							<AccordionTrigger>{item.q}</AccordionTrigger>
							<AccordionPanel>{item.a}</AccordionPanel>
						</AccordionItem>
					))}
				</Accordion>
			</div>
		</Region>
	)
}
```

# FeatureGridBlock

A feature section: an overline, an h2 and a lede over a grid of article cards, each with an icon in a well, a title and one sentence — 1, 2 then 3 columns.

**Intent:** Reach for this to explain what a product does in six or fewer points. For a sequence (first this, then that), use StepsBlock; for one proof point with numbers, TestimonialBlock.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Copied from the LandingPage page shell's features section.
- Six features fill 3 × 2 evenly; keep the count a multiple of three, or drop to cols={{ lg: 2 }}.
- Each body is one sentence. A feature that needs a paragraph needs its own section.
- Icons sit in a `sable-well`, which derives its fill from the card surface it is on.

## Accessibility

- Each feature is an <article> with an h3 under the section's h2.
- The icons are decorative; each title says what the feature is.

## Source

```tsx
import { useId } from "react"
import { Card, CardContent, cn, Grid, Icon, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const intro = {
	eyebrow: "Why Sable",
	title: "A design system with the rules written down",
	lede: "The decisions a senior designer would make are encoded once, so every screen your team or your agent builds starts from them.",
}

const features = [
	{ icon: "component", title: "Behavior built in", body: "Focus management, keyboard navigation, and ARIA come from Base UI primitives under every control." },
	{ icon: "eyedropper", title: "Semantic tokens end to end", body: "Re-theme the whole product, light and dark, from one preset without touching a component." },
	{ icon: "layout", title: "Pages, not just parts", body: "Landing, dashboard, settings, auth, and list-detail shells to copy and adapt." },
	{ icon: "book", title: "A contract agents can read", body: "registry.json, llms.txt, and a CLI hand agents the exact props, examples, and rules." },
	{ icon: "circle-check", title: "Lint that knows the design", body: "sable-lint flags raw colors, hand-built controls, and motion that ignores reduced motion." },
	{ icon: "play", title: "Motion with an off switch", body: "Named recipes run on one scale variable, so reduced motion stops every transition at once." },
]

export interface FeatureGridBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function FeatureGridBlock({ className }: FeatureGridBlockProps) {
	const titleId = useId()
	return (
		<Region as="section" aria-labelledby={titleId} max="wide" className={cn("w-full py-16 sm:py-24", className)}>
			<Stack gap={10}>
				<Stack gap={3} className="max-w-2xl">
					<p className="text-overline text-muted-foreground">{intro.eyebrow}</p>
					<h2 id={titleId} className="text-balance text-heading-1">
						{intro.title}
					</h2>
					<p className="text-body-lg text-muted-foreground">{intro.lede}</p>
				</Stack>
				<Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap={4}>
					{features.map((feature) => (
						<Card key={feature.title} render={<article />} className="h-full">
							<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">
								<span className="grid size-10 place-items-center rounded-md sable-well">

								</span>
								<h3 className="pt-2 text-title-lg">{feature.title}</h3>

							</CardContent>
						</Card>
					))}
				</Grid>
			</Stack>
		</Region>
	)
}
```

# FeedbackFormBlock

A feedback card: a one-to-five rating as a full-width ToggleGroup, an optional notes field, and Skip / Send feedback.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a post-session or post-purchase survey in a Sheet, Dialog or end-of-flow screen. For a feedback control anchored to a button in the app chrome, use the Feedback component (a popover).

**Block:** Social & messaging · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The rating is preselected, so one tap on Send is a complete answer; the notes are optional and say so.
- Skip is a ghost Button before the primary, so dismissing is always available and never competes with sending.
- `onDone` reports whether feedback was sent and, if so, the score and notes.

## Accessibility

- The ToggleGroup carries aria-label="Rating"; each Toggle's number is its name.
- The Textarea carries aria-label="Notes"; its placeholder is a prompt, not the label.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Textarea, Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@sableui/react"

const scale = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]

export interface FeedbackFormBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet or Dialog that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Skip calls it with `sent: false`; Send with `sent: true` and the answers. */
	onDone?: (sent: boolean, feedback?: { score: number; notes: string }) => void
}

export function FeedbackFormBlock({ className, framed = true, onDone }: FeedbackFormBlockProps) {
	const [score, setScore] = useState("4")
	const [notes, setNotes] = useState("")
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>How was the session?</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>One tap is enough. Notes help us more.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-4">
				<ToggleGroup value={[score]} onValueChange={(v: unknown[]) => v[0] && setScore(String(v[0]))} aria-label="Rating" className="w-full">
					{scale.map((n) => (
						<Toggle key={n} value={n} className="flex-1">
							{n}
						</Toggle>
					))}
				</ToggleGroup>
				<Textarea placeholder="What worked, what didn’t…" aria-label="Notes" rows={3} value={notes} onChange={(e) => setNotes(e.target.value)} />
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter actions className="justify-end">
				<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => onDone?.(false)}>
					Skip
				</Button>
				<Button size="sm" onClick={() => onDone?.(true, { score: Number(score), notes })}>
					Send feedback
				</Button>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# GoalProgressBlock

A goals card: a ring per goal in a RadialChart against its track (a full ring is 100%), a legend, and which goals are behind in the footer.

**Intent:** Reach for this for progress toward two to four targets — a quarter's goals, a plan's limits, onboarding steps. A single reading in a settings row is a Meter; many goals are a list of Progress bars.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 18rem–24rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- max={100} makes a full ring mean done; each ring draws round from 12 o'clock as the card scrolls into view.
- The footer names what is behind, so the card is actionable without reading the rings.
- Values are formatted as percents in the tooltip and data table.

## Accessibility

- The rings' data table lists each goal and its percent.
- Arrowing through the rings announces each goal; the legend names every ring's colour.

## Source

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, RadialChart } from "@sableui/react"

const goals = [
	{ goal: "Releases", progress: 82 },
	{ goal: "Collectors", progress: 64 },
	{ goal: "Revenue", progress: 91 },
]

export interface GoalProgressBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function GoalProgressBlock({ className, framed = true }: GoalProgressBlockProps) {
	const behind = goals.filter((g) => g.progress < 70)
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-sm", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Quarter goals</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Progress toward each target, in percent.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<RadialChart label="Progress toward quarter goals" data={goals} index="goal" valueKey="progress" max={100} className="h-64" valueFormatter={(v) => `${v}%`} />
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">
				{behind.length ? `${behind.map((g) => g.goal).join(" and ")} behind pace.` : "Every goal on pace."}
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

```tsx
					<p className="max-w-(--measure-prose) text-pretty text-body-lg text-muted-foreground">{hero.lede}</p>

							{hero.secondary.label}

					<CodeBlock prompt="$" code={hero.install} />
				</div>
			</Stack>
```

# InviteTeamBlock

An invite card: who is already on the team as an AvatarGroup, and an email field with Send.

**Intent:** Reach for this for team or project invites in onboarding, an empty workspace, or a settings section. For managing an existing member list with roles, use a CardList of Entity rows instead.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The field and Send are a <form>, so Enter sends; `onSend` receives the typed address.
- The AvatarGroup ring matches the card surface when framed and inherits the host surface when not.

## Accessibility

- The AvatarGroup carries an aria-label with the count, so the stack reads as one item, not four initials.
- The email Input carries aria-label; there is no visible label in this compact layout.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Input } from "@sableui/react"

const collaborators = ["MO", "SR", "JL", "AK"]

export interface InviteTeamBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet, Dialog or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the address typed, on Send or Enter. */
	onSend?: (email: string) => void
}

export function InviteTeamBlock({ className, framed = true, onSend }: InviteTeamBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>Invite your team</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Collaborators can edit every project.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-4">
				<AvatarGroup aria-label={`${collaborators.length} collaborators`} size="sm" surface={framed ? "card" : undefined}>
					{collaborators.map((initials) => (
						<Avatar variant="art" key={initials} fallback={initials} alt={initials} />
					))}
				</AvatarGroup>
				<form
					className="flex gap-2"
					onSubmit={(event) => {
						event.preventDefault()
						onSend?.(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("email") ?? ""))
					}}
				>
					<Input name="email" type="email" placeholder="name@company.com" aria-label="Email address" />
					<Button type="submit">Send</Button>
				</form>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# InvoiceHistoryBlock

A billing history card: a flush Table of date, plan, amount and status per invoice, with a download button on each row.

**Intent:** Reach for this in billing settings, under the current plan. For a long, filterable history (hundreds of rows, date ranges, export), use DataTable on its own page.

**Block:** Commerce · card · designed for 20rem–42rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The table runs edge to edge (CardContent flush); its first and last columns still line up with the card header's padding.
- Amounts are a numeric column — right-aligned with tabular figures — so they compare by eye.
- On a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways inside the card (with a quiet scrollbar) rather than squeezing its columns.

## Accessibility

- The download column has a screen-reader-only header, and each button names its invoice ("Download INV-0042").
- Status is text in a Badge; the dot's colour only reinforces it.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Icon, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@sableui/react"

const invoices = [
	{ id: "INV-0042", date: "Oct 1, 2026", plan: "Studio · yearly", amount: "$192.00", status: "Paid" },
	{ id: "INV-0031", date: "Sep 1, 2026", plan: "Studio · monthly", amount: "$20.00", status: "Paid" },
	{ id: "INV-0027", date: "Aug 1, 2026", plan: "Studio · monthly", amount: "$20.00", status: "Refunded" },
	{ id: "INV-0019", date: "Jul 1, 2026", plan: "Starter", amount: "$0.00", status: "Paid" },
]

export interface InvoiceHistoryBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the invoice id to download. */
	onDownload?: (id: string) => void
}

export function InvoiceHistoryBlock({ className, framed = true, onDownload }: InvoiceHistoryBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-2xl", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Invoices</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Sent to billing@studio.com on the 1st of each month.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent flush className="overflow-x-auto scrollbar-quiet">
				<Table>
					<TableHeader>
						<TableRow>
							<TableHead>Date</TableHead>
							<TableHead>Plan</TableHead>
							<TableHead numeric>Amount</TableHead>
							<TableHead>Status</TableHead>
							<TableHead className="w-0">
								<span className="sr-only">Download</span>
							</TableHead>
						</TableRow>
					</TableHeader>
					<TableBody>
						{invoices.map((invoice) => (
							<TableRow key={invoice.id}>
								<TableCell className="whitespace-nowrap">{invoice.date}</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="text-muted-foreground">{invoice.plan}</TableCell>
								<TableCell numeric>{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
								<TableCell>
									<Badge appearance="plain" tone={invoice.status === "Paid" ? "success" : "neutral"} dot>
										{invoice.status}
									</Badge>
								</TableCell>
								<TableCell>
									<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label={`Download ${invoice.id}`} onClick={() => onDownload?.(invoice.id)}>
										<Icon name="download" />
									</Button>
								</TableCell>
							</TableRow>
						))}
					</TableBody>
				</Table>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# KpiSparklineBlock

A KPI row with trends: three stat cards, each the value in the metric mono tier, a Sparkline of its last twelve weeks, and the change as a Badge.

**Intent:** Reach for this at the top of a dashboard or a landing page's proof section, where each number needs its recent shape. Without the trend, StatRowBlock is calmer; for one headline trend, TrafficTrendBlock.

**Block:** Dashboard · section

## Notes

- Each sparkline is coloured by what its measure is, and the change Badge by whether it is good: churn falling is good news in a warning-toned trend.
- The sparklines draw on as the row scrolls into view.
- One column on a phone, three from sm.

## Accessibility

- Each Sparkline is an image named by the measure and the period, with its range spoken.
- The change is stated in text (+8.2% vs last quarter) with an arrow icon; colour only reinforces it.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Grid, Icon, Sparkline } from "@sableui/react"

const kpis = [
	{ label: "Revenue", value: "$18,240", delta: "+8.2%", up: true, trend: [12, 14, 13, 17, 16, 19, 18, 21, 20, 24, 23, 26], tone: "success" },
	{ label: "Active users", value: "3,912", delta: "+3.1%", up: true, trend: [30, 31, 29, 33, 34, 33, 36, 35, 37, 38, 37, 39], tone: "info" },
	{ label: "Churn", value: "4.1%", delta: "−0.6%", up: false, trend: [9, 8, 9, 7, 8, 6, 7, 5, 6, 4, 5, 4], tone: "warning" },
] as const

export interface KpiSparklineBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function KpiSparklineBlock({ className }: KpiSparklineBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 3 }} gap={3} className={cn("w-full", className)}>
			{kpis.map((kpi) => (
				<Card key={kpi.label}>
					<CardHeader>
						<CardDescription>{kpi.label}</CardDescription>
						<CardTitle className="text-mono-xl">{kpi.value}</CardTitle>
						<CardAction>
							<Sparkline label={`${kpi.label}, last 12 weeks`} data={[...kpi.trend]} variant="area" tone={kpi.tone} />
						</CardAction>
					</CardHeader>
					<CardContent>
						<Badge tone={kpi.up ? "success" : "neutral"} size="sm" icon={<Icon name={kpi.up ? "arrow-up" : "arrow-down"} />}>
							{kpi.delta} vs last quarter
						</Badge>
					</CardContent>
				</Card>
			))}
		</Grid>
	)
}
```

# MediaPlayerBlock

A now-playing card: cover, title and artist as an Entity with a Like action, a position Slider with elapsed and remaining time, and previous / play-pause / next.

**Intent:** Reach for this for audio or video playback controls outside the media itself — a mini player, a podcast card, a preview in a feed. Playback over the video frame is the Video component's own chrome.

**Block:** Media & files · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Play/pause is the one filled control, centred between two ghost skips.
- Times are `text-mono-caption`, so the digits do not shift as they count.
- The cover is painted from the palette as a placeholder; swap it for the real artwork.

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only Button carries aria-label, and play/pause's label follows its state.
- The Slider carries aria-label="Position". Give it aria-valuetext in your player ("1:24 of 3:40") so the position is read as time, not a percentage.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardContent, cn, Entity, Icon, MediaImage, Slider } from "@sableui/react"

// `cover` is the artwork URL; left empty, the cover paints art seeded by the title.
const track = { title: "Low tide, high noon", artist: "Juno Avery", cover: "", duration: 220, position: 84 }

/** Seconds → m:ss, the way the readout and the screen reader both say it. */
function formatTime(seconds: number) {
	return `${Math.floor(seconds / 60)}:${String(Math.floor(seconds % 60)).padStart(2, "0")}`
}


export interface MediaPlayerBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the new playing state. */
	onPlayingChange?: (playing: boolean) => void
	onPrevious?: () => void
	onNext?: () => void
}

export function MediaPlayerBlock({ className, framed = true, onPlayingChange, onPrevious, onNext }: MediaPlayerBlockProps) {
	const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(true)
	const [position, setPosition] = useState(track.position)
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-4">
				{/* Entity's own row padding is for lists; inside a card's content the
				    card already pads it. */}
				<Entity
					className="p-0"
					leading={<MediaImage src={track.cover} seed={track.title} className="size-14 shrink-0 rounded-md" />}
					title={track.title}
					subtitle={track.artist}
					action={
						<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Like">
							<Icon name="heart" />
						</Button>
					}
				/>
				<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
					<Slider
						value={position}
						max={track.duration}
						onValueChange={setPosition}
						aria-label="Position"
						// Spoken as a time, not "38": the number alone means nothing.
						getAriaValueText={(_, value) => `${formatTime(value)} of ${formatTime(track.duration)}`}
					/>
					<div className="flex justify-between text-mono-caption text-muted-foreground">
						<span>{formatTime(position)}</span>
						<span>-{formatTime(track.duration - position)}</span>
					</div>
				</div>
				<div className="flex items-center justify-center gap-3">
					<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Previous" onClick={onPrevious}>
						<Icon name="previous" variant="solid" />
					</Button>
					<Button
						size="icon"
						aria-label={playing ? "Pause" : "Play"}
						onClick={() => {
							setPlaying(!playing)
							onPlayingChange?.(!playing)
						}}
					>
						<Icon name={playing ? "pause" : "play"} variant="solid" />
					</Button>
					<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Next" onClick={onNext}>
						<Icon name="next" variant="solid" />
					</Button>
				</div>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# NewsletterBlock

A newsletter sign-up card: the list's name, what it sends and how often, and an email field with Subscribe.

**Intent:** Reach for this in a footer, at the end of an article, or beside a changelog. Creating an account is SignUpBlock; inviting a teammate is InviteTeamBlock.

**Block:** Marketing · card · designed for 18rem–24rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Copied from the BrandLandingPage page shell's footer.
- The description says how often mail arrives — the one thing people want to know before they subscribe.
- The field and button sit side by side from sm up and stack on a phone, where the button goes full width.

## Accessibility

- The input has a real (visually hidden) <label>, not just a placeholder.
- The CardTitle renders an h2, so the sign-up is reachable by heading in a footer.

## Source

```tsx
import { useId } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Input } from "@sableui/react"

const newsletter = { title: "The Cove digest", body: "One note a month on trusted workflows and product releases." }

export interface NewsletterBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a footer or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the address on Subscribe or Enter. */
	onSubscribe?: (email: string) => void
}

export function NewsletterBlock({ className, framed = true, onSubscribe }: NewsletterBlockProps) {
	const emailId = useId()
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-sm", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>{newsletter.title}</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>{newsletter.body}</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<form
					className="grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_auto]"
					onSubmit={(event) => {
						event.preventDefault()
						onSubscribe?.(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("email") ?? ""))
					}}
				>
					<label htmlFor={emailId} className="sr-only">
						Work email
					</label>
					<Input id={emailId} name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" placeholder="you@company.com" required />
					<Button type="submit" className="w-full sm:w-auto">
						Subscribe
					</Button>
				</form>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# NotFoundBlock

A not-found page body: the status code in mono, a plain-language h1, what probably happened, and two ways on — home and search.

**Intent:** Reach for this as the body of a 404 route. An empty list or a search with no results inside a working page is EmptyState, not this.

**Block:** System · section

## Notes

- The heading says what happened in words; the code is a small mono label for people who look for it.
- Two ways on, one primary. Never a dead end with only the browser's back button.
- Capped at the `form` region width, so the short message stays a tight, centred column.

## Accessibility

- It renders the page's h1 — use it as the route's main content, inside <main>.
- Both actions are links styled as Buttons, because they navigate.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, cn, Icon, Region, Row, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const notFound = {
	code: "404",
	title: "This page isn't here",
	body: "It may have moved, or the link may be mistyped. Check the address, or head back to somewhere you know.",
	home: { label: "Go home", href: "/" },
	help: { label: "Search the docs", href: "/docs" },
}

export interface NotFoundBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function NotFoundBlock({ className }: NotFoundBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Region as="section" max="form" className={cn("w-full py-16 sm:py-24", className)}>
			<Stack gap={4} align="center" className="text-center">
				<p className="text-mono-md text-muted-foreground">{notFound.code}</p>
				<h1 className="text-balance text-heading-1">{notFound.title}</h1>
				<p className="text-pretty text-body-md text-muted-foreground">{notFound.body}</p>
				<Row gap={2} justify="center" wrap className="pt-2">
					<Button iconStart={<Icon name="home" />} render={<a href={notFound.home.href} />}>
						{notFound.home.label}
					</Button>
					<Button variant="outline" iconStart={<Icon name="search" />} render={<a href={notFound.help.href} />}>
						{notFound.help.label}
					</Button>
				</Row>
			</Stack>
		</Region>
	)
}
```

# NotificationListBlock

An activity list: Entity rows with the actor's Avatar, who did what, and a compact time with an unread StatusDot.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a notifications popover, a recent-activity card or an inbox preview. A full inbox with selection and bulk actions is a ListDetailPage.

**Block:** Social & messaging · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Rows are Card + CardList + Entity, inset from the card's padding at any density.
- Unread is a quiet info dot before the time, so the times keep one right edge — the list stays calm when most items are unread.
- framed={false} drops the surface for a Popover, which already is one.

## Accessibility

- The unread dot is decorative; each unread row also carries a screen-reader-only "(unread)" after the name.
- Each Avatar's alt is the actor's name.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Card, CardList, cn, Entity, StatusDot } from "@sableui/react"

const notifications = [
	{ initials: "MO", name: "Mara Okafor", what: "collected your edition", when: "2m", unread: true },
	{ initials: "SR", name: "Sam Rivera", what: "left a comment on Dusk", when: "1h", unread: false },
]

export interface NotificationListBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Popover or Sheet that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function NotificationListBlock({ className, framed = true }: NotificationListBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs overflow-hidden", className)}>
			<CardList>
				{notifications.map((n) => (
					<Entity
						key={n.name}
						leading={<Avatar variant="art" size="sm" fallback={n.initials} alt={n.name} />}
						title={
							<>
								{n.name}
								{n.unread ? <span className="sr-only"> (unread)</span> : null}
							</>
						}
						subtitle={n.what}
						action={
							<span className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-caption text-muted-foreground">
								{n.unread ? <StatusDot tone="info" /> : null}
								{n.when}
							</span>
						}
					/>
				))}
			</CardList>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# NotificationSettingsBlock

A preferences card: Entity rows in a CardList, each with a title, a one-line detail and a Switch that applies instantly.

**Intent:** Reach for this for any short list of on/off preferences — notifications, privacy, feature flags in a settings section. For a full settings route with a section rail, start from the SettingsPage page shell.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Switches apply the moment they change; never pair them with a Save button. `onChange` receives the row id and the new state.
- Rows are Card + CardList + Entity, so they inset with the card's padding at any density.

## Accessibility

- Each Switch takes its row title as aria-label, since the Entity title is not a <label>.
- Keep details to one line — Entity truncates its subtitle.

## Source

```tsx
import { Card, CardList, cn, Entity, Switch } from "@sableui/react"

const preferences = [
	{ id: "email", title: "Email notifications", detail: "Replies and mentions", on: true },
	{ id: "push", title: "Push notifications", detail: "On this device", on: false },
	{ id: "digest", title: "Weekly digest", detail: "Every Monday", on: true },
]

export interface NotificationSettingsBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet, Dialog or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called the moment a switch changes. Toggles apply instantly; there is no Save. */
	onChange?: (id: string, on: boolean) => void
}

export function NotificationSettingsBlock({ className, framed = true, onChange }: NotificationSettingsBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs overflow-hidden", className)}>
			<CardList>
				{preferences.map((p) => (
					<Entity
						key={p.id}
						title={p.title}
						subtitle={p.detail}
						action={<Switch defaultChecked={p.on} aria-label={p.title} onCheckedChange={(on: boolean) => onChange?.(p.id, on)} />}
					/>
				))}
			</CardList>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# OrderTrackingBlock

An order status card: order number, item and a status Badge in the header over a vertical dot Stepper of delivery milestones.

**Intent:** Reach for this for anything that moves through known stages — a delivery, an application, a review, a deployment. For an open-ended activity log, use a list of Entity rows with timestamps instead.

**Block:** Commerce · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The Stepper's `current` is the step under way; finished steps show their timestamp and future steps show none.
- The status Badge restates the current stage in one word so the card scans without reading the steps.

## Accessibility

- The Stepper is labelled "Delivery status" and marks the current step for assistive tech.
- The Badge's tone is backed by its text; colour alone never carries the status.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Stepper, StepperItem } from "@sableui/react"

const order = { number: "Order #2048", item: "Giclée print, 18 × 24 in", status: "In transit", current: 2 }

const steps = [
	{ title: "Order placed", detail: "Oct 9, 10:14 AM" },
	{ title: "Printed and packed", detail: "Oct 10, 4:02 PM" },
	{ title: "Out for delivery", detail: "Arriving today by 6 PM" },
	{ title: "Delivered", detail: undefined },
]

export interface OrderTrackingBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function OrderTrackingBlock({ className, framed = true }: OrderTrackingBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>{order.number}</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>{order.item}</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Badge tone="warning" size="sm">
						{order.status}
					</Badge>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<Stepper orientation="vertical" indicator="dot" current={order.current} aria-label="Delivery status">

					))}
				</Stepper>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# PricingCardBlock

A single-plan pricing card: a Monthly/Yearly ToggleGroup, the price and billing note, a checked feature list, and one full-width call to action.

**Intent:** Reach for this when one plan is on offer — an upgrade prompt, a paywall, a plan summary in billing settings. Comparing several tiers side by side is a pricing table, not three of these.

**Block:** Commerce · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The period switch is a ToggleGroup (a segmented control), not Tabs: it changes a value in place rather than showing another panel.
- The price is a heading tier because it is the card's headline; its unit and billing note sit beside and below it in muted body text.
- `onStart` receives the period showing, so checkout opens on the plan the person was looking at.

## Accessibility

- The ToggleGroup carries aria-label="Billing period"; each Toggle's text is its name.
- The check icons are decorative beside each feature's text.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Button, Card, CardContent, cn, Icon, Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@sableui/react"

const plan = {
	monthly: { price: "$20", note: "Billed monthly. Cancel anytime." },
	yearly: { price: "$16", note: "Billed $192 yearly. You save 20%." },
	features: ["Unlimited projects", "Version history", "Priority support"],
}

type Period = "monthly" | "yearly"

export interface PricingCardBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the billing period showing when the trial starts. */
	onStart?: (period: Period) => void
}

export function PricingCardBlock({ className, framed = true, onStart }: PricingCardBlockProps) {
	const [period, setPeriod] = useState<Period>("yearly")
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-5">
				<ToggleGroup
					value={[period]}
					onValueChange={(v: unknown[]) => v[0] && setPeriod(v[0] as Period)}
					aria-label="Billing period"
					className="w-full"
				>
					<Toggle value="monthly" className="flex-1">
						Monthly
					</Toggle>
					<Toggle value="yearly" className="flex-1">
						Yearly
					</Toggle>
				</ToggleGroup>
				<div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
					<div className="flex items-baseline gap-1.5">
						<span className="text-heading-2">{plan[period].price}</span>
						<span className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">per seat / month</span>
					</div>
					<span className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{plan[period].note}</span>
				</div>
				<ul className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-body-sm">
					{plan.features.map((feature) => (
						<li key={feature} className="flex items-center gap-2">
							<Icon name="check" className="text-success" />
							{feature}
						</li>
					))}
				</ul>
				<Button className="w-full" onClick={() => onStart?.(period)}>
					Start free trial
				</Button>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# PricingTableBlock

A three-tier pricing section: heading, a Monthly/Yearly ToggleGroup, and three equal-height plan cards with the recommended one outlined in primary and badged "Most popular".

**Intent:** Reach for this on a pricing page or the pricing band of a landing page, to compare plans side by side. A single plan on offer (an upgrade prompt, a paywall) is PricingCardBlock.

**Block:** Commerce · section

## Notes

- One featured tier at most: it takes the primary button and a primary outline; the others take outline buttons so the recommendation is unmistakable.
- Cards stretch to the tallest one and push their buttons to the bottom, so the calls to action line up across the row.
- The yearly saving is stated in the toggle itself, where the choice is made. `onChoose` receives the tier id and the period showing.

## Accessibility

- Each plan is an <article> with an h3 under the section's h2, so the tiers are navigable by heading.
- The ToggleGroup is labelled "Billing period"; prices update in place and stay in the reading order of each card.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState, useId } from "react"
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Grid, Icon, Region, Stack, Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@sableui/react"

const tiers = [
	{
		id: "starter",
		name: "Starter",
		blurb: "For one person shipping their first editions.",
		monthly: 0,
		yearly: 0,
		cta: "Start for free",
		featured: false,
		features: ["3 live editions", "Collector profiles", "Community support"],
	},
	{
		id: "studio",
		name: "Studio",
		blurb: "For working artists with a steady release schedule.",
		monthly: 20,
		yearly: 16,
		cta: "Start free trial",
		featured: true,
		features: ["Unlimited editions", "Scheduled drops", "Sales analytics", "Priority support"],
	},
	{
		id: "collective",
		name: "Collective",
		blurb: "For galleries and teams releasing together.",
		monthly: 48,
		yearly: 40,
		cta: "Talk to sales",
		featured: false,
		features: ["Everything in Studio", "Up to 10 seats", "Shared payouts", "Roles and approvals"],
	},
]

type Period = "monthly" | "yearly"

export interface PricingTableBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** Called with the chosen tier and the billing period showing. */
	onChoose?: (tier: string, period: Period) => void
}

export function PricingTableBlock({ className, onChoose }: PricingTableBlockProps) {
	const [period, setPeriod] = useState<Period>("yearly")
	const titleId = useId()
	return (
		<Region as="section" aria-labelledby={titleId} max="wide" className={cn("w-full py-16", className)}>
			<Stack gap={10}>
				<Stack gap={4} align="center" className="text-center">
					<h2 id={titleId} className="text-balance text-heading-1">
						Pricing that grows with your practice
					</h2>
					<p className="max-w-(--measure-prose) text-body-lg text-muted-foreground">
						Every plan includes unlimited collectors and no fees on your first $1,000 in sales.
					</p>
					<ToggleGroup value={[period]} onValueChange={(v: unknown[]) => v[0] && setPeriod(v[0] as Period)} aria-label="Billing period">
						<Toggle value="monthly">Monthly</Toggle>
						<Toggle value="yearly">Yearly · save 20%</Toggle>
					</ToggleGroup>
				</Stack>
				<Grid cols={{ base: 1, md: 3 }} gap={4} className="items-stretch">
					{tiers.map((tier) => (
						<Card
							key={tier.id}
							render={<article />}
							className={cn("flex flex-col", tier.featured && "border-primary ring-1 ring-primary")}
						>
							<CardHeader>
								<CardTitle render={<h3 />}>{tier.name}</CardTitle>
								<CardDescription>{tier.blurb}</CardDescription>
								{tier.featured ? (
									<CardAction>
										<Badge tone="edition" size="sm">
											Most popular
										</Badge>
									</CardAction>
								) : null}
							</CardHeader>
							<CardContent className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-5">
								<div className="flex items-baseline gap-1.5">
									<span className="text-heading-2">${tier[period]}</span>
									<span className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">per seat / month</span>
								</div>
								<ul className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-body-sm">
									{tier.features.map((feature) => (
										<li key={feature} className="flex items-center gap-2">
											<Icon name="check" className="text-success" />
											{feature}
										</li>
									))}
								</ul>
							</CardContent>
							<CardFooter>
								<Button className="w-full" variant={tier.featured ? "primary" : "outline"} onClick={() => onChoose?.(tier.id, period)}>
									{tier.cta}
								</Button>
							</CardFooter>
						</Card>
					))}
				</Grid>
			</Stack>
		</Region>
	)
}
```
