# ProductCardBlock

A product card: edge-to-edge artwork, title and maker, an edition Badge, and the price beside a single buy action.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a product, edition or listing in a grid or a featured slot. For a row in a dense list, use an Entity with the image as `leading` instead.

**Block:** Commerce · card · designed for 16rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The artwork runs to the card's edges; the card clips it to its own corners (overflow-hidden).
- Prices are `text-mono-lg` — the metric mono tier with tabular figures — never a heading tier.
- The placeholder art is painted from the palette's decorative tones so it follows the theme; swap it for the product image with real alt text.

## Accessibility

- The placeholder art is aria-hidden. A real product image needs alt text naming the product.
- The card is not a link: it holds its own button. To make the whole card navigate, move the action to the detail page and render the Card as an <a>.

## Source

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, MediaImage } from "@sableui/react"

// `image` is the product shot URL; left empty, it paints art seeded by the title.
const product = { title: "Untitled (gold rush)", maker: "Mara Okafor", image: "", edition: "12 of 50", price: "0.42 SOL" }


export interface ProductCardBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** The buy action. */
	onCollect?: () => void
}

export function ProductCardBlock({ className, framed = true, onCollect }: ProductCardBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs overflow-hidden", className)}>
			<AspectBox ratio={4 / 3}>
				<MediaImage src={product.image} seed={product.title} />
			</AspectBox>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>{product.title}</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>{product.maker}</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Badge tone="edition">{product.edition}</Badge>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardFooter className="justify-between pt-4">
				<span className="text-mono-lg">{product.price}</span>
				<Button onClick={onCollect}>Collect</Button>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# ProfileCardBlock

A profile card: a cover banner, an avatar rising into it, Share and Follow, the name and handle, a one-line bio and two counts.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a person or creator summary — a suggested-follow card, a hover target's full view, the top of a profile sidebar. For a small inline preview on hover, use ContextCard; for a row in a list of people, use Entity.

**Block:** Social & messaging · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The avatar overlaps the banner by half its height with a ring in the card colour, so it reads as sitting on the card, not pasted over the art.
- Follow is the one primary action and flips to a secondary Following once pressed; Share is an icon-only ghost Button beside it.
- Counts pair a label-tier number with muted body text, so the numbers scan as a row.

## Accessibility

- The Share button carries aria-label; Follow's visible text changes with its state.
- The banner is decorative (aria-hidden); the Avatar's alt is the person's name.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Avatar, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardTitle, cn, GradientArt, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

const profile = {
	name: "Juno Avery",
	initials: "JA",
	handle: "@juno · Sound and light",
	bio: "Field recordings, slowed down. New edition every full moon.",
	stats: [
		{ value: "128", label: "posts" },
		{ value: "4.2k", label: "followers" },
	],
}


export interface ProfileCardBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the new follow state. */
	onFollowChange?: (following: boolean) => void
	onShare?: () => void
}

export function ProfileCardBlock({ className, framed = true, onFollowChange, onShare }: ProfileCardBlockProps) {
	const [following, setFollowing] = useState(false)
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs overflow-hidden", className)}>
			{/* Placeholder banner painted from the theme, so it follows every look. Replace with the person's cover image. */}
			<GradientArt aria-hidden seed={profile.handle} className="h-20" />
			{/* pt-0: the avatar rises into the banner above, so the content
			    starts at the banner's edge rather than a full pad below it. */}
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3 pt-0">
				<div className="flex items-start justify-between">
					<Avatar variant="art" size="lg" fallback={profile.initials} alt={profile.name} className="-mt-6 ring-4 ring-card" />
					<div className="flex gap-1.5 pt-3">
						<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Share profile" onClick={onShare}>
							<Icon name="share" />
						</Button>
						<Button
							size="sm"
							variant={following ? "secondary" : "primary"}
							onClick={() => {
								setFollowing(!following)
								onFollowChange?.(!following)
							}}
						>
							{following ? "Following" : "Follow"}
						</Button>
					</div>
				</div>
				<div className="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
					<CardTitle>{profile.name}</CardTitle>
					<CardDescription>{profile.handle}</CardDescription>
				</div>
				<p className="text-body-sm">{profile.bio}</p>
				<div className="flex gap-4 text-body-sm">
					{profile.stats.map((s) => (
						<span key={s.label}>
							<span className="text-label-lg">{s.value}</span> <span className="text-muted-foreground">{s.label}</span>
						</span>
					))}
				</div>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# ProfileFormBlock

A profile settings card: avatar with upload/remove, name and handle side by side, a bio, a timezone Select, and one Save profile in the footer.

**Intent:** Reach for this for the profile or account section of settings, or any form of drafted text that is committed together. Toggles that apply instantly belong in NotificationSettingsBlock, never behind this Save.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 20rem–42rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Copied from the SettingsPage page shell's Profile section; the shell keeps its own copy so it stays one self-contained file.
- One explicit save for the whole card. Short pairs (name + handle) sit side by side from sm up with Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }}.
- The CardTitle renders an h2, so the section joins the page outline under its h1.

## Accessibility

- Field wires label, description and error to each control; the handle's URL preview is its description.
- The photo actions are type="button", so neither one submits the form.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Field, Form, Grid, Input, Row, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, Stack, Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

const profile = {
	name: "Ada Lovelace",
	initials: "AL",
	handle: "ada",
	bio: "Generative artist working in plotted ink and code. New editions of 25 to 100 every month.",
	timezone: "europe-london",
}

const timezones = [
	{ value: "europe-london", label: "London (GMT+1)" },
	{ value: "europe-paris", label: "Paris (GMT+2)" },
	{ value: "america-new-york", label: "New York (GMT−4)" },
	{ value: "america-los-angeles", label: "Los Angeles (GMT−7)" },
	{ value: "asia-tokyo", label: "Tokyo (GMT+9)" },
]

export interface ProfileFormBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the form's fields on Save profile. */
	onSave?: (fields: FormData) => void
}

export function ProfileFormBlock({ className, framed = true, onSave }: ProfileFormBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-2xl", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Profile</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>How collectors see you.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			{/* The one explicit save: profile text is drafted, then committed. */}
			<Form
				className="gap-0"
				onSubmit={(event) => {
					event.preventDefault()
					onSave?.(new FormData(event.currentTarget))
				}}
			>
				<CardContent>
					<Stack gap={3}>
						<Row gap={2}>
							<Avatar variant="art" size="lg" fallback={profile.initials} alt={profile.name} />
							<Stack gap={0.5} align="start">
								<Row gap={1}>
									<Button type="button" variant="outline" size="sm">
										Upload photo
									</Button>
									<Button type="button" variant="ghost" size="sm">
										Remove
									</Button>
								</Row>
								<p className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">Square PNG or JPG, at least 400 px.</p>
							</Stack>
						</Row>
						<Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }} gap={3}>
							<Field label="Display name" name="displayName" required>
								<Input defaultValue={profile.name} autoComplete="name" />
							</Field>
							<Field label="Handle" name="handle" description={`atelier.com/@${profile.handle}`} required>
								<Input defaultValue={profile.handle} autoComplete="username" spellCheck={false} />
							</Field>
						</Grid>
						<Field label="Bio" name="bio" description="Shown on your profile and edition pages.">
							<Textarea rows={3} defaultValue={profile.bio} />
						</Field>
						<Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }} gap={3}>
							<Field label="Timezone" name="timezone" description="Release times use this zone.">
								<Select defaultValue={profile.timezone} items={timezones}>
									<SelectTrigger />
									<SelectContent>
										{timezones.map((zone) => (
											<SelectItem key={zone.value} value={zone.value}>
												{zone.label}
											</SelectItem>
										))}
									</SelectContent>
								</Select>
							</Field>
						</Grid>
					</Stack>
				</CardContent>
				<CardFooter actions className="justify-end">
					<Button type="submit">Save profile</Button>
				</CardFooter>
			</Form>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# RevenueBreakdownBlock

A stat card with a breakdown: the KPI in the metric mono tier, its trend Badge, a SegmentedBar of how the total divides, and a StatusDot legend.

**Intent:** Reach for this when a headline number is worth splitting into a few categories — revenue by product, storage by type, tickets by priority. A plain KPI with no split is a smaller stat card (see DashboardPage's stat row).

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The value is `text-mono-xl` — tabular figures, never a heading tier — and the label above it is CardDescription.
- The legend reflows from two columns to one by measuring in em, so larger type or a narrower card never truncates a label.
- Each category keeps the same tone in the bar and its legend dot; reuse those tones wherever the category appears.

## Accessibility

- The SegmentedBar is one image whose name reads every share; the legend repeats it visually and is aria-hidden so it is not announced twice.
- The trend Badge states the change as text (+8.2%), not by colour.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, cn, Grid, SegmentedBar, StatusDot } from "@sableui/react"

const revenue = { label: "Revenue this month", total: "$12,480", change: "+8.2%" }

const segments = [
	{ label: "Editions", value: 42, tone: "edition" },
	{ label: "Collectibles", value: 27, tone: "collectible" },
	{ label: "Standard", value: 19, tone: "standard" },
	{ label: "Commissions", value: 12, tone: "info" },
] as const

export interface RevenueBreakdownBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function RevenueBreakdownBlock({ className, framed = true }: RevenueBreakdownBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardDescription>{revenue.label}</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Badge tone="success" size="sm">
						{revenue.change}
					</Badge>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-4 pt-2">
				<span className="text-mono-xl">{revenue.total}</span>
				<SegmentedBar label="Revenue by type" segments={[...segments]} size="lg" />
				{/* Two columns while each entry fits whole, one when they would not:
				    sized in em, so a larger type or a narrower card drops to one.
				    aria-hidden: the bar already reads every share aloud. */}
				<Grid aria-hidden minItemWidth="9.5em" gap="calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5) calc(var(--spacing) * 4)">
					{segments.map((s) => (
						<div key={s.label} className="flex items-center gap-2 text-body-sm">
							<StatusDot tone={s.tone} />
							<span className="flex-1 text-muted-foreground">{s.label}</span>
							<span className="text-mono-caption">{s.value}%</span>
						</div>
					))}
				</Grid>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# SignInBlock

A sign-in card: email and password, a primary Sign in, and a passkey alternative under an "or" separator.

**Intent:** Reach for this wherever someone signs in inside a surface you already have — a Sheet, a Dialog, a gated panel. For a whole sign-in route with brand art beside the form, start from the AuthPage page shell instead.

**Block:** Auth · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- One primary action. The passkey is an outline Button under a labelled Separator, so it reads as an alternative, not a second submit.
- The fields are a real <form>: Enter submits, and the browser's password manager recognises the autocomplete hints.
- framed={false} keeps the padding and drops the surface, for a Sheet or Dialog that is already the frame.

## Accessibility

- Inputs carry aria-label because the design shows placeholders, not visible labels; add Field labels if your brief wants them visible.
- `onSignIn` receives "password" or "passkey", so focus and error handling stay with the caller's auth flow.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Icon, Input, Separator } from "@sableui/react"

export interface SignInBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet, Dialog or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the method the person chose. Wire your auth here. */
	onSignIn?: (method: "password" | "passkey") => void
}

export function SignInBlock({ className, framed = true, onSignIn }: SignInBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>Welcome back</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Sign in to pick up where you left off.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<form
					className="flex flex-col gap-4"
					onSubmit={(event) => {
						event.preventDefault()
						onSignIn?.("password")
					}}
				>
					<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
						<Input name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" placeholder="you@studio.com" aria-label="Email" />
						<Input name="password" type="password" autoComplete="current-password" placeholder="Password" aria-label="Password" />
					</div>
					<Button type="submit" className="w-full">
						Sign in
					</Button>
					<Separator label="or" />
					<Button variant="outline" className="w-full" iconStart={<Icon name="lock" />} onClick={() => onSignIn?.("passkey")}>
						Use a passkey
					</Button>
				</form>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# SignUpBlock

A sign-up card: name, work email and password as labelled Fields, one full-width Create account, and a link to sign in instead.

**Intent:** Reach for this to create an account inside a surface you already have, or as the form of a sign-up route. For the whole route with brand art beside it, start from the AuthPage page shell and drop this card in.

**Block:** Auth · card · designed for 18rem–24rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Visible labels, not placeholders: someone filling a new form needs to see what each field is after typing in it.
- The password rule is stated up front in the Field description, before anyone fails it.
- `onSignUp` receives the fields only after the browser's own validation (required, type=email, minLength) passes.

## Accessibility

- Field wires each label, description and error to its input; never hand-roll <label> + <input> pairs.
- autoComplete hints (name, email, new-password) let password managers offer to generate and save the password.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

export interface SignUpBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet, Dialog or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the submitted fields once the browser's validation passes. */
	onSignUp?: (account: { name: string; email: string; password: string }) => void
}

export function SignUpBlock({ className, framed = true, onSignUp }: SignUpBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-sm", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>Create your account</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Free for 14 days. No card needed.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<Form
				className="gap-0"
				onSubmit={(event) => {
					event.preventDefault()
					const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget)
					onSignUp?.({
						name: String(data.get("name") ?? ""),
						email: String(data.get("email") ?? ""),
						password: String(data.get("password") ?? ""),
					})
				}}
			>
				<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">
					<Field label="Name" name="name" required>
						<Input autoComplete="name" />
					</Field>
					<Field label="Work email" name="email" required>
						<Input type="email" autoComplete="email" placeholder="you@studio.com" />
					</Field>
					<Field label="Password" name="password" description="At least 12 characters." required>
						<Input type="password" autoComplete="new-password" minLength={12} />
					</Field>
				</CardContent>
				<CardFooter className="flex-col items-stretch gap-3">
					<Button type="submit" className="w-full">
						Create account
					</Button>
					<p className="text-center text-caption text-muted-foreground">
						Already have an account?{" "}
						<a href="/sign-in" className="text-foreground underline underline-offset-4 motion-interactive hover:text-muted-foreground">
							Sign in
						</a>
					</p>
				</CardFooter>
			</Form>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# SiteFooterBlock

A site footer: the brand and a one-line tagline beside link groups in a labelled Footer nav, over a copyright line.

**Intent:** Reach for this at the foot of a marketing or docs site. App screens inside an AppShell take no footer; their navigation lives in the sidebar.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Copied from the LandingPage page shell's footer.
- Every link is at least 36px tall (min-h-9), so the dense list is still an easy touch target.
- Groups go two up on a phone and three up from sm; add a group only if it has three links or more.

## Accessibility

- Renders <footer> with a <nav aria-label="Footer">, distinct from the page's main navigation.
- Group titles are h2s, so the footer's structure is navigable by heading.

## Source

```tsx
import { cn, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const brand = { name: "Sable", tagline: "React components, patterns, and tokens for products built with AI agents." }

const groups = [
	{
		title: "Product",
		links: [
			{ label: "Components", href: "/components" },
			{ label: "Patterns", href: "/patterns" },
			{ label: "Themes", href: "/themes" },
			{ label: "Canvas", href: "/canvas" },
		],
	},
	{
		title: "Resources",
		links: [
			{ label: "Documentation", href: "/docs" },
			{ label: "Changelog", href: "/changelog" },
			{ label: "llms.txt", href: "/llms.txt" },
		],
	},
	{
		title: "Community",
		links: [
			{ label: "GitHub", href: "/github" },
			{ label: "npm", href: "/npm" },
			{ label: "Discussions", href: "/discussions" },
		],
	},
]

export interface SiteFooterBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function SiteFooterBlock({ className }: SiteFooterBlockProps) {
	return (
		<footer className={cn("w-full border-t border-border", className)}>
			<Region max="wide" className="py-12">
				<div className="grid gap-10 md:grid-cols-[minmax(0,2fr)_minmax(0,3fr)]">
					<Stack gap={3} className="max-w-xs">
						<a href="/" className="w-fit text-title-lg motion-interactive hover:text-muted-foreground">
							{brand.name}
						</a>
						<p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{brand.tagline}</p>
					</Stack>
					<nav aria-label="Footer" className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-8 sm:grid-cols-3">
						{groups.map((group) => (
							<div key={group.title}>
								<h2 className="text-label-md text-muted-foreground">{group.title}</h2>
								<ul className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-1">
									{group.links.map((link) => (
										<li key={link.label}>
											<a href={link.href} className="flex min-h-9 items-center text-body-sm motion-interactive hover:text-muted-foreground">
												{link.label}
											</a>
										</li>
									))}
								</ul>
							</div>
						))}
					</nav>
				</div>
				<div className="mt-12 border-t border-border pt-6">
					<p className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">
						© 2026 {brand.name}. Released under the MIT license.
					</p>
				</div>
			</Region>
		</footer>
	)
}
```

# StatRowBlock

A KPI row: four stat cards, each a label, the value in the metric mono tier, and a trend Badge with its comparison note — 2 × 2 on a phone, one row from xl.

**Intent:** Reach for this at the top of a dashboard or report, above the tables and charts it summarises. One headline number worth splitting into categories is RevenueBreakdownBlock.

**Block:** Dashboard · section

## Notes

- Copied from the DashboardPage page shell's stat row.
- Values are `text-mono-xl` — tabular figures, never a heading tier — so the four numbers align digit for digit.
- The trend Badge sits with its note in CardContent, so the value keeps the full card width when the row folds to 2 × 2.
- Keep it to four. A fifth stat is a sign one of them belongs in a table.

## Accessibility

- The trend is stated in text (+8.2%) with an arrow icon; the tone is reinforcement, not the signal.
- Each card's label is read before its value, in source order.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Grid, Icon, Row } from "@sableui/react"

const stats = [
	{ label: "Revenue", value: "$18,240", delta: "+8.2%", up: true, note: "vs. $16,857" },
	{ label: "Collects", value: "1,284", delta: "+3.1%", up: true, note: "182 first-time" },
	{ label: "Collectors", value: "312", delta: "+12.4%", up: true, note: "Best month yet" },
	{ label: "Sell-through", value: "64%", delta: "−1.8%", up: false, note: "6 open editions" },
]

export interface StatRowBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function StatRowBlock({ className }: StatRowBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Grid cols={{ base: 2, xl: 4 }} gap={3} className={cn("w-full", className)}>
			{stats.map((stat) => (
				<Card key={stat.label}>
					<CardHeader>
						<CardDescription>{stat.label}</CardDescription>
						<CardTitle className="text-mono-xl">{stat.value}</CardTitle>
					</CardHeader>
					<CardContent>
						<Row gap={1} wrap>
							<Badge tone={stat.up ? "success" : "warning"} size="sm" icon={<Icon name={stat.up ? "arrow-up" : "arrow-down"} />}>
								{stat.delta}
							</Badge>
							<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">{stat.note}</span>
						</Row>
					</CardContent>
				</Card>
			))}
		</Grid>
	)
}
```

# StepsBlock

A how-it-works section: the heading, lede and a guide link on the left; three numbered steps on the right, each under a strong rule.

**Intent:** Reach for this when the pitch is a sequence — onboarding, a workflow, a setup. Parallel benefits with no order are FeatureGridBlock; progress through a live process is a Stepper.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Copied from the BrandLandingPage page shell's how-it-works section.
- The steps are an <ol>, so the order is semantic and the 01 / 02 / 03 numbers are its visual echo, set in the mono tier.
- Three steps fit the 1 : 2 split on desktop; on a phone everything stacks with the intro first.

## Accessibility

- Each step has an h3 under the section's h2.
- The guide link is an <a> styled as an outline Button, because it navigates.

## Source

```tsx
import { useId } from "react"
import { Button, cn, Icon, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const intro = {
	eyebrow: "How it works",
	title: "From request to sealed record.",
	lede: "Teams are usually live within a week. Cove adapts to the routes you already run instead of asking you to start over.",
	link: { label: "Read the rollout guide", href: "/guides/rollout" },
}

const steps = [
	{ title: "Connect your spaces", body: "Bring teams, vendors, and record stores into one workspace, with roles that mirror how you already work." },
	{ title: "Route every approval", body: "Requests follow the path you define, with reviewers, deadlines, and escalation built in from the start." },
	{ title: "Seal the record", body: "Approved work is archived with its full context and is ready for review the moment it closes." },
]

export interface StepsBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function StepsBlock({ className }: StepsBlockProps) {
	const titleId = useId()
	return (
		<Region as="section" aria-labelledby={titleId} max="wide" className={cn("w-full py-16 sm:py-24", className)}>
			<div className="grid gap-12 lg:grid-cols-[1fr_2fr] lg:gap-16">
				<Stack gap={2} className="max-w-md">
					<p className="text-overline text-muted-foreground">{intro.eyebrow}</p>
					<h2 id={titleId} className="text-balance text-heading-1">
						{intro.title}
					</h2>
					<p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">{intro.lede}</p>
					<div className="pt-3">
						<Button variant="outline" iconEnd={<Icon name="arrow-right" />} render={<a href={intro.link.href} />}>
							{intro.link.label}
						</Button>
					</div>
				</Stack>
				<ol className="grid gap-10 sm:grid-cols-3 sm:gap-6">
					{steps.map((step, index) => (
						<li key={step.title} className="flex flex-col gap-2 border-t border-border-strong pt-6">
							<span className="text-mono-sm text-muted-foreground">{String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0")}</span>
							<h3 className="mt-3 text-title-lg sm:mt-6">{step.title}</h3>
							<p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{step.body}</p>
						</li>
					))}
				</ol>
			</div>
		</Region>
	)
}
```

# TaskListBlock

A checklist card: a titled list of Checkbox rows with a category Badge each, a live count of what is left, and a quiet Add task action.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a short, personal to-do list on a dashboard or in onboarding. A team's task board with assignees and status columns needs a Table or DataTable.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Finishing a task strikes it through and mutes it rather than removing it, so the list does not jump under the pointer.
- The count in CardAction updates with every check, so progress reads without counting rows.
- Add task is a ghost Button in the footer — present, but quieter than the list.

## Accessibility

- Every Checkbox has a real <Label htmlFor>, so the whole title is the click target and the accessible name.
- Category Badges carry text; the tone only groups them visually.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState, useId } from "react"
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, Checkbox, cn, Icon, Label } from "@sableui/react"

const tasks = [
	{ title: "Pick the cover type", tag: "Design", tone: "collectible", done: true },
	{ title: "Wire up checkout", tag: "Engineering", tone: "info", done: false },
	{ title: "Draft launch post", tag: "Launch", tone: "edition", done: false },
] as const

export interface TaskListBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	onAddTask?: () => void
}

export function TaskListBlock({ className, framed = true, onAddTask }: TaskListBlockProps) {
	const [done, setDone] = useState<boolean[]>(tasks.map((t) => t.done))
	const id = useId()
	const left = done.filter((d) => !d).length
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>This week</CardTitle>
				<CardAction>
					<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">{left} left</span>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<ul className="flex flex-col gap-1">
					{tasks.map((task, i) => (
						<li key={task.title} className="flex items-center gap-3 py-1.5">
							<Checkbox
								id={`${id}-${i}`}
								checked={done[i]}
								onCheckedChange={(v: boolean) => setDone(done.map((d, j) => (j === i ? v : d)))}
							/>
							<Label
								htmlFor={`${id}-${i}`}
								className={cn("min-w-0 flex-1 motion-interactive", done[i] && "text-muted-foreground line-through")}
							>
								{task.title}
							</Label>
							<Badge tone={task.tone} size="sm">
								{task.tag}
							</Badge>
						</li>
					))}
				</ul>
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter>
				<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" bleed="start" iconStart={<Icon name="plus" />} onClick={onAddTask}>
					Add task
				</Button>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# TeamMembersBlock

A members card: Entity rows with avatar, name and email, a role Badge, and an OverflowMenu of role changes and removal; pending invites sit in the same list.

**Intent:** Reach for this to manage who is in a workspace, project or team. For inviting people when the list is empty or short, InviteTeamBlock is the lighter shape; for hundreds of members with filters, use a DataTable.

**Block:** Settings & team · card · designed for 20rem–42rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Each row's menu offers only what applies to it: Make admin or Make member, Resend invite for pending rows, then the destructive action after a separator.
- The owner has no menu — ownership is transferred elsewhere — and a control-sized spacer keeps the role badges aligned.
- Pending invites are outline Badges in the same list, so the team's full size reads in one place.

## Accessibility

- Each OverflowMenu is labelled with the member's name ("Manage Mara Okafor"), so the triggers are distinguishable in a list.
- Roles are text in a Badge; tone only distinguishes the owner.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, cn, Entity, Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

const members = [
	{ id: "u1", name: "Ada Lovelace", initials: "AL", email: "ada@studio.com", role: "Owner" },
	{ id: "u2", name: "Mara Okafor", initials: "MO", email: "mara@studio.com", role: "Admin" },
	{ id: "u3", name: "Sam Rivera", initials: "SR", email: "sam@studio.com", role: "Member" },
	{ id: "u4", name: "jun@studio.com", initials: "J", email: "Invited 2 days ago", role: "Pending" },
]

export interface TeamMembersBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	onInvite?: () => void
	/** Called with the member's id and the action chosen from their menu. */
	onMemberAction?: (id: string, action: "make-admin" | "make-member" | "resend" | "remove") => void
}

export function TeamMembersBlock({ className, framed = true, onInvite, onMemberAction }: TeamMembersBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-2xl", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Members</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>{members.length} people in this workspace.</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Button size="sm" iconStart={<Icon name="plus" />} onClick={onInvite}>
						Invite
					</Button>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardList>
				{members.map((m) => (
					<Entity
						key={m.id}
						leading={<Avatar variant="art" size="sm" fallback={m.initials} alt={m.name} />}
						title={m.name}
						subtitle={m.email}
						action={
							<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
								<Badge appearance={m.role === "Pending" ? "outline" : "plain"} tone={m.role === "Owner" ? "edition" : "neutral"} size="sm">
									{m.role}
								</Badge>
								{/* The owner is not managed from here; a placeholder keeps the column aligned. */}
								{m.role === "Owner" ? (
									<span aria-hidden className="size-(--control-sm)" />
								) : (
									<OverflowMenu label={`Manage ${m.name}`} size="icon-sm">
										{m.role === "Pending" ? (
											<MenuItem onClick={() => onMemberAction?.(m.id, "resend")}>Resend invite</MenuItem>
										) : m.role === "Admin" ? (
											<MenuItem onClick={() => onMemberAction?.(m.id, "make-member")}>Make member</MenuItem>
										) : (
											<MenuItem onClick={() => onMemberAction?.(m.id, "make-admin")}>Make admin</MenuItem>
										)}
										<MenuSeparator />
										<MenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => onMemberAction?.(m.id, "remove")}>
											{m.role === "Pending" ? "Cancel invite" : "Remove from workspace"}
										</MenuItem>
									</OverflowMenu>
								)}
							</div>
						}
					/>
				))}
			</CardList>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# TestimonialBlock

A customer story: one large blockquote with the person's avatar, name and role, beside three outcome figures separated by rules.

**Intent:** Reach for this for one strong, attributable quote backed by numbers. A wall of short quotes is a different section; a logo row is Marquee.

**Block:** Marketing · section

## Notes

- Copied from the BrandLandingPage page shell's customer story.
- The quote and the outcomes share one Card as a <figure>; the outcomes move under the quote below lg.
- Outcome values use display sizes because they are the proof; their labels say what each number counts.

## Accessibility

- <figure> + <blockquote> + <figcaption> tie the quote to the person who said it.
- The section is labelled "Customer story" so it is reachable as a landmark.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Card, CardContent, cn, Region, Separator, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const story = {
	quote: "We used to chase approvals across four tools. Now every request has an owner, a deadline, and a record, and our auditors stopped asking for screenshots.",
	name: "Maya Okafor",
	initials: "MO",
	role: "Head of operations, Fielddesk",
}

const outcomes = [
	{ value: "3.2×", label: "faster approvals in the first quarter" },
	{ value: "68%", label: "fewer follow-ups on handoffs" },
	{ value: "1 day", label: "to prepare a quarterly audit" },
]

export interface TestimonialBlockProps {
	className?: string
}

export function TestimonialBlock({ className }: TestimonialBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Region as="section" aria-label="Customer story" max="wide" className={cn("w-full py-16", className)}>
			<Card render={<figure />}>
				<div className="grid lg:grid-cols-[1.5fr_1fr]">
					<CardContent className="flex flex-col justify-between gap-10 sm:p-10">
						<Stack gap={3}>
							<p className="text-overline text-muted-foreground">Customer story</p>
							<blockquote className="text-balance text-heading-3 sm:text-heading-2">“{story.quote}”</blockquote>
						</Stack>
						<figcaption className="flex items-center gap-3">
							<Avatar variant="art" size="lg" fallback={story.initials} alt={story.name} />
							<div>
								<p className="text-title-sm">{story.name}</p>
								<p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{story.role}</p>
							</div>
						</figcaption>
					</CardContent>
					<div className="border-border max-lg:border-t lg:border-s">
						<CardContent className="flex h-full flex-col justify-center gap-6 sm:p-10">
							{outcomes.map((outcome, index) => (
								<Stack key={outcome.label} gap={3}>
									{index > 0 && <Separator />}
									<div>
										<p className="text-heading-1 sm:text-display-lg">{outcome.value}</p>
										<p className="mt-1 text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{outcome.label}</p>
									</div>
								</Stack>
							))}
						</CardContent>
					</div>
				</div>
			</Card>
		</Region>
	)
}
```

# TrafficSourcesBlock

A share card: a donut PieChart of where a total comes from, the total in the hole, a legend, and the headline share in words in the footer.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a split of one total into four or fewer parts — traffic sources, revenue by plan, tickets by channel. More parts, or values to compare exactly, belong in a horizontal BarChart.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 18rem–24rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The total sits in the donut's hole, so the card answers "how many" and "from where" at once.
- The footer puts the biggest share in a sentence — the takeaway does not depend on reading the slices.
- The slices sweep in clockwise as the card scrolls into view.

## Accessibility

- The chart's data table lists every source and its count; the legend repeats it visually.
- Hovering or arrowing through the slices pulls each out and announces it.

## Source

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, PieChart } from "@sableui/react"

const sources = [
	{ source: "Search", visitors: 4280 },
	{ source: "Direct", visitors: 2910 },
	{ source: "Social", visitors: 1840 },
	{ source: "Email", visitors: 960 },
]

const total = sources.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.visitors, 0)

export interface TrafficSourcesBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function TrafficSourcesBlock({ className, framed = true }: TrafficSourcesBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-sm", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Traffic sources</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Where this month's visitors came from.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<PieChart
					label="Visitors by source, this month"
					data={sources}
					index="source"
					valueKey="visitors"
					donut
					centerLabel={{ value: total.toLocaleString("en-US"), label: "Visitors" }}
				/>
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">
				Search brings {Math.round((sources[0].visitors / total) * 100)}% of visitors.
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# TrafficTrendBlock

A trend card: a stacked gradient AreaChart of two series by day, a time-range ToggleGroup in the header, and a one-line takeaway with its direction in the footer.

**Intent:** Reach for this as the headline chart of a dashboard or an analytics section on a landing page. For a single number with a small trend beside it, KpiSparklineBlock is lighter.

**Block:** Dashboard · card · designed for 20rem–48rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Switching the range eases the chart from one shape to the next instead of redrawing it.
- The footer states the takeaway in words, so the card says something even before the chart is read.
- The tooltip heading spells out the weekday; the axis keeps short dates so they fit.

## Accessibility

- The chart's accessible name includes the range showing, and its data table updates with it.
- The range control is a labelled ToggleGroup; the chart is one tab stop with arrow-key navigation.

## Source

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { AreaChart, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Icon, Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@sableui/react"

/** 90 days of visitors — replace with your own rows ({ date, desktop, mobile }). */
const days = Array.from({ length: 90 }, (_, i) => {
	const wave = Math.sin(i / 6) * 60 + Math.sin(i / 2.3) * 25
	return {
		date: new Date(2026, 6, 1 + i).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
		desktop: Math.round(240 + wave + (i % 7) * 9),
		mobile: Math.round(160 + wave * 0.7 + ((i * 3) % 11) * 6),
	}
})

const series = [
	{ key: "desktop", label: "Desktop" },
	{ key: "mobile", label: "Mobile" },
]

const ranges = [
	{ id: "90d", label: "3 months", days: 90 },
	{ id: "30d", label: "30 days", days: 30 },
	{ id: "7d", label: "7 days", days: 7 },
]

const shortDate = (iso: string) => new Date(`${iso}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })

export interface TrafficTrendBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
}

export function TrafficTrendBlock({ className, framed = true }: TrafficTrendBlockProps) {
	const [range, setRange] = useState("90d")
	const shown = days.slice(-(ranges.find((r) => r.id === range)?.days ?? 90))
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-3xl", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle render={<h2 />}>Visitors</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Desktop and mobile, by day.</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<ToggleGroup value={[range]} onValueChange={(v: unknown[]) => v[0] && setRange(String(v[0]))} aria-label="Time range">
						{ranges.map((r) => (
							<Toggle key={r.id} value={r.id}>
								{r.label}
							</Toggle>
						))}
					</ToggleGroup>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<AreaChart
					label={`Visitors per day, last ${ranges.find((r) => r.id === range)?.label}`}
					data={shown}
					index="date"
					series={series}
					indexFormatter={shortDate}
					tooltip={{ labelFormatter: (d) => new Date(`${d}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { weekday: "short", month: "short", day: "numeric" }) }}
					stacked
					gradient
					className="h-64"
				/>
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter className="gap-1.5 text-body-sm">
				<Icon name="arrow-up" className="text-success" />
				<span>
					Up 5.2% on the previous period <span className="text-muted-foreground">· desktop leads every week</span>
				</span>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# UploadListBlock

An upload queue: full-width Attachment rows — one uploading with progress and a cancel button, one finished with a success check.

**Intent:** Reach for this under a FileDropzone, or anywhere files are in flight — a composer, an import step, a document form. For files attached to a message, Attachment chips in the composer fit better.

**Block:** Media & files · card · designed for 16rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- Rows, not chips: each Attachment drops its chip cap (`max-w-none`) to fill the block's width.
- The success check sits in a control-sized box so it lines up with the cancel button on the row above.
- No card: Attachment rows are their own surfaces. Wrap the block in a Card if it needs a header.

## Accessibility

- Attachment announces upload progress; the cancel Button carries aria-label.
- The finished row's check carries aria-label="Uploaded", so the state is spoken, not only coloured.

## Source

```tsx
import { Attachment, Button, cn, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

const uploading = { name: "brand-guidelines.pdf", meta: "4.2 MB of 6.8 MB", progress: 62 }
const uploaded = { name: "cover-final.png", meta: "Uploaded · 2.1 MB" }

export interface UploadListBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** Called when the in-progress upload is cancelled. */
	onCancel?: () => void
}

export function UploadListBlock({ className, onCancel }: UploadListBlockProps) {
	return (
		// An upload list, not chips: rows fill the block's width.
		<div className={cn("flex w-full max-w-xs flex-col gap-2", className)}>
			<Attachment
				className="max-w-none"
				name={uploading.name}
				meta={uploading.meta}
				status="uploading"
				progress={uploading.progress}
				actions={
					<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Cancel upload" onClick={onCancel}>
						<Icon name="xmark" />
					</Button>
				}
			/>
			<Attachment
				className="max-w-none"
				name={uploaded.name}
				icon="image-stack"
				meta={uploaded.meta}
				// The same box as the icon-sm button above, so the check centres on
				// the cancel button's line instead of hugging the edge.
				actions={
					<span className="grid size-(--control-sm) place-items-center">
						<Icon name="circle-check" className="text-success" aria-label="Uploaded" />
					</span>
				}
			/>
		</div>
	)
}
```

# VerifyCodeBlock

A one-time-code card: where the code went, a six-slot OtpField grouped 3 + 3 under a visible label, and a quiet Resend.

**Intent:** Reach for this for email or SMS verification, two-factor sign-in, or confirming a sensitive change. For a code someone copies out (a recovery key), show it with Code and a copy button instead.

**Block:** Auth · card · designed for 18rem–24rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- No submit button: the code verifies the moment the last slot fills, which is what people expect from a code field.
- The destination is named in the description, so a mistyped address is caught before the wait.
- Resend is a ghost Button — present for the stuck case, never competing with the field.

## Accessibility

- OtpField names each slot ("Character 1 of 6") and accepts a pasted code into all six at once.
- Field labels the group and reads the expiry as its description.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

const sentTo = "ada@studio.com"

export interface VerifyCodeBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet, Dialog or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	/** Called with the code as soon as the last digit is entered. */
	onVerify?: (code: string) => void
	onResend?: () => void
}

export function VerifyCodeBlock({ className, framed = true, onVerify, onResend }: VerifyCodeBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-sm", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>Check your email</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>
					We sent a 6-digit code to <span className="text-foreground">{sentTo}</span>.
				</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>
				<Field label="Verification code" description="The code expires in 10 minutes.">
					<OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} onValueComplete={(code: string) => onVerify?.(code)} />
				</Field>
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter className="justify-between gap-3">
				<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">Didn’t get it?</span>
				<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" bleed="end" onClick={onResend}>
					Resend code
				</Button>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# WalletBlock

A balance card: the balance in the metric mono tier, Send and Receive as an equal pair, and recent activity as Entity rows with signed amounts.

**Intent:** Reach for this for a wallet, account balance or credits summary with its latest movements. For a full transaction history with filters, use a DataTable.

**Block:** Commerce · card · designed for 18rem–20rem wide (fills its container up to the max)

## Notes

- The balance is CardTitle at `text-mono-xl` — tabular figures, never a heading tier — under its label as CardDescription.
- Send is primary and Receive secondary, side by side at equal width: two directions of one action, with sending the riskier and more frequent.
- Incoming amounts are `text-success`; outgoing stay muted rather than red, because a withdrawal is not an error.

## Accessibility

- Each activity row's leading swatch is aria-hidden; the title and detail carry the meaning.
- Amounts keep their sign in text (+0.80 / -1.50), so the direction does not depend on colour.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Entity, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

const balance = "14.62 SOL"

const activity = [
	{ title: "Sold “Dusk, no. 4”", detail: "Edition · 2h ago", amount: "+0.80", tone: "edition" },
	{ title: "Royalty", detail: "Collectible · Yesterday", amount: "+0.12", tone: "collectible" },
	{ title: "Withdrawal", detail: "To Phantom · Mon", amount: "-1.50", tone: "standard" },
]

export interface WalletBlockProps {
	className?: string
	/** false drops the card's surface and border — for a Sheet or muted section that already frames it. */
	framed?: boolean
	onSend?: () => void
	onReceive?: () => void
}

export function WalletBlock({ className, framed = true, onSend, onReceive }: WalletBlockProps) {
	return (
		<Card variant={framed ? "default" : "flat"} className={cn("w-full max-w-xs", className)}>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardDescription>Balance</CardDescription>
				<CardTitle className="text-mono-xl">{balance}</CardTitle>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">
				<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2">
					<Button iconStart={<Icon name="arrow-up" />} onClick={onSend}>
						Send
					</Button>
					<Button variant="secondary" iconStart={<Icon name="arrow-down" />} onClick={onReceive}>
						Receive
					</Button>
				</div>
				<div className="flex flex-col">
					{activity.map((item) => (
						<Entity
							key={item.title}
							className="px-0"
							leading={
								<span
									aria-hidden
									className="block size-8 rounded-full"
									// design-lint-disable-next-line inline-color -- relative colour derived from the theme's own --tone token, so it follows every look
									style={{ background: `oklch(from var(--tone-${item.tone}) clamp(0.5, calc(l + 0.16), 0.9) max(calc(c * 1.25), 0.1) h)` }}
								/>
							}
							title={item.title}
							subtitle={item.detail}
							action={
								<span className={cn("text-mono-md", item.amount.startsWith("+") ? "text-success" : "text-muted-foreground")}>
									{item.amount}
								</span>
							}
						/>
					))}
				</div>
			</CardContent>
		</Card>
	)
}
```

# Region

**Status:** stable

The page region: fluid, edge-to-edge with the fluid page inset (--page-inset). Opt-in centered max cap picked by ROLE (prose/form/feed/content/wide/full), never a global page max-width. The root of nearly every route.

**Keywords:** region, page width, container, layout

## Usage

Use Region as the page-width primitive that applies fluid page inset and an optional purpose-named max width.

### Best practices

- Do: Choose the max value by content role, such as prose, form, feed, content, wide, or full.
- Do: Use Region near the route or section boundary so inner layout stays intentional.
- Don't: Do not use Region as a global wrapper that forces every page into the same max width.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| as | ElementType | "div" | Semantic element to render (e.g. "main", "section", "nav"). |
| inset | boolean | true | Apply the fluid horizontal page inset (--page-inset). |
| max | "prose" \| "form" \| "feed" \| "content" \| "wide" \| "full" \| CSS length | — | Opt-in centered max-width cap, purpose-named: prose 65ch (long-form reading) · form 480px (auth, narrow single-column forms) · feed 640px (single-column timeline) · content 896px (settings/admin panes) · wide 1280px (dashboards, tables, card grids) · full 1536px (full-bleed ceiling). Omit for fully fluid. |
| bleed | boolean | false | Full-bleed: edge to edge with no inset. Overrides inset. |
| safeArea | boolean \| ("top"\|"bottom"\|"left"\|"right")[] | false | env(safe-area-inset-*) padding for fixed or native-shell surfaces. true pads top+bottom; pass an edge array to target edges. |

## Related

- Components: Page, Grid, Columns

## Examples

### Settings pane

```tsx
import { PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

<Region as="main" max="content"><PageHeader title="Settings" /></Region>
```

### Fluid dashboard region

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid, Region } from "@sableui/react"

<Region max="wide"><Grid minItemWidth="16rem"><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Revenue</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Collects</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Grid></Region>
```

---

# Page

**Status:** stable

A route shell: Region (inset + opt-in max cap) whose children flow as a vertically-rhythmic Stack. Use as the top-level wrapper of a route's content — distinct from AppShell (the frame around routes) and PageHeader (the heading block inside).

**Keywords:** page, route shell, region, stack

## Usage

Use Page as a route content shell that combines Region sizing with vertical rhythm.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it as the top-level wrapper for route content after application chrome.
- Do: Set max by the page's content role rather than by the current viewport.
- Don't: Do not confuse Page with AppShell; Page is content, AppShell is the frame around routes.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 4 | Vertical gap between stacked page sections. Number = rhythm units (×8px, so 4 = 32px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "stretch" | Cross-axis alignment of the stacked sections. |
| …RegionProps | as, inset, max, bleed, safeArea | — | All Region props pass through (Page IS a Region). |

## Related

- Components: Region, Stack, PageHeader, AppShell

## Examples

### Feed route

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, Page, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<Page as="main" max="feed"><PageHeader title="Home" description="Latest posts from artists you follow." /><Card><CardContent><p className="text-body-md">First post.</p></CardContent></Card></Page>
```

# Grid

**Status:** stable

CSS Grid within a region. Two modes: fixed/responsive cols count, or minItemWidth so cells breathe with NO breakpoints (the default choice for card grids). A minItemWidth grid keeps its empty columns (track="fill"), so one result stays one cell wide; track="fit" stretches a fixed set across the row.

**Keywords:** grid, card grid, auto fit, layout

## Usage

Use Grid for uniform grid layouts inside a Region, especially card grids that can breathe responsively.

### Best practices

- Do: Prefer minItemWidth for responsive card grids that do not need breakpoint-specific spans.
- Do: Keep the default track="fill" for collections whose count is data (search results, shelves, galleries): sparse rows keep their empty columns, so one result stays one cell wide.
- Do: Use track="fit" only for a fixed set designed to span the row, such as three KPI cards.
- Do: Use explicit columns only when the design truly needs a fixed track count.
- Don't: Do not use Grid to set a page's reading width; use Region or Center.
- Don't: Do not use track="fit" for results or other data-driven collections: with one or two items the empty columns collapse and each item stretches across the row (a single result rendered as a full-width cover).

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cols | number \| { base?, sm?, md?, lg?, xl?, "2xl"? } | 12 | Fixed column count or a mobile-first breakpoint map ({ base: 2, md: 4 }). Ignored when minItemWidth is set. |
| minItemWidth | string | — | Breathing mode: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(minItemWidth, 1fr)) — as many columns of at least minItemWidth as fit, wrapping without breakpoints. e.g. "16rem". |
| track | "fill" \| "fit" | "fill" | What a minItemWidth grid does with columns it has no items for (only visible when fewer items than fit one row). "fill" (auto-fill) keeps them, so items keep their size whatever their count — one search result is one cover wide, not a banner. Use it for collections whose count is data: results, shelves, galleries. "fit" (auto-fit) collapses them and stretches the items to share the row — only for a fixed set designed to span it (three KPI cards, plan tiers). |
| gap | number \| [row, column] \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between cells. Number = rhythm units (×8px); [row, column] = two rhythm counts, for a gallery whose rows want more air than its columns; string = raw CSS. |

## Related

- Components: Region, Columns, Card

## Examples

### Card grid that breathes (no breakpoints)

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid minItemWidth="16rem" gap={3}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Alpha</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Beta</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Gamma</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Grid>
```

### Sparse results keep their size

```tsx
import { Card, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

// One match still renders one cover wide: the empty columns are kept (track="fill", the default).
<Grid minItemWidth="10rem" gap={2}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Night Swim</CardTitle><CardDescription>Album · Undertow</CardDescription></CardHeader></Card></Grid>
```

### A fixed set that spans the row

```tsx
import { Card, CardDescription, CardHeader, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid minItemWidth="12rem" track="fit" gap={2}><Card><CardHeader><CardDescription>Listeners</CardDescription><span className="text-mono-xl">48.2k</span></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardDescription>Streams</CardDescription><span className="text-mono-xl">1.3M</span></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardDescription>Saves</CardDescription><span className="text-mono-xl">9,410</span></CardHeader></Card></Grid>
```

### Responsive fixed columns

```tsx
import { Badge, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid cols={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }}><Badge appearance="plain" tone="standard" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="warning" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="neutral" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="destructive" dot /></Grid>
```

# Columns

**Status:** stable

An explicit N-column track (default 12) for proportioned layouts — pair with Col spans (list-detail, asymmetric editorial layouts). For uniform card grids prefer Grid minItemWidth.

**Keywords:** columns, 12 column, span, layout

## Usage

Use Columns and Col for proportioned layouts that need explicit spans, such as list-detail or asymmetric panes.

### Best practices

- Do: Use breakpoint span maps when the same layout needs to collapse cleanly on smaller screens.
- Do: Use Columns for proportional composition, not for uniform card wrapping.
- Don't: Do not use column spans as a replacement for Region width or text measure.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Columns | yes | The explicit column track container. |
| Col | yes | A child cell with span and optional start placement. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Col | span?: number \| breakpoint map · start?: number \| breakpoint map | A cell in the track: columns to span (default 1) and optional 1-based start column. Both accept breakpoint maps ({ base: 12, lg: 8 }). |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count | number \| breakpoint map | 12 | Columns in the track; a breakpoint map ({ base: 2, md: 6, lg: 12 }) thins the track on small screens. |
| gap | number \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between columns and rows. Number = rhythm units (×8px); string = raw CSS. The column gap is capped so all gaps together never take more than 75% of the track's width — a large gap can't push a narrow screen into horizontal scroll, and at normal desktop widths it renders exactly as given. The row gap is never capped. |

## Related

- Components: Grid, SplitPane, Region

## Examples

### List-detail (8/4)

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Col, Columns } from "@sableui/react"

<Columns count={12}><Col span={{ base: 12, lg: 8 }}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Posts</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Col><Col span={{ base: 12, lg: 4 }}><Card variant="flat"><CardHeader><CardTitle>Filters</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Col></Columns>
```

# Stack

**Status:** stable

Vertical flow on the 8px rhythm — the default container for stacked content. Gap by role: tight within a group (1.5–2), looser between groups (3–4), generous between sections (6+).

**Keywords:** stack, vertical rhythm, layout, spacing

## Usage

Use Stack for vertical flow where child spacing should follow the Sable rhythm scale.

### Best practices

- Do: Use smaller gaps within a group and larger gaps between sections.
- Do: Use Stack instead of ad hoc margins when siblings form a vertical composition.
- Don't: Do not use Stack to create page width or grid structure; pair it with Region, Grid, or Columns.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 2 | Vertical gap. Number = rhythm units (×8px, fractions ok — 2 = 16px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "stretch" | Cross-axis alignment. |
| justify | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between" | "start" | Main-axis distribution. |

## Related

- Components: Row, Page, Fieldset

## Examples

### Form field group

```tsx
import { Field, Input, Stack, Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={2}><Field label="Display name"><Input name="name" /></Field><Field label="Bio"><Textarea name="bio" /></Field></Stack>
```

# Row

**Status:** stable

Horizontal flex flow — inline rows of controls, toolbars, action clusters. Defaults to center-aligned, no wrap.

**Keywords:** row, toolbar, horizontal, layout

## Usage

Use Row for horizontal clusters such as action groups, toolbars, metadata, and inline controls.

### Best practices

- Do: Use wrap when controls may not fit on smaller screens.
- Do: Use justify and align intentionally so clusters scan as one unit.
- Don't: Do not use Row for navigation menus or dense tabular structure.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 2 | Horizontal gap. Number = rhythm units (×8px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "center" | Cross-axis alignment. |
| justify | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between" | "start" | Main-axis distribution. |
| wrap | boolean | false | Allow items to wrap. |

## Related

- Components: Stack, Button, Spacer

## Examples

### Action cluster

```tsx
import { Button, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={2} justify="end"><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button><Button>Save changes</Button></Row>
```

# Spacer

**Status:** stable

Explicit space on the rhythm, or a flexible grow pusher between siblings (e.g. pushing a footer item to the end of a Row).

**Keywords:** spacer, spacing, grow, layout

## Usage

Use Spacer for explicit rhythm space or a flex grow pusher between siblings.

### Best practices

- Do: Use grow inside Row when one side of a cluster should push to the far edge.
- Do: Use fixed size only when the space has semantic rhythm value.
- Don't: Do not use Spacer to patch broad layout problems that should be solved by Stack, Row, Grid, or Region.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | number | 1 | Fixed size in rhythm units (×8px; fractions ok). Ignored when grow. |
| axis | "vertical" \| "horizontal" | "vertical" | Axis the fixed size applies to. |
| grow | boolean | — | Flex-grow to push siblings apart (fills available space). |

## Related

- Components: Row, Stack

## Examples

### Push actions to the end

```tsx
import { Button, Row, Spacer } from "@sableui/react"

<Row><span className="text-title-sm">Members</span><Spacer grow /><Button size="sm">Invite</Button></Row>
```

# Center

Horizontally center a block, optionally capping its width (commonly "prose" for a reading column inside a wider layout).

## Usage

Use Center to center a block and optionally cap its width inside a wider layout.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for reading columns, forms, or compact content inside a broad Region.
- Do: Choose a named max when the content role matches Sable's measure tokens.
- Don't: Do not use Center for full page inset or app chrome; use Region or AppShell.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| max | "prose" \| "form" \| "feed" \| "content" \| "wide" \| CSS length | — | Cap width: a named region token or any raw CSS length. |

# AspectBox

**Status:** stable

Reserves space via aspect-ratio so async media loads with zero layout shift. Wrap images, video, embeds.

**Keywords:** aspect box, aspect ratio, media, layout shift

## Usage

Use AspectBox to reserve stable aspect-ratio space for async media, embeds, and responsive previews.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it around images, video, and embeds that should not shift layout while loading.
- Do: Match the ratio to the expected media or design slot.
- Don't: Do not use AspectBox for content whose height should grow with text or controls.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ratio | number | 16/9 | Width / height ratio (e.g. 1 for square, 4/5 for portrait). |

## Related

- Components: Video, Dialog, Browser

## Examples

### Cover image slot

```tsx
import { AspectBox } from "@sableui/react"
```

# Bleed

**Status:** stable

Escape a width-capped or inset ancestor to span the full CONTENT area (container-query units, so it stops at a fixed Sidebar instead of bleeding under it). Hero bands, profile covers, full-bleed media inside a capped Page.

**Keywords:** bleed, full bleed, media band, layout

## Usage

Use Bleed to let a band or media element escape an inset or width-capped ancestor while staying within the content area.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for hero bands, profile covers, or media that should align beyond a capped page column.
- Do: Keep surrounding content inside Region or Page so the bleed remains intentional.
- Don't: Do not use Bleed to place content under fixed app chrome or sidebars.

## Related

- Components: Page, Region, AspectBox

## Examples

### Full-bleed hero inside a capped page

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Bleed, Page, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<Page max="feed"><Bleed><AspectBox ratio={3}><img src="/cover.jpg" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" /></AspectBox></Bleed><PageHeader title="Profile" /></Page>
```

# SplitPane

**Status:** stable

Responsive two-pane layout: side-by-side at/above a breakpoint, stacked (primary first) below. List-detail, media + metadata.

**Keywords:** split pane, two pane, list detail, responsive

## Usage

Use SplitPane for responsive two-pane layouts where a primary pane and supporting pane stay conceptually linked.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for media-detail, list-detail, or editor-preview workflows.
- Do: Pick a ratio that reflects the actual priority of the panes.
- Don't: Do not use SplitPane for unrelated columns or uniform grids.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| primary | ReactNode | — | The leading / larger pane (e.g. the media column). |
| secondary | ReactNode | — | The trailing / supporting pane (e.g. the detail column). |
| collapseBelow | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" | "lg" | Breakpoint at/above which panes sit side by side. |
| ratio | string | "1/1" | Primary:secondary width ratio as "a/b" fr units (e.g. "2/1"). |
| gap | number \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between panes. |

## Related

- Components: Columns, Grid, Sheet

## Examples

### Media + detail

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Button, SplitPane, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<SplitPane ratio="2/1" primary={<AspectBox ratio={1}><img src={post.imageUrl} alt={post.title} className="size-full object-cover" /></AspectBox>} secondary={<Stack gap={2}><h1 className="text-heading-1">{post.title}</h1><p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">{post.description}</p><Button>Collect</Button></Stack>} />
```

# SafeArea

**Status:** stable

Pads for device safe-areas (notch, home indicator) on fixed or native-shell surfaces. Wrap fixed bars; content in normal flow rarely needs it.

**Keywords:** safe area, notch, home indicator, fixed chrome

## Usage

Use SafeArea to pad fixed or native-shell surfaces away from device notches and home indicators.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it around fixed headers, bottom bars, and native-shell surfaces.
- Do: Target only the edges that need device inset padding when possible.
- Don't: Do not wrap normal document-flow content in SafeArea unless it actually touches unsafe edges.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| edges | ("top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right")[] | all four | Which edges get env(safe-area-inset-*) padding. |

## Related

- Components: BottomNav, AppHeader, AppShell

## Examples

### Fixed bottom bar

```tsx
import { Button, Row, SafeArea } from "@sableui/react"

<SafeArea edges={["bottom"]} className="fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 bg-card border-t border-border"><Row gap={2} justify="between" className="p-3"><span className="text-label-md">1 item selected</span><Button size="sm">Continue</Button></Row></SafeArea>
```

# Accordion

**Status:** stable

Stacked, collapsible disclosure sections over Base UI Accordion — roving focus, arrow-key navigation, ARIA region/heading/button wiring, and an animated height transition. Each item pairs a full-width trigger (with a rotating chevron) and a panel.

**Keywords:** accordion, disclosure, collapse, faq

## Usage

Use Accordion to reveal a vertical set of related sections while keeping the surrounding page scannable.

### Best practices

- Do: Use concise trigger text that describes the content revealed below it.
- Do: Keep section content focused so expanding one item does not feel like navigating to a new page.
- Don't: Do not hide required fields, primary actions, or critical errors inside collapsed sections.
- Don't: Do not nest an Accordion inside an Accordion. Two layers of roving focus fight each other, and the arrow keys become ambiguous — flatten the hierarchy or use a Tree.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AccordionItem | yes | One expandable section in the group. |
| AccordionTrigger | yes | The button-like control that opens the section. |
| AccordionPanel | yes | The content revealed by the trigger. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AccordionItem | Base UI Accordion.Item props + className (value, disabled, onOpenChange) | Pairs a header with its panel. Give each a stable `value` to control or set initial open state. |
| AccordionTrigger | Base UI Accordion.Trigger props + className + indicator?: ReactNode | The header button (Header + Trigger composed). Renders children plus a chevron that rotates via data-[panel-open] by default; pass `indicator` to replace the icon and its open-state behavior entirely (e.g. a plus that becomes an × for a FAQ-style toggle). |
| AccordionPanel | Base UI Accordion.Panel props + className (keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound) | The collapsible body. Animates height using the --accordion-panel-height CSS var; fades on data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style]. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accordion (Root) | Base UI Accordion.Root props (value, defaultValue, multiple, disabled, onValueChange, orientation, loopFocus, keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound) | — | Groups all items and owns the open value(s). Uncontrolled via defaultValue, controlled via value. |
| defaultValue | Value[] | [] | Uncontrolled set of item values that start expanded (e.g. ['faq-1']). |
| value | Value[] | — | Controlled set of expanded item values; pair with onValueChange. |
| onValueChange | (value: Value[]) => void | — | Called with the new set of expanded item values when an item opens or closes. |
| multiple | boolean | false | Whether more than one item can be open at the same time. When false, opening one closes the others. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — An accordion is page furniture that is present from first paint. Animating it in would stage content the reader is already scanning past.
- **response** · AccordionTrigger · `motion-interactive` — The whole header row is the hit target, and it looks like a heading rather than a control. The hover shift is what tells the reader it can be clicked before they click it.
- **transition** · AccordionPanel · `motion-disclosure` — Panel height is the only cue that content came from THIS header rather than appearing at the bottom of the page. Snapping it open moves everything below by a screenful with nothing connecting cause to effect.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — Nothing here is indeterminate — the panel content is already resident. A panel that loads on expand should put its own loader inside the panel.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the trigger inside an <h3> heading and wires aria-expanded / aria-controls to the panel region.
- Arrow keys move roving focus between triggers; Home/End jump to the first/last; loopFocus wraps by default.
- Each trigger toggles its panel with Enter/Space; the panel is announced as a labelled region.
- A disabled AccordionItem dims and is skipped by keyboard focus while neighbouring items stay interactive.
- The chevron rotation is driven by data-[panel-open] and the focus ring by focus-visible — both honor reduced-motion via the consumer's transitions.

## Related

- Components: Collapsible, Tabs

## Examples

### Single (default)

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion defaultValue={["a"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>Is it permanent?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Yes — stored on Arweave.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem><AccordionItem value="b"><AccordionTrigger>How much?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>A one-time mint fee.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

### Multiple open

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion multiple defaultValue={["a", "b"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>First</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>One.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem><AccordionItem value="b"><AccordionTrigger>Second</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Two.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

### Custom indicator (plus-becomes-×)

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion defaultValue={["a"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger indicator={<Icon name="plus" className="text-xs text-muted-foreground transition-transform [[data-panel-open]_&]:rotate-45" />}>Is it permanent?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Yes — stored on Arweave.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

# AppHeader

**Status:** stable

Mobile top bar (sticky, hidden at lg) with leading / title / actions slots on a 3-column grid that keeps the title optically centered. Grows into the top safe-area.

**Keywords:** app header, top bar, mobile header, chrome

## Usage

Use AppHeader for compact application chrome at the top of a screen, usually with navigation, identity, and a small action set. Pass it to AppShell's `header` slot so screen content clears it on mobile (it is sticky and hides itself at lg).

### Best practices

- Do: Keep the header actions narrow and predictable so the page title remains legible.
- Do: Use it once per app view as chrome, not as repeated content inside page sections.
- Don't: Do not overload it with filters, forms, or page-specific controls that belong in the content area.
- Don't: Do not render more than one per app, or put a second one inside a route. It is sticky chrome, so two of them stack and permanently eat the top of the viewport.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| leading | ReactNode | — | Leading slot — back button, create action, or menu trigger. |
| title | ReactNode | — | Center slot — brand wordmark or contextual page title. |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Trailing slot — wallet trigger, action buttons. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `border`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a <header> landmark.
- Pair with a leading control that has an accessible label (e.g. a BackButton).

## Related

- Components: AppShell, PageHeader, BottomNav

## Examples

### Contextual header

```tsx
import { AppHeader, Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<AppHeader leading={<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Back"><Icon name="chevron-left" /></Button>} title="Notifications" />
```

### Choosing between AppHeader and PageHeader

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppShell, PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// AppHeader is APP chrome — it persists across routes and holds global
// affordances (brand, search, account). One per app.
<AppShell header={<AppHeader title="Studio" />}>
  <Region max="content">Route content</Region>
</AppShell>

// PageHeader is CONTENT — it introduces the current route and scrolls away
// with it. One per page, INSIDE the region.
<Region max="content">
  <PageHeader title="Billing" description="Plans, invoices, payment methods." />
</Region>

// ✗ Putting route-specific actions in AppHeader. They then persist onto routes
//   where they mean nothing, and the header becomes a dumping ground.
```
