# GlidingHighlight

**Status:** stable

One highlight that travels to the active item, instead of each item toggling its own background. Measured, not assumed, so rows of unequal height stay exact.

**Keywords:** highlight, active, selection, indicator, menu, list, glide, slide, thumb, hover

## Usage

Use GlidingHighlight for a set of items where one is active at a time and the pointer or arrow keys move between them — a menu, an option list, a command palette, a segmented control. It replaces per-item `hover:bg-*` with a single element that moves.

### Best practices

- Do: Pass `hovered ?? selected`. The fallback is what makes the pointer leaving a menu return the highlight to the current choice instead of dropping it, so the reader's place is never lost.
- Do: Reach for it wherever a list is keyboard-navigable. The gain is largest for arrow keys: a background that teleports between rows makes the eye re-find the highlight at every step, where one that moves can be tracked while it travels — which is what keeps a long list readable in motion rather than only at rest.
- Do: Keep selection semantics on the items — `aria-selected`, `aria-current`, `data-selected`. The highlight is `aria-hidden` decoration over whatever the children already announce.
- Don't: Do not use it for items that are not mutually exclusive. A travelling highlight says 'one of these, and it is this one'; over a multi-select list it contradicts the checkboxes beside it, and only one of the two can be right.
- Don't: Do not put non-item chrome among the direct children — a group heading, a separator, a footer hint. Every direct child is a measurable row, so `active` counts them, and the highlight lands one row off from the index the caller is reasoning about. Wrap the items in their own GlidingHighlight, or move the chrome outside.
- Don't: Do not drive it from a scroll position or a timer. It is an affordance for a set with a discrete active member; a highlight that moves without an item becoming active reads as the interface selecting things on its own.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | Positioning context for the highlight. Each direct child is measured as one item. |
| Highlight | yes | The travelling element. `aria-hidden`, absolutely positioned, invisible until something is active. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| active | number \| null | — | Index of the item the highlight sits behind, or `null` for none. Pass `hovered ?? selected`. |
| orientation | "vertical" \| "horizontal" | — | Deprecated and ignored: the highlight measures both axes, so a horizontal row needs no flag. |
| onPointerLeave | PointerEventHandler (and every other div prop) | — | The container is a plain div, so its props pass through. For a hover-following list, reset the hovered index here so the highlight returns to the selected row when the pointer leaves. |
| highlightClassName | string | — | Class for the travelling highlight itself, for changing its fill or radius. The radius defaults to `sable-frame-inner`, so inside a `sable-frame` container it nests concentrically; in any other rounded, inset container pass `rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset>` here and on the rows. The container's own `className` styles the list. |

## Tokens used

`accent`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Highlight · _no motion_ — It deliberately does not animate in. Fading it up at rest position — usually row 0 — makes a menu look like it opened with the first item pre-selected, which is a claim about state that is not true. It stays invisible until something is genuinely active.
- **response** · Container · _no motion_ — The container is not the control; the items are, and they own their own pointer states. This draws the result.
- **transition** · Highlight · `motion-interactive` — The travel IS the component — a highlight that jumps is just a background toggle with extra machinery. Position, size and opacity ride one declaration so a tall row's height cannot catch up after its position has, which would read as the highlight stretching into place rather than moving.
- **activity** · Highlight · _no motion_ — Nothing here is indeterminate. A list still loading its options shows a Skeleton in place of the rows.

## Accessibility

- The highlight is `aria-hidden` and carries no semantics — it renders selection, it does not declare it. Keep `aria-selected` / `aria-current` on the items themselves.
- Pointer-free by construction (`pointer-events-none`), so it can never intercept a click meant for the item beneath it.
- Works with roving-tabindex and `aria-activedescendant` lists alike: it reads an index the caller already owns, and does not manage focus.
- Under reduced motion or with MotionProvider off, the highlight moves instantly rather than gliding — the active item is still shown, which is the part that carries meaning.

## Related

- Components: Menu, Select, Combobox, CommandMenu, SideNav

## Examples

### A hoverable menu, returning home on leave

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={hovered ?? selected} className="sable-frame sable-surface sable-surface-popover sable-frame-popover" onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(null)}>{items.map((item, i) => (<button key={item.id} type="button" className="sable-frame-inner px-2 py-1.5 text-start" onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(i)} onClick={() => setSelected(i)}>{item.label}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

### Horizontal, as a segmented control

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={tab} className="sable-well flex gap-1 rounded-md p-1" highlightClassName="rounded-concentric-md/1">{tabs.map((t, i) => (<button key={t} type="button" className="rounded-concentric-md/1 px-3 py-1" onClick={() => setTab(i)}>{t}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

### Keyboard navigation — the case it exists for

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={cursor} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "ArrowDown") setCursor((c) => (c + 1) % rows.length) }}>{rows.map((r) => (<div key={r.id} role="option" aria-selected={false}>{r.label}</div>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

# GradientArt

**Status:** beta

Placeholder artwork painted by a static WebGL shader from the preset's own art direction (the --art-* tokens: palette, ground, warp, softness, grain) — Ember burns, Prism airbrushes, Meridian is grainy monochrome — with a CSS gradient underneath for prerendered pages and browsers without WebGL2.

**Keywords:** gradient, mesh gradient, grain, shader, artwork, placeholder image, cover, banner, avatar fallback, generative

## Usage

Use GradientArt where a real image belongs but none exists yet, or where the image is decoration: a product cover before upload, a profile banner, an album tile, an avatar with no photo. It reads the theme's own tokens, so it follows every preset, mode and live edit; `seed` fixes each item's composition so a list of covers or avatars stays individually recognisable.

### Best practices

- Do: Pass a stable `seed` per item — the name for an avatar, the title for a cover. Each item then keeps the same art across renders, reloads and themes, which is what lets someone recognise it.
- Do: Size it with layout classes (`aspect-[4/3]`, `h-20`, `size-10 rounded-full`) and put any glyph or initials inside as children; they render above the art.
- Do: Keep the default `mesh` for covers, tiles and avatars. Reach for `grain` where a printed, tactile surface suits — a banner, a hero card — and keep one variant per surface type so art reads as a system.
- Don't: Do not put body text over it. The art spans the palette's lightest and most saturated tones, so no single ink is guaranteed to clear contrast across it; reserve overlays for a short label on a scrim or an avatar's initials.
- Don't: Do not pass colours, and reach for `tones` rarely. The art follows the preset's --art-* tokens on purpose; to change how a product's art looks, set the --theme-art-* hooks in its theme or preset, so every cover, banner and avatar changes together.
- Don't: Do not use it as a page or hero background. It paints at the element's pixel size, so a full-viewport instance costs a large frame on every theme change; it is sized for covers, banners and tiles.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "mesh" \| "grain" | "mesh" | mesh: soft spots of colour pulled together by gentle waves. grain: glowing light over deep corners with a printed texture. |
| tones | ("info" \| "standard" \| "collectible" \| "edition" \| "warning")[] | — | Paint these `--tone-*` colours instead of the preset's art palette. Leave unset to follow the preset's art direction. |
| seed | string \| number | — | Fixes the composition: the same seed paints the same art in every theme. Pass a stable id. |
| children | ReactNode | — | Rendered above the art — initials, a glyph, a short label. |
| className | string | — | Size and shape: aspect, height, rounding. |

## Variants

- **variant**: mesh, grain

## Tokens used

`art-1`, `art-2`, `art-3`, `art-4`, `art-5`, `art-6`, `art-ground`, `art-warp`, `art-softness`, `art-grain`, `primary`, `tone-info`, `tone-standard`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-edition`, `tone-warning`

## Motion

- **arrival** · canvas · `motion-interactive` — The shader frame fades in over the CSS gradient it replaces, so the swap from fallback to shader reads as the art settling rather than a flash.
- **response** · root · _no motion_ — Artwork, not a control: it does not react to the pointer.
- **transition** · canvas · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — A theme change repaints the frame in place on the next animation frame; there are no states to move between.
- **activity** · root · _no motion_ — Static by design: nothing animates between paints, so it costs nothing while idle and respects reduced motion without a branch.

## Accessibility

- Decorative by default: the canvas is aria-hidden. When the art stands for something (an avatar), label the element that contains it, not the art.
- Children render above the art in the normal reading order, so initials or a label are announced as usual.

## Related

- Components: Avatar, Card, AspectBox

## Examples

### Product cover

```tsx
import { GradientArt } from "@sableui/react"

<GradientArt seed="Untitled (gold rush)" className="aspect-[4/3] rounded-lg" />
```

### Grain banner

```tsx
import { GradientArt } from "@sableui/react"

<GradientArt variant="grain" seed="juno" tones={["info", "edition"]} className="h-20 rounded-md" />
```

### Avatar with initials

```tsx
import { GradientArt } from "@sableui/react"

<GradientArt seed="Mara Okafor" className="grid size-10 place-items-center rounded-full text-label-md text-overlay-foreground">MO</GradientArt>
```

# InlineStatus

**Status:** stable

A borderless single-line status message — a leading semantic icon + one line of text over the canonical tone scale (neutral/info/success/warning/destructive). The non-boxed sibling of Note for inline affirmations, errors, and progress; pass a custom icon (e.g. a Spinner) for a pending row.

**Keywords:** inline status, state, message, availability

## Usage

Use InlineStatus for short state messages placed near the thing they describe.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it beside inputs, rows, actions, or settings that need local status.
- Do: Keep the message brief and pair color with text.
- Don't: Do not use InlineStatus for global announcements or page-level alerts.
- Don't: Do not use tone as the only signal. Colour alone fails for colour-blind users — the leading icon is what carries the meaning, so never hide it.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | Severity tone — drives the leading icon (name + color) and the text color. The shared status-tone vocabulary (STATUS_TONES). |
| size | "sm" \| "md" | "sm" | Text size: sm (text-body-sm) or md (text-body-md). sm is the default for inline placement under a control; md matches surrounding body copy. |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Override the leading glyph (e.g. a <Spinner />); otherwise the tone selects it. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, info, success, warning, destructive
- **size**: sm, md

## Tokens used

`tone-info`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Color reinforces, never replaces, meaning — the leading icon and the message text carry the status.
- For a live status (e.g. a form submit result), render it in an aria-live region or pair it with the field's error wiring so the change is announced.

## Related

- Components: StatusDot, Badge, Banner, Note

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { InlineStatus, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={1}><InlineStatus tone="success">Top-up confirmed.</InlineStatus><InlineStatus tone="destructive">Insufficient balance.</InlineStatus></Stack>
```

### Pending (custom icon)

```tsx
import { InlineStatus, Spinner } from "@sableui/react"

<InlineStatus tone="neutral" icon={<Spinner size="sm" />}>Preparing transaction…</InlineStatus>
```

# Input

**Status:** stable

Styled native text input. Soft-square (rounded-sm), card surface, 2px focus ring; aria-invalid raises the destructive error treatment.

**Keywords:** input, text input, field, form, email, search, file, invalid, validation

## Usage

Use Input for short freeform text, search, email, password, file, and native input types. In forms, wrap Input in Field so label, description, required state, and validation messaging stay accessible and consistent.

### Best practices

- Do: Pair every Input with a visible label through Field or an explicit label/htmlFor connection.
- Do: Use type, inputMode, autoComplete, and placeholder as progressive hints, not as the only label.
- Do: Set aria-invalid or use Field error copy when validation fails.
- Do: Keep a focusable field at 16px or larger on mobile. iOS Safari zooms the whole page when a focused input computes under 16px and never zooms back out. Input handles this itself — below the sm breakpoint it renders text-body-lg (17px) and returns to text-body-md at sm and up. Build a custom field the same way: a second paired tier under a max-sm: variant, never a hand-set font-size.
- Don't: Override an Input's type with a page tier below 16px (text-body-md, text-body-sm, text-label-*) without a >=16px mobile arm — that reintroduces the iOS focus zoom.
- Don't: Use placeholder text as the label; it disappears once the user types and is not enough context.
- Don't: Use Input for long body copy. Use Textarea for multi-line content.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | yes | The native input element with Sable surface, disabled, focus, and invalid styling. |
| Label | yes | Usually provided by Field or a separate Label. It gives the input its visible purpose. |
| Description | no | Optional helper copy connected through aria-describedby when using Field. |
| Error | no | Validation message paired with aria-invalid and destructive styling. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | "md" \| "xs" | "md" | md is the form field. xs is the dense inset field of a tool panel (an inset panel-field fill, no outline, tight padding) — the same ladder as Select and Combobox. Use it instead of overriding the height with className. |
| type | string | "text" | Native input type (text, email, password, search, number, file, …). type="file" themes the native selector button via file: token utilities. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the control and blocks pointer interaction. |
| aria-invalid | boolean | — | Surfaces the destructive border + ring. Base UI form fields set this automatically. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"input"> | — | All native input attributes (placeholder, value, onChange, ref, …) pass through. |

## Variants

- **size**: md, xs

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <input> — labels, keyboard, and form semantics come for free.
- Renders through Base UI's Input (Field.Control): inside a Field it picks up the label, description, error and validity wiring from context, even when nested in a wrapper.
- Always associate a <label htmlFor> (or wrap) — placeholder text is not a label.
- Focus-visible ring uses the --ring token at 40% opacity.
- Set aria-invalid='true' on error so the destructive treatment is conveyed, not color-only.

## Related

- Components: Field, Form, Textarea, SearchInput, NumberField
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input placeholder="Search posts" />
```

### With a label

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Email"><Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" /></Field>
```

### Field with helper text

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Display name" description="Shown on your public profile."><Input placeholder="Nova Reed" /></Field>
```

### Field error

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Email" error="Enter a valid email address."><Input type="email" defaultValue="not-an-email" /></Field>
```

### Search input

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Search posts"><Input type="search" placeholder="Search by title, creator, or tag" /></Field>
```

### Invalid

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input aria-invalid defaultValue="not-an-email" />
```

### File

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input type="file" accept="image/*" />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input disabled placeholder="Disabled" />
```

# Kbd

**Status:** stable

A keyboard key indicator. Renders a raised <kbd> key cap sized from the surrounding text, so one Kbd fits body copy, menus and tooltips; KbdGroup sets one cap per key for a combo. `mod` renders the platform modifier (⌘ or Ctrl); `variant="ghost"` is the bare label for menu rows and tooltips.

**Keywords:** keyboard, shortcut, key, kbd

## Usage

Use Kbd to display keyboard keys or shortcuts in help text, menus, and docs.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it only for literal keyboard input such as Cmd, Enter, or Esc.
- Do: Show a combo as one cap per key inside KbdGroup — `<KbdGroup><Kbd mod /><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>` — not several keys typed into one cap.
- Do: Use `variant="ghost"` where the shortcut sits on a surface of its own — a menu row's trailing slot, a tooltip — so it reads as a hint, not a second control.
- Don't: Do not use Kbd as a decorative badge or button replacement.
- Don't: Do not set a text size on a Kbd. It sizes itself from the text around it.
- Don't: Do not hardcode ⌘ or Ctrl. The modifier differs by platform; use `<Kbd mod />`, which renders ⌘ on macOS/iOS and Ctrl elsewhere, or Windows users read Mac keys.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mod | boolean | false | Render the platform's shortcut modifier in place of children: ⌘ on macOS and iOS, Ctrl everywhere else. Server-rendered as Ctrl and corrected on hydration. |
| variant | "key" \| "ghost" | "key" | `key`: a raised cap on the surface it sits on, with a heavier bottom edge as the key's lip. `ghost`: the bare label, for menu rows, tooltips and other surfaces that are already a frame. |
| className | string | — | Merge additional classes onto the key cap. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"kbd"> | — | All native <kbd> attributes (children, ref, etc.). |

## Tokens used

`border`, `border-strong`, `background`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Uses the semantic <kbd> element so assistive tech announces keyboard input.
- KbdGroup is itself a <kbd> around the per-key caps — the HTML spelling of one key combination — so the combo is announced as a single piece of input.
- Sized in em from the surrounding text, so it scales with the user's text size and never shrinks below 12px.

## Related

- Components: Code, Menu, CommandMenu

## Examples

### Single keys

```tsx
import { Kbd } from "@sableui/react"

<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

### Combo

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<KbdGroup><Kbd mod /><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>
```

### In a menu row

```tsx
import { Kbd, MenuItem } from "@sableui/react"

<MenuItem>Search<KbdGroup className="ms-auto"><Kbd variant="ghost" mod /><Kbd variant="ghost">K</Kbd></KbdGroup></MenuItem>
```

# Label

**Status:** stable

Styled native <label>. Paired label typography via a size step (xs / sm / md / lg, all sentence case) or an uppercase eyebrow (eyebrow), non-selectable, dims when its peer control is disabled. Optional hint adds a dotted-underline tooltip affordance.

**Keywords:** label, form label, control, accessibility

## Usage

Use Label to name a form control and create a clear accessible relationship with that control.

### Best practices

- Do: Use explicit, persistent labels for inputs, selects, textareas, and grouped controls.
- Do: Place helper text separately so the label stays short and direct.
- Don't: Do not rely on placeholder text as the only label for a control.
- Don't: Do not use it as a bare styled span. A Label without htmlFor or a wrapped control looks like a label and does nothing — clicking it will not focus the field, which is the entire point.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| htmlFor | string | — | Associates the label with a control by its id (native <label for>). |
| size | "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "lg" | Paired label typography step, all sentence case. xs is simply the smallest; for an uppercase eyebrow use eyebrow. |
| eyebrow | boolean | false | Set the label as an eyebrow: the uppercase, letter-spaced text-overline tier (themeable to sentence case). Replaces size. For a kicker above a group, not an ordinary field label. |
| hint | ReactNode | — | When set, the label gets a dotted-underline affordance and reveals this content in a tooltip on hover/focus. |
| className | string | — | Merge or override classes via cn(). |

## Variants

- **size**: xs, sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <label> — clicking it focuses/activates the associated control.
- Associate with a control via htmlFor (matching the control's id) or by wrapping the control.
- In a form, use Field: it renders this Label, wires htmlFor/id, and dims the label when the field is disabled. Hand-wired outside a Field, the label only dims via peer-disabled when the control carries `peer` AND precedes the Label in the DOM (Tailwind peer-* only matches a later sibling).
- With `hint`, the label becomes focusable and the help text is announced via the tooltip's aria-describedby — so the affordance works for keyboard and screen-reader users, not just hover.

## Related

- Components: Input, Textarea, Fieldset, Form, Field

## Examples

### With control

```tsx
import { Input, Label, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={1}><Label htmlFor="name">Display name</Label><Input id="name" /></Stack>
```

### In a form

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Display name" disabled><Input /></Field>
```

### With hint

```tsx
import { Label } from "@sableui/react"

<Label htmlFor="royalty" hint="A percentage of every resale, paid to you.">Royalty</Label>
```

# LineChart

**Status:** beta

Lines over a sequence — for comparing how measures move. Smooth, linear or step curves, optional dots (coloured by series or by category) and value labels. Lines draw on as the chart scrolls into view.

**Keywords:** chart, line, trend, time series, graph, compare, analytics, dashboard

## Usage

Use LineChart to compare how two or more measures change over the same sequence, or to show one trend precisely (with dots and labels). Unlike AreaChart, its value axis is fitted to the data rather than forced to zero, so small movements stay visible — say so if the axis is shown.

### Best practices

- Do: Turn on dots and labels for six or fewer points, when the exact values are the story.
- Do: Use curve="step" for values that hold until they change — prices, plan tiers, headcount.
- Don't: Plot unordered categories (channels, products) as a line — the line implies a path between them; use BarChart.
- Don't: Use it for data-heavy views — streaming or real-time data, thousands of points, zoom and brushing, trading charts. Those belong on a charting library (Recharts, visx, ECharts); Sable's charts are for dashboards, landing pages and decks.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | Record<string, unknown>[] | — | The rows, in order along the category axis. |
| index | string | — | The datum field naming each row's category (a month, a day, a channel). |
| series | { key: string; label: string; tone?: ChartTone; color?: string; icon?: string }[] | — | The measures to plot: the datum field, its name in the legend/tooltip/table, and its colour (a tone by role, or any CSS colour). Omitted, series take the chart palette in order: --chart-1 … --chart-8, validated for colour-blind separation in light and dark; a theme may override the set. |
| label | string | — | What the chart shows. Its accessible name and the caption of the data table assistive tech reads. |
| className | string | "h-60" | Sizes the chart (plot + legend). Set a height: `h-72`, `aspect-video h-auto`. |
| valueFormatter | (value: number) => string | — | Format values everywhere (axis, labels, tooltip, table) — units like "$12,480". Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere. |
| indexFormatter | (value: string) => string | — | Shorten category labels on the axis ("January" → "Jan"); the tooltip keeps the full value. |
| locale | string | runtime locale | BCP 47 locale for default number and date formatting. |
| tooltip | boolean \| { indicator?: "dot" \| "line" \| "dashed" \| "none"; hideLabel?: boolean; labelFormatter?: (label, datum) => ReactNode; showTotal?: boolean } | true | Show a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, or configure it: the row marker, hiding the heading, rewriting it, adding a Total row. |
| legend | boolean | true when there is more than one series | Show the legend under the chart. |
| grid | boolean | true (false for horizontal bars) | Hairline gridlines along the value axis. |
| xAxis | boolean | true for columns; false for horizontal bars | The horizontal axis. |
| yAxis | boolean | false for columns; true for horizontal bars | The vertical axis. |
| animate | boolean | true | Play the arrival once the chart scrolls into view. Reduced motion shows the finished chart. |
| activeIndex | number \| null | — | The highlighted row (controlled); `null` for none. |
| defaultActiveIndex | number \| null | — | The row highlighted at first — a tooltip already open before anyone hovers. |
| onActiveIndexChange | (index: number \| null) => void | — | Called as the pointer or keyboard moves between rows. |
| curve | "smooth" \| "linear" \| "step" | "smooth" | How the line runs between points. `smooth` is monotone: it never overshoots a value the data does not contain. |
| dots | boolean | false | Mark every data point with a dot. |
| colorBy | "series" \| "index" | "series" | Colour the dots by series, or each by its category. |
| labels | boolean | false | Print each point's value above it. |

## Tokens used

`tone-edition`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-standard`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `foreground`, `background`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Line · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Once on screen each line draws on from the first point (stroke-dashoffset), series staggered, then the dots and labels fade in. On the motion tokens; reduced motion shows the finished chart.
- **response** · Cursor + tooltip · _no motion_ — Hover and focus move the cursor and tooltip instantly — a lagging cursor reads as a slow chart.
- **transition** · Line + dots · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Geometry eases from the old shape to the new one through a CSS `d` transition on the motion tokens (no recipe animates path geometry); browsers without `d` transitions update in place.
- **activity** · LineChart · _no motion_ — A chart has no indeterminate state; show a Skeleton while the data loads.

## Accessibility

- The drawing is aria-hidden; the same numbers are in a visually hidden data table (captioned by `label`) that the chart is aria-describedby, so assistive tech reads values, not shapes.
- With a tooltip, the chart is one tab stop (role=group, aria-roledescription="chart"): arrow keys, Home and End step through the data, Escape clears, and each step is announced in a polite live region.
- Colour is never the only key: series are named in the legend, tooltip and table.

## Related

- Components: AreaChart, BarChart, Sparkline, Card

## Examples

### Compare two series

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@sableui/react"

<LineChart
	label="Desktop and mobile visitors"
	data={visitors}
	index="month"
	series={[
		{ key: "desktop", label: "Desktop", tone: "primary" },
		{ key: "mobile", label: "Mobile", tone: "info" },
	]}
	indexFormatter={(m) => m.slice(0, 3)}
/>
```

### Dots and labels

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@sableui/react"

<LineChart
	label="Desktop visitors"
	data={visitors}
	index="month"
	series={[{ key: "desktop", label: "Desktop" }]}
	curve="linear"
	dots
	labels
	grid={false}
/>
```

# Marker

**Status:** stable

A non-message row in a conversation: streaming status, system note, bordered notice, or a labelled rule for date breaks. Quieter than the message tier by design.

**Keywords:** chat status, typing indicator, thinking, streaming, tool call, system message, date separator, date break, conversation divider

## Usage

Everything in a conversation that is not a message. Date breaks, "Carla joined", "Thinking…", "Ran search — 3 results", "Message failed to send". One component because they share one job: annotate the stream without competing with it.

### Best practices

- Do: Use `status` with `icon="spinner" spin` for work in flight, and add `shimmer` while text is actually streaming. The shimmer is scale-aware, so it freezes with the rest of the system under reduced motion.
- Do: Use `variant="separator"` for date breaks. The label sits between two rules, which reads as a division of the transcript rather than as another thing someone said.
- Do: Replace a status marker's text as the work progresses — "Thinking…" → "Searching the docs" → "Writing the answer". It is a live region, so each change is announced.
- Do: Reach for `bordered` only when a note needs containing — an error, an escalation, a retention notice. Boxing routine system events makes a transcript look like a list of alerts.
- Don't: Do not style a Marker up to message weight. Its whole value is being below that tier; a marker as loud as a message competes with the conversation it is annotating.
- Don't: Do not leave a status marker mounted after the work finishes. A permanent "Thinking…" is a live region that never resolves, which is worse than no status at all.
- Don't: Do not use it for a message from a person or an assistant. That is `Message` + `Bubble` — a marker has no author and no side.
- Don't: Do not set `live` on a `separator` or on a run of `note` markers. Announcing every date break and join event turns the live region into noise and buries the status that mattered.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "status" \| "note" \| "bordered" \| "separator" | "status" | `status` for live activity, `note` for a system event, `bordered` for a note that needs containing, `separator` for a labelled rule. |
| icon | string | — | Semantic icon name shown before the label, resolved through IconProvider. |
| spin | boolean | false | Spin the icon — pair with `icon="spinner"` for work in flight. |
| shimmer | boolean | false | Sweep the label while something is streaming, via the scale-aware `motion-text-shimmer` recipe (freezes under reduced motion). |
| live | boolean | true for `status`, false otherwise | Announce the label to assistive tech as it changes. On for `status`, because a screen-reader user otherwise gets silence for the whole generation and no way to tell a slow answer from a dead one. |
| ...div props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | — | Spread onto the row. |

## Variants

- **variant**: status, note, bordered, separator

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `muted`, `border`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- `status` markers render as `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so a change of activity is announced without interrupting whatever is being read.
- The other variants are silent by default and can opt in with `live` — announcing every date break and join event would bury the status that mattered.
- The separator's rules are `aria-hidden`, leaving only the label in the accessibility tree; the shimmer is decoration over readable text, not a replacement for it.
- `motion-text-shimmer` keeps the label opaque through every frame — the gradient runs muted-foreground → foreground rather than fading to transparent, so the text never becomes unreadable mid-animation, and `--motion-scale` freezes it entirely under reduced motion.

## Related

- Components: Message, Bubble, MessageScroller, InlineStatus, Separator

## Examples

### Streaming status

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Thinking…</Marker>
```

### Date break

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="separator">Yesterday</Marker>
```

### System note

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="note" icon="user">Carla joined the conversation</Marker>
```

### A notice that needs containing

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="bordered" icon="warning">This conversation will be archived in 7 days.</Marker>
```

### In a transcript

```tsx
import { Bubble, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96">
	<Marker variant="separator">Today</Marker>
	<Message messageId="m1"><Bubble>Can you summarise the release?</Bubble></Message>
	<Marker variant="note" icon="sparkles">Ran changelog — 12 entries</Marker>
	<Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Writing the answer</Marker>
</MessageScroller>
```

# Marquee

**Status:** stable

Seamless, constant-speed infinite loop (logos, tags, testimonials). Zero-dependency: duplicates children to fill the track and advances exactly one group + gap per iteration so it never seams. Pauses on hover/focus; freezes to a scroll region when motion is off/reduced.

**Keywords:** marquee, ticker, scrolling, ambient

## Usage

Use Marquee for decorative or ambient continuous content where motion supports the surface.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for low-priority repeated content such as logos, tags, or lightweight highlights.
- Do: Respect reduced motion and keep the content understandable without relying on animation.
- Don't: Do not put critical messages, controls, or required reading inside Marquee.
- Don't: Do not put content that must be read in a Marquee. It moves continuously, so anything longer than a logo or a short label cannot be read reliably — and it must stop for prefers-reduced-motion.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direction | "left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" | "left" | Scroll direction; up/down switch to a vertical loop, which needs a bounded height (e.g. className="h-56"). |
| speed | number | 40 | Constant speed in px/s — independent of content length. |
| gap | string | "calc(var(--spacing) * 8)" | Gap between items (any CSS length). Use a spacing-scale value (calc(var(--spacing) * n)) so it moves with density. |
| pauseOnHover | boolean | true | Pause while hovered or keyboard-focused (WCAG 2.2.2). |
| controls | boolean | false | Render a visible pause/play control — recommended for WCAG 2.2.2 when content auto-scrolls. |
| fade | boolean | false | Fade the leading/trailing edges with a mask. |
| label | string | — | Accessible label for the scrolling region. |

## Accessibility

- Duplicate groups are aria-hidden, so screen readers read the content once.
- Pauses on hover and focus-within; under prefers-reduced-motion / MotionProvider off it stops and becomes a normal scroll region.
- Decorative by default — pass a label only when the row conveys meaning.

## Related

- Components: Scroller, Carousel, Badge

## Examples

### Logo row

```tsx
import { Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee>{logos.map((l) => <img key={l.id} src={l.src} alt={l.name} className="h-8" />)}</Marquee>
```

### Reverse, faster

```tsx
import { Badge, Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee direction="right" speed={70}>{tags.map((t) => <Badge key={t} appearance="outline">{t}</Badge>)}</Marquee>
```

### Vertical

```tsx
import { Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee direction="up" className="h-64">{items}</Marquee>
```

# MediaImage

**Status:** beta

An image that fills its box and falls back to GradientArt seeded by the item when it has no source or the source fails — Avatar's image-load tracking, for covers, thumbnails and product shots instead of faces.

**Keywords:** image, img, image fallback, broken image, cover art, album art, thumbnail, placeholder image, onError, missing image

## Usage

Use MediaImage wherever content imagery may be missing or broken: a cover in a grid, a thumbnail in a row, a product shot. It fills the box it is given — an AspectBox for a cover, a sized and rounded box for a thumbnail — shows a quiet muted surface while the image loads, fades the image in once decoded, and paints GradientArt seeded by the item when there is no image to show, so a grid of missing covers still reads as distinct things. For a person use Avatar; for a whole tile with title and actions use MediaTile, which composes this.

### Best practices

- Do: Give the box the shape: `<AspectBox ratio={1} className="rounded-md"><MediaImage … /></AspectBox>`, or `size-14 rounded-md` on MediaImage itself for a thumbnail. It clips to whatever radius the box has.
- Do: Pass `seed` (the title or an id) when `alt` is empty, so the fallback art is the item's own and stays the same in every list it appears in.
- Do: Leave `alt` empty when a visible title sits next to the image — a tile, a row — and describe it when the image stands alone. A set `alt` also names the fallback, so the description survives a broken URL.
- Don't: Do not hand-write `<img onError={() => setBroken(true)}>`. An image that fails before hydration never fires the handler on a prerendered page; MediaImage preloads off the DOM and catches it.
- Don't: Do not use it for profile pictures. A person is a circle with initials — Avatar, whose `variant="art"` is the same fallback with the person's initials over it.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src | string | — | Image URL. Omitted, empty or failing to load ⇒ the fallback shows. |
| alt | string | "" | Alt text. Empty is decorative — right beside a visible title. When set and no image shows, it names the fallback instead. |
| seed | string \| number | — | Seeds the fallback art. Defaults to `alt`; pass the title or an id when `alt` is empty. |
| fallback | ReactNode | — | Replaces the GradientArt fallback — a glyph or monogram. Fills the frame under the same clipping. |
| fit | "cover" \| "contain" | "cover" | `cover` crops to fill (artwork, photos); `contain` letterboxes on the muted surface (a logo, a product that must not be cropped). |
| srcSet | string | — | Responsive sources, passed to the `<img>`. |
| sizes | string | — | The `sizes` attribute for `srcSet`. |
| loading | "lazy" \| "eager" | "lazy" | Native lazy loading. Use `eager` for the first row of a grid above the fold. |
| className | string | — | Sizing and rounding when MediaImage is the box itself (`size-14 rounded-md`). Inside an AspectBox it already fills. |

## Variants

- **fit**: cover, contain

## Tokens used

`muted`, `art-1`, `art-2`, `art-3`, `art-4`, `art-5`, `art-6`, `art-ground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · image · `motion-fade` — The image fades in over the muted surface once it has decoded, so a slow cover settles in instead of popping row by row as the grid loads.
- **response** · root · _no motion_ — Imagery, not a control. The tile or row around it answers the pointer.
- **transition** · root · _no motion_ — Its only state change is loading → loaded or failed, which the arrival covers.
- **activity** · root · _no motion_ — A loading image rests on a static muted surface; a shimmer per cover across a long grid would be noise.

## Accessibility

- `alt` defaults to empty (decorative), because the usual neighbour is a visible title that already names the item; describe the image when it stands alone.
- When no image is on screen and `alt` is set, the frame takes `role="img"` with that label, so a broken URL does not erase the description. The fallback art itself is always aria-hidden.
- The `<img>` mounts only once it has loaded, so assistive technology never meets a broken-image icon.

## Related

- Components: MediaTile, Avatar, GradientArt, AspectBox

## Examples

### Cover with fallback

```tsx
import { AspectBox, MediaImage } from "@sableui/react"

<AspectBox ratio={1} className="rounded-md">
	<MediaImage src={album.cover} seed={album.title} />
</AspectBox>
```

### No image yet

```tsx
import { AspectBox, MediaImage } from "@sableui/react"

<AspectBox ratio={1} className="rounded-md">
	<MediaImage seed="Low tide, high noon" />
</AspectBox>
```

### Row thumbnail

```tsx
import { MediaImage } from "@sableui/react"

<MediaImage src={track.art} seed={track.title} className="size-12 shrink-0 rounded-sm" />
```

### Logo, never cropped

```tsx
import { AspectBox, MediaImage } from "@sableui/react"

<AspectBox ratio={16 / 9} className="rounded-lg">
	<MediaImage src={brand.logo} alt={brand.name} fit="contain" />
</AspectBox>
```

# MediaTile

**Status:** beta

A cover-first tile — square, 16:9 or poster artwork with an optional play-style action over it, then a title and a subtitle that can each be links — that is one link as a whole without nesting its other controls inside one.

**Keywords:** album, album art, cover, tile, media card, video thumbnail, podcast, playlist, gallery, product tile, poster, grid item, play button, music

## Usage

The item in a media grid or shelf: an album, a playlist, a video, a podcast, a film, a photo, a product. The cover leads and carries the weight; the title and subtitle sit underneath without a card around them. The whole tile follows the title's link, the subtitle can link somewhere else (the artist, the channel), and an action — usually play — floats over the cover's corner, revealed on hover and focus and always shown on touch. A missing or broken cover becomes GradientArt seeded by the title, so a grid of items without artwork still reads as distinct things.

### Best practices

- Do: Lay tiles out with `Grid` (`<Grid minItemWidth="10rem">`) or a horizontal `Scroller` for a shelf. The tile fills its cell; the grid decides the width.
- Do: Pass `render={<Link to="…" />}` (or `href`) for where the tile goes, and `subtitleRender` / `subtitleHref` for a second destination. Each stays a separate control; never wrap the tile in your own link.
- Do: Name the action for its item — `aria-label="Play Low tide, high noon"`, not "Play". A grid of twenty identical "Play" buttons is unusable from a screen reader's list of controls.
- Do: Use `titleAs="h3"` when the tiles sit under a section heading, so screen-reader users can move tile to tile by heading.
- Don't: Do not build this from `Card render={<Link />}`. A card that is a link cannot hold a second link or a button — interactive content cannot nest — which is exactly what a media tile needs.
- Don't: Do not put more than one action on the cover. A second control over the art is a toolbar on a thumbnail; move secondary actions (add to queue, share) into an OverflowMenu in the action slot or onto the item's page.
- Don't: Do not use it for a framed commerce card with a price and a buy button — that is ProductCardBlock — or for a person, which is an Avatar.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover | yes | An AspectBox holding MediaImage: the image, or GradientArt seeded by the title. Drawn first, read last. |
| Title | yes | The item's name. When the tile links, this is the link, stretched over the whole tile. |
| Subtitle | no | The second line. Optionally its own link, raised above the stretched one. |
| Action | no | One control over the cover's bottom-end corner — usually play. Revealed on hover and focus; always visible on touch. |
| Badge | no | A static label over the cover's top-start corner — a duration, "New". Click-through. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | ReactNode | — | The item's name. Seeds the fallback art when it is a string. |
| subtitle | ReactNode | — | The second line — an artist, a channel, a year. |
| src | string | — | Cover image URL. Without one, or when it fails, the cover is GradientArt seeded by the item. |
| alt | string | "" | Cover alt text. Empty by default: the title below already names the item. |
| seed | string \| number | — | Seeds the fallback art. Defaults to `title` when it is a string. |
| aspect | "square" \| "video" \| "poster" \| number | "square" | The cover's shape: square (albums, podcasts), video (16:9), poster (2:3 — films, books), or any width / height ratio. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Moves the type tier, the cover-to-text gap, the corner and the overlay inset together. |
| href | string | — | Where the tile goes. The title becomes the link, stretched over the whole tile. |
| render | useRender.RenderProp | — | The title link's element, for a router: `render={<Link to="/albums/1" />}`. Takes precedence over `href`. |
| subtitleHref | string | — | Makes the subtitle its own link — a separate tab stop above the tile's. |
| subtitleRender | useRender.RenderProp | — | The subtitle link's element, for a router. |
| action | ReactNode | — | One control over the cover's bottom-end corner, usually a play Button. Hidden until hover or focus on hover-capable devices; always shown on touch. |
| badge | ReactNode | — | A static label on the cover's top-start corner — `<Badge appearance="overlay">`. |
| titleAs | "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "p" | "p" | The title's element. A heading one level below the section's lets screen-reader users move tile to tile. |
| loading | "lazy" \| "eager" | "lazy" | Native image loading. `eager` for the first row above the fold. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "title"> | — | Spread onto the root. |

## Variants

- **size**: sm, md, lg
- **aspect**: square, video, poster

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `muted`, `overlay`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Cover · `motion-fade` — The cover image fades in over a quiet surface once it decodes, so a grid loading on a slow connection settles tile by tile instead of popping.
- **response** · Cover · `motion-interactive` — Hovering the tile deepens the cover with a light scrim and lifts the action in (`reveal-on-hover`), so it is clear the whole tile is one target and where its action is.
- **transition** · root · _no motion_ — A tile has no states of its own to move between; the action carries any (play / pause).
- **activity** · root · _no motion_ — Nothing runs inside a tile; a now-playing indicator belongs to the player, not the grid.

## Accessibility

- No nested interactive content: the title is the tile's link, and its `stretched-link` overlay covers the tile, while the subtitle link and the action sit above it as separate controls.
- Tab order is title → subtitle → action. The text comes first in the DOM and the cover is drawn above it with CSS `order`, so focus follows how a reader names the item.
- Focusing the title link rings the whole tile, rounded like the cover, because the whole tile is what the link is; the subtitle link and the action ring themselves.
- The action is hidden with opacity only, and only where the device can hover; it stays in the tab order and the accessibility tree, appears when anything in the tile has focus, and is always visible on touch.
- The cover is decorative by default (`alt=""`), since the title names the item; the fallback art is aria-hidden.
- Truncated titles keep their full text in the link's accessible name and in a `title` tooltip.

## Related

- Components: MediaImage, GradientArt, Grid, AspectBox, Card, Scroller

## Examples

### Album grid

```tsx
import { Button, Grid, Icon, MediaTile } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<Grid minItemWidth="10rem" gap={3}>
	{albums.map((album) => (
		<MediaTile
			key={album.id}
			title={album.title}
			subtitle={album.artist}
			src={album.cover}
			render={<Link to={`/albums/${album.id}`} />}
			subtitleRender={<Link to={`/artists/${album.artistId}`} />}
			action={
				<Button size="icon" aria-label={`Play ${album.title}`} onClick={() => play(album)}>
					<Icon name="play" variant="solid" />
				</Button>
			}
		/>
	))}
</Grid>
```

### Video tile with a duration

```tsx
import { Badge, MediaTile } from "@sableui/react"

<MediaTile
	aspect="video"
	title="Building a synth from scratch"
	subtitle="Undertow Sessions · 2 days ago"
	src={video.thumbnail}
	href={`/watch/${video.id}`}
	badge={<Badge appearance="overlay">12:04</Badge>}
/>
```

### Gallery, no links

```tsx
import { Grid, MediaTile } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid minItemWidth="8rem" gap={2}>
	{photos.map((photo) => (
		<MediaTile key={photo.id} size="sm" title={photo.caption} src={photo.url} alt={photo.description} />
	))}
</Grid>
```

### Poster shelf

```tsx
import { MediaTile } from "@sableui/react"

<MediaTile aspect="poster" size="lg" titleAs="h3" title="The Long Dark" subtitle="2026 · Drama" href="/films/the-long-dark" />
```

# Menu

**Status:** stable

Dropdown menu over Base UI Menu — roving focus, typeahead, ARIA menu/menuitem wiring, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal. Trigger + portal-rendered popup with items, groups, and separators.

**Keywords:** menu, dropdown, actions, commands

## Usage

Use Menu for a compact list of actions opened from a visible trigger.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for secondary or grouped commands that do not need to be visible all the time.
- Do: Keep item labels action-oriented and easy to scan.
- Do: Inside a <Workspace> a Menu adapts automatically — its popup re-applies the compact density across the portal, so items render on the chrome type tier and the control ladder resolves to workspace sizes. Do NOT override the size per call site; that was necessary before v0.41 and is now drift.
- Don't: Do not use Menu for complex forms, persistent navigation, or arbitrary rich content.
- Don't: Do not build a Select out of it. A menu fires actions and has no value; a Select holds one and reports changes. Swapping them loses form semantics and keyboard type-ahead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MenuTrigger | yes | The control that opens the menu. |
| MenuContent | yes | The floating command surface. |
| MenuItem | yes | One selectable command. |
| MenuSeparator | no | A divider between groups. |
| MenuGroup | no | A grouped set of menu items. |
| MenuGroupLabel | no | A label for a group of items. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MenuTrigger | Base UI Menu.Trigger props + render | The button that opens the menu. Compose with render={<Button … />}. |
| MenuContent | Base UI Popup props + side: 'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' + align: 'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' + sideOffset: number + className | Portal + Positioner + Popup. side picks which side of the trigger the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision; defaults to 'bottom'); align sets alignment along that side (defaults to 'start'); sideOffset is the gap in px between trigger and popup (defaults to 6). |
| MenuItem | Base UI Menu.Item props + className (disabled, closeOnClick, onClick) + variant?: "default" \| "destructive" | An interactive row. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; dims via data-[disabled]. variant="destructive" for a delete or irreversible action: it keeps the destructive ink when highlighted (never className="text-destructive", which the highlight repaints). |
| MenuSeparator | Base UI Separator props + className | Hairline rule between item runs. |
| MenuSubmenu | Base UI Menu.SubmenuRoot props | A nested menu. Wraps a MenuSubmenuTrigger and its own MenuContent — pass side="inline-end" to that content so the submenu opens away from its parent in RTL as well as LTR. |
| MenuSubmenuTrigger | Base UI Menu.SubmenuTrigger props + value: ReactNode + className | The row that opens a submenu: item styling, a trailing chevron, and an optional `value` showing the current choice so the row reads "Effort  High ›" rather than making the reader open it to find out. |
| MenuRadioGroup | Base UI Menu.RadioGroup props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange) | A single-choice group inside a menu. Controlled via value/onValueChange, uncontrolled via defaultValue. |
| MenuRadioItem | Base UI Menu.RadioItem props + className (value, disabled) | One option in a MenuRadioGroup, rendered as menuitemradio with a real checked state. The check sits in a reserved leading column so labels never shift sideways as the highlight moves. |
| MenuCheckboxItem | Base UI Menu.CheckboxItem props + className + { checked?: boolean; defaultChecked?: boolean; onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void; disabled?: boolean } | A toggling row, with the same reserved leading column as MenuRadioItem so a menu mixing the two keeps one text margin. |
| MenuGroup | Base UI Menu.Group props + className | Groups related items; pair with MenuGroupLabel for an accessible group name. |
| MenuGroupLabel | Base UI Menu.GroupLabel props + className | The label for a MenuGroup — auto-associated with the group for screen readers. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Menu (Root) | Base UI Menu.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal, orientation, loopFocus) | — | Groups all parts and controls open state. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead.
- Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
- MenuGroupLabel is auto-associated with its MenuGroup for screen readers.
- A disabled MenuItem stays in the arrow-key order — Base UI keeps it focusable with aria-disabled so screen-reader users learn the command exists — but it cannot be activated, and it ignores the pointer.

## Related

- Components: ContextMenu, OverflowMenu

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu><MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Options</Button>} /><MenuContent><MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem>Duplicate</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenuItem></MenuContent></Menu>
```

### Grouped

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuGroup, MenuGroupLabel, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu><MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Account</Button>} /><MenuContent><MenuGroup><MenuGroupLabel>Signed in</MenuGroupLabel><MenuItem>Profile</MenuItem><MenuItem>Settings</MenuItem></MenuGroup><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem>Sign out</MenuItem></MenuContent></Menu>
```

### Nested, with a single-choice submenu

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, MenuSubmenu, MenuSubmenuTrigger, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu>
	<MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">View</Button>} />
	<MenuContent>
		<MenuItem>Reload</MenuItem>
		<MenuSubmenu>
			<MenuSubmenuTrigger value={density}>Density</MenuSubmenuTrigger>
			<MenuContent side="inline-end" align="start" sideOffset={4}>
				<MenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
					<MenuRadioItem value="Comfortable">Comfortable</MenuRadioItem>
					<MenuRadioItem value="Compact">Compact</MenuRadioItem>
				</MenuRadioGroup>
			</MenuContent>
		</MenuSubmenu>
	</MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

### Toggling rows

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuContent, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu>
	<MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Columns</Button>} />
	<MenuContent>
		<MenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.status} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCol("status", v)}>Status</MenuCheckboxItem>
		<MenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.updated} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCol("updated", v)}>Updated</MenuCheckboxItem>
	</MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

# Message

**Status:** stable

One row in a conversation: avatar gutter, side, and stacked header / content / footer. Layout only — the surface is Bubble, passed as children.

**Keywords:** chat, message, conversation row, turn, thread, messaging, grouped messages, ai chat

## Usage

The row a single turn occupies. It owns the geometry — which side, the avatar gutter, where the name and timestamp go, where reactions and receipts go — and nothing about how the content looks. That separation is the point: an assistant's markdown answer, a one-line reply, an attachment, and a tool-call card are all the same row with different children.

### Best practices

- Do: Set `messageId`. It is what MessageScroller reads for `scrollToMessage`, `initialScroll`, and visibility tracking — a message without one cannot be jumped to or marked as read.
- Do: Pass the same `align` to Message and to the Bubble inside it, so the flattened tail corner lands on the speaker's side.
- Do: Use `grouped` for consecutive messages from one author. It tightens the spacing and hides the avatar while keeping its column reserved, so the run reads as one block instead of stepping left. Pass `tail={false}` to the Bubble in each continuation too, so only the first message in the run carries a tail.
- Do: Match `avatarSize` to the `size` of the Avatar you pass (sm/md/lg line up 1:1). The gutter is declared, not measured, because it has to hold its width when `grouped` hides the avatar.
- Don't: Do not justify the content to move a message to the right. `align="end"` already mirrors the whole row, gutter included; adding your own justification fights it.
- Don't: Do not put the timestamp inside the Bubble. It belongs in `header` or `footer`, which stay outside the surface so `variant="plain"` content still has one.
- Don't: Do not reach for Message to lay out a system note or a date break. That is `Marker`, which is deliberately quieter than the message tier.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avatar gutter | no | Fixed-width column for the author's Avatar. Kept (but emptied) when `grouped`, which is what keeps a run aligned. |
| Header | no | Author name and timestamp, above the content. |
| Content | yes | The children — usually a Bubble, but equally an Attachment, a tool card, or plain rendered markdown. |
| Footer | no | Reactions, delivery receipts, retry actions. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| messageId | string | — | Stable id, published as `data-message-id`. The handle MessageScroller uses for scroll commands and visibility tracking. |
| align | "start" \| "end" | "start" | Which side of the conversation. "start" is the other party or the assistant; "end" is the person reading. Mirrors the whole row, gutter included. |
| avatar | ReactNode | — | Avatar node for the gutter. Omit for a message with no author identity. |
| avatarSize | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "sm" | Gutter width, matching Avatar's own size scale 1:1 (32 / 40 / 48px). Declared rather than measured so it survives `grouped`. |
| header | ReactNode | — | Author name, timestamp — anything above the content. |
| footer | ReactNode | — | Reactions, receipts, retry actions — anything below the content. |
| grouped | boolean | false | This message continues a run from the same author: tightens the spacing (via `--message-gap`) and drops the avatar while reserving its column. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "id"> | — | Spread onto the row. Use `messageId` rather than `id` — the scroller matches on `data-message-id`. |

## Variants

- **align**: start, end
- **avatarSize**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- A plain container with no imposed role — the conversation's semantics belong to the list or log element you wrap it in, not to each row.
- `align` reverses the visual row without reordering the DOM, so reading order in assistive tech stays chronological regardless of which side a message is on.
- The header and footer render at the secondary type step in muted ink, keeping both below the message tier in the visual hierarchy without dropping either below the AA contrast floor.

## Related

- Components: Bubble, MessageScroller, Marker, Attachment, Avatar

## Examples

### Incoming and outgoing

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, Message, RelativeTime } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="CA" />} header={<><strong className="text-foreground">Carla</strong><RelativeTime date={sentAt} /></>}>
		<Bubble>Did the deploy finish?</Bubble>
	</Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" align="end">
		<Bubble variant="primary" align="end">Green across the board.</Bubble>
	</Message>
</>
```

### A grouped run

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="CA" />} header={<strong className="text-foreground">Carla</strong>}>
		<Bubble>One more thing.</Bubble>
	</Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" grouped>
		<Bubble tail={false}>The staging cert expires Friday.</Bubble>
	</Message>
</>
```

### With reactions in the footer

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, BubbleReaction, BubbleReactions, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m3" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="JR" />} footer={<BubbleReactions><BubbleReaction emoji="🎉" count={3} active /><BubbleReaction emoji="👀" /></BubbleReactions>}>
	<Bubble>Shipped 0.45.0.</Bubble>
</Message>
```

### An attachment as the content

```tsx
import { Attachment, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m4" align="end">
	<Attachment name="proposal.pdf" meta="2.4 MB · PDF" />
</Message>
```

# MessageScroller

**Status:** stable

Scroll container for a conversation. Auto-follows new messages until the reader scrolls away, holds position when older history is prepended, and exposes scroll commands and visibility tracking through its ref.

**Keywords:** chat, conversation, messages, thread, transcript, stick to bottom, auto scroll, streaming, infinite scroll, inbox, ai chat, support chat

## Usage

The scroll region a conversation lives in. It owns the scrolling and nothing else — not your messages, not your AI state, not your transport or persistence — so you bring the content renderer and it handles the behaviors that make streaming chat feel right: pinning to the newest message, releasing when the reader scrolls up, keeping the view still when older history loads above, jumping to a specific message, restoring a saved read position, and reporting what is actually on screen.

### Best practices

- Do: Bound it the way you would bound any scroll box — `flex-1 min-h-0` inside a flex column, or `max-h-96`. `className` lands on the element that actually scrolls, so the obvious bound is the correct one (same contract as Scroller).
- Do: Give every Message a `messageId`. It is the handle for `scrollToMessage`, `initialScroll`, and `onVisibleMessagesChange` — a message without one is invisible to all three.
- Do: Prepend older history directly into `children` when the reader reaches the top. The scroller anchors on the first rendered message and re-adds the height that appeared above it, so the view does not jump.
- Do: Set the rhythm between messages with the `gap` prop, not with a flex class on `className` — the messages are laid out in a column inside the scroll region, not directly on it.
- Do: Restore a reopened thread with `initialScroll={{ messageId: lastRead }}` instead of dropping the reader at the bottom of a conversation they have not finished.
- Do: Wrap a docked agent panel in `<Density value="compact">`. The scroller tightens its rhythm and every message inside it drops to the workspace type tier — one attribute for the whole conversation, no per-component sizing.
- Don't: Do not call `scrollToBottom` on every incoming token. Auto-follow already does it, and doing it yourself fights the reader who scrolled up to read something.
- Don't: Do not expect `ref` to be the DOM node — it is a command handle (`scrollToBottom`, `scrollToMessage`, `isFollowing`). Reach for `ref.current.element` when you genuinely need the element.
- Don't: Do not wrap it in a positioned div to place a jump-to-latest button. It ships one, stuck to the bottom edge from inside the scroll region, which is why `className` gets to stay on the scrolling element.
- Don't: Do not use it for an ordinary long list. That is `Scroller` — this one's follow-the-bottom behavior is wrong for content the reader is browsing rather than receiving.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scroll region | yes | The element that scrolls. Carries `className`: sizing, padding, and background. |
| Message column | yes | The flex column holding the children, spaced by `gap`. Publishes `--message-gap` so `<Message grouped>` can close it. |
| Jump to latest | no | A control stuck to the bottom edge, shown only while the reader is scrolled away from the newest message. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ref | Ref<MessageScrollerHandle> | — | Imperative commands, not the DOM node: `scrollToBottom(opts)`, `scrollToTop(opts)`, `scrollToMessage(id, opts)` (returns false when the message is not rendered), `isFollowing()`, and `element` for the scrolling node itself. |
| autoFollow | boolean | true | Keep the newest message in view as content arrives, until the reader scrolls away from the bottom. Set false for a transcript that must never move under the reader. |
| followThreshold | number | 64 | Distance from the bottom, in px, that still counts as following. A band rather than a pixel, so a token arriving mid-frame does not flicker the state. |
| onFollowChange | (following: boolean) => void | — | Notified when the viewport pins to, or releases from, the newest message. |
| initialScroll | "bottom" \| "top" \| { messageId: string } | "bottom" | Where a freshly mounted thread lands. Pass a messageId to restore a saved read position. Applied once, on mount — changing it later will not yank a reader mid-conversation. |
| jumpToLatest | boolean | true | Show the jump-to-latest control while the reader is scrolled away from the newest message. |
| jumpToLatestLabel | string | "Jump to latest" | Accessible label and tooltip for that control. |
| gap | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Vertical rhythm between messages. Also published as `--message-gap`, which `<Message grouped>` reads to collapse the gap within a run. |
| onVisibleMessagesChange | (ids: string[]) => void | — | Ids of the messages currently intersecting the viewport, in DOM order. The hook for read receipts, mark-as-seen, and unread counters. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "ref"> | — | Spread onto the scrolling element. `className` bounds and pads the scroll region; `onScroll` composes with the component's own. |

## Variants

- **gap**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`border`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Native overflow, so keyboard scrolling (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End) and the OS scrollbar work unchanged; the scrollbar is styled thin, not replaced.
- Overscroll is contained, so a wheel gesture that runs out of conversation does not start scrolling the page behind it.
- The jump-to-latest control is a real button with an accessible label, reachable by keyboard, and only present when there is somewhere to jump to.
- Smooth scrolling is used only when motion is enabled — `prefers-reduced-motion` and <MotionProvider> off both collapse every scroll command to an instant jump.

## Related

- Components: Message, Bubble, Marker, Attachment, Scroller

## Examples

### Streaming conversation

```tsx
import { Bubble, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="flex-1 min-h-0 px-4 py-6">{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}><Bubble variant={m.mine ? "primary" : "muted"} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}{pending ? <Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Thinking…</Marker> : null}</MessageScroller>
```

### Scroll to a message on demand

```tsx
import { Bubble, Button, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

function Thread({ messages, replyTo }) {
	const thread = useRef(null)
	return (
		<>
			<Button onClick={() => thread.current?.scrollToMessage(replyTo)}>Show original</Button>
			<MessageScroller ref={thread} className="max-h-96">
				{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}
			</MessageScroller>
		</>
	)
}
```

### Restore a saved read position and track receipts

```tsx
import { Bubble, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96" initialScroll={{ messageId: lastRead }} onVisibleMessagesChange={(ids) => markSeen(ids)}>{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}</MessageScroller>
```

### Prepend older history without moving the view

```tsx
import { Bubble, Button, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96" gap="sm">{hasMore ? <Button variant="secondary" loadingLabel="Loading…" onClick={loadOlder}>Load earlier messages</Button> : null}{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}</MessageScroller>
```

# Meter

**Status:** stable

A role=meter reading over Base UI Meter, drawn as a bar or a ring — how full something is within a known range (storage, quota, strength), with a tone for good/caution/bad. Not task progress.

**Keywords:** meter, usage bar, storage, quota, capacity, limit, password strength, level

## Usage

Use Meter to show a static measurement against a known maximum — storage used, seats taken, API quota, password strength. It is announced as a meter, not a progress bar, so a screen-reader user hears a level rather than a task underway.

### Best practices

- Do: Label it and show the reading in units people use ("7.2 of 10 GB"), with MeterLabel and MeterValue. The bar shows proportion; the number is what gets acted on.
- Do: Pick `tone` from thresholds you own and apply them consistently across the page — warning near the limit, destructive at or over it. The component does not guess where good becomes bad.
- Do: Use shape="ring" when the reading is a score that belongs in a small, glanceable spot on a card. It is the same measurement drawn as a circular gauge, not a different component.
- Don't: Do not use Meter for a task in flight — an upload, an install, a step count. That is Progress; Meter tells assistive tech nothing is happening.
- Don't: Do not use it for a value without a meaningful maximum (followers, total spend). A bar implies a full scale; an unbounded count is a stat.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MeterTrack | yes | The rail that represents the full range. |
| MeterIndicator | yes | The fill, sized from value and coloured by tone. |
| MeterLabel | no | The visible name; also names the meter for assistive tech. |
| MeterValue | no | The formatted reading. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MeterTrack | Base UI Track props + className + size | The rail. Rendered automatically when Meter has no children; renders a MeterIndicator by default. |
| MeterIndicator | Base UI Indicator props + className + tone | The fill. Inherits the Meter's tone unless given its own. |
| MeterLabel | Base UI Label props + className | Visible label; wires aria-labelledby on the root. |
| MeterValue | Base UI Value props + className | Formatted reading. Accepts a `(formatted, value) => ReactNode` child. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number | — | The current reading, between min and max. Required. |
| min | number | 0 | The bottom of the range. |
| max | number | 100 | The top of the range. |
| tone | "primary" \| "standard" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "primary" | Fill colour, mapped to a semantic token. Choose it from your own thresholds. |
| shape | "bar" \| "ring" | "bar" | bar is a horizontal track; ring is a circular gauge for a small, glanceable reading — the same value, min, max and tones. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Ring diameter (40 / 64 / 96px at the default spacing; the centre value steps with it), or bar thickness on the same sm / md / lg rails as Progress. |
| showValue | boolean | — | Print the value in the ring's centre (formatted like MeterValue). |
| strokeWidth | number | 6 | Ring stroke width, in viewBox units of 100. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Formatting for MeterValue and aria-valuetext (percent, unit, currency). |
| getAriaValueText | (formatted: string, value: number) => string | — | Human-readable reading for assistive tech ("7.2 of 10 gigabytes used"). |
| locale | Intl.LocalesArgument | — | Locale for formatting. Defaults to the runtime locale. |

## Variants

- **tone**: primary, standard, success, warning, destructive
- **shape**: bar, ring
- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `primary`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Meter · _no motion_ — A meter is a reading, present with the page that reports it. Animating the fill up from zero on load would act out a change that did not happen.
- **response** · Meter · _no motion_ — It reports and accepts no input. A bar that reacted to the pointer would read as a Slider the user could drag.
- **transition** · MeterIndicator · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Width and colour ease on the motion tokens (no recipe animates width) when the reading changes — freeing space after a delete visibly shrinks the bar, so the user sees the cause and effect rather than a different bar.
- **activity** · Meter · _no motion_ — A meter has no indeterminate state; a reading is either known or not shown. Unknown-but-working is Progress with no value.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders role=meter with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext — distinct from Progress's role=progressbar.
- Name it with MeterLabel or aria-label; an unnamed meter is announced as a bare number.
- Tone is colour only. Say the state in text too ("Almost full") when it matters, and use getAriaValueText to give units.

## Related

- Components: Progress, Badge

## Examples

### Ring

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter shape="ring" value={72} showValue aria-label="Storage used" />
```

### Bare

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter value={64} aria-label="Storage used" />
```

### Storage with label and reading

```tsx
import { Meter, MeterLabel, MeterTrack, MeterValue } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter value={7.2} max={10} tone="warning" getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v} of 10 gigabytes used`}>
	<div className="mb-2 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1">
		<MeterLabel>Storage</MeterLabel>
		<MeterValue>{(_, value) => `${value} of 10 GB`}</MeterValue>
	</div>
	<MeterTrack />
</Meter>
```

### Tones

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
	<Meter value={30} tone="success" aria-label="Seats used" />
	<Meter value={82} tone="warning" aria-label="API quota used" />
	<Meter value={100} tone="destructive" aria-label="Storage used" />
</div>
```

# MiddleTruncate

**Status:** stable

Middle-truncates a long string (hash, address, signature) to `5J7s…8xQp`, keeping the start and end legible while preserving the full value on hover.

**Keywords:** truncate, middle truncate, hash, identifier

## Usage

Use MiddleTruncate when both the beginning and end of a long identifier must remain visible.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for hashes, addresses, long filenames, URLs, or generated IDs.
- Do: Provide the full value through title text, copy action, or surrounding detail when needed.
- Don't: Do not use MiddleTruncate for human prose where the middle words carry meaning.
- Don't: Do not middle-truncate a value with no way to obtain it in full. Truncation removes characters from the page, so the value needs a copy affordance beside it: an icon Button with useCopy, as in the Copyable value example.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | string | — | The full string to render. When it is truncated, the full value is also set as the title attribute (a pointer tooltip). |
| startChars | number | 6 | How many leading characters to keep before the ellipsis. |
| endChars | number | 6 | How many trailing characters to keep after the ellipsis. |

## Accessibility

- When truncated, the visible abbreviation is aria-hidden and a visually hidden copy carries the full value, so screen readers announce the whole string. The title attribute holds it too, for a pointer tooltip only.
- Renders the string verbatim when it is too short to benefit from truncation, so no value is hidden needlessly.

## Related

- Components: Code, Button

## Examples

### Solana address

```tsx
import { MiddleTruncate } from "@sableui/react"

<MiddleTruncate text="5J7sX2QpHt9vK4mNbR8wYcZ3dF6gH1jL0pA8xQpVnTu" />
```

### Custom start/end counts

```tsx
import { MiddleTruncate } from "@sableui/react"

<MiddleTruncate text="0xAbC1234567890dEf1234567890aBcDeF12345678" startChars={4} endChars={4} />
```

### Copyable value

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, MiddleTruncate, Row, useCopy } from "@sableui/react"

const { copy, copied } = useCopy(address)
<Row gap={1}><MiddleTruncate text={address} /><Button variant="ghost" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Copy address" onClick={copy}><Icon name={copied ? "check" : "copy"} /></Button></Row>
```
