# Note

**Status:** stable

Callout / admonition box. Its tone follows the shared status-tone vocabulary (neutral/info/success/warning/destructive), pairing a soft tone fill with a matching leading icon. Optional title.

**Keywords:** note, callout, admonition, warning, caveat, hint, context

## Usage

Use Note for helpful supporting information that should sit near the relevant content — including a caveat or warning attached to a form, a dialog, or a section. It is the in-context callout; Banner is the page-level strip.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for tips, caveats, or secondary context that improves understanding.
- Do: Reach for Note rather than Banner when the message qualifies something on the page — a warning inside a dialog, a caveat above a submit button. Banner is a full-width announcement strip for page- or app-level state; inside a form it reads as a slab, and its soft fill carries no border or tone-colored icon, so the severity stops being visible.
- Do: Keep tone calm and concise so the note does not compete with primary content.
- Do: When the reader can resolve the state, pass `action` rather than putting a Button in children. The prop is data — label plus handler — so the callout owns the placement and weight; a Button dropped into children inherits neither, floats in the box's padding, and (in `secondary`) punches a near-background hole in the tone fill.
- Don't: Do not use Note for state the whole page or app is in (an outage, an offline session, a blocked account) — that is Banner — or for a message tied to one field, which is the field's own error text.
- Don't: Do not give a Note two actions. One remedy reads as the sentence's next move; two make it a decision point, which is a Dialog's job.
- Don't: Do not stack several in a row. Three notes together are a wall of asides; if everything is called out, nothing is.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| action | { label: string; onClick?: () => void; href?: string } | — | A single remedy, rendered below the body and aligned to the text column. Deliberately data, not a slot: Note owns the placement, weight, ink and motion, so the action cannot be styled into a button that outweighs the sentence explaining it. Use onClick for an in-place action (renders a button, no glyph) or href for a link (renders an anchor with a trailing chevron) — the chevron means navigate, so it appears only when the action genuinely goes somewhere. |
| tone | "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "info" | Severity tone — drives the border, fill, and leading icon color/name. The shared status-tone vocabulary (STATUS_TONES). |
| title | string | — | Optional bold lead-in rendered above the body (text-title-sm). |
| icon | string \| ReactNode \| null | — | Override the variant glyph: a string swaps the icon name (keeping the tone color), a ReactNode replaces it, null removes it; omit for the variant default. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, info, success, warning, destructive

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `success`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Rendered with role="note" so assistive tech can announce it as an aside.
- Color is never the sole signal — the leading icon and optional title reinforce severity.

## Related

- Components: Banner, InlineStatus, EmptyState

## Examples

### Info

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="info">Editions mint on Solana mainnet.</Note>
```

### With title

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="warning" title="Low balance">Top up SOL before minting.</Note>
```

### Warning with a remedy, inside a dialog

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="warning" action={{ label: "Unload chat model", onClick: unloadChatModel }}>gemma-4 is holding VRAM — generating now may be slow or fail.</Note>
```

### Custom icon

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="neutral" icon="lock">Pricing and supply cannot be changed after an edition is purchased.</Note>
```

# NotificationBadge

**Status:** stable

An unread indicator. Renders a bare dot or a count pill (capped as "{max}+"), or nothing when there's nothing to show. overlay pins it to the corner of a relative host; it is aria-hidden, so the host's name carries the count.

**Keywords:** notification, badge, count, unread

## Usage

Use NotificationBadge to show a compact unread count, alert count, or attention marker.

### Best practices

- Do: Place it on or near the item that owns the notifications.
- Do: Use compact counts and cap large numbers when exact precision is not useful.
- Don't: Do not use NotificationBadge as a standalone status label or category marker.
- Don't: Do not show a bare dot when the count is meaningful. A dot says "something"; if the user can act on "how many", show the number.
- Don't: Do not put a neutral badge on a secondary host. Both are the secondary surface, so the badge disappears; use primary or destructive there.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dot | boolean | false | Render a bare dot indicator with no number. Takes precedence over count. |
| count | number | — | Unread count. Renders nothing when <= 0 and dot is unset. |
| max | number | 99 | Cap before showing "{max}+". |
| tone | "destructive" \| "primary" \| "neutral" | "destructive" | Fill color. destructive for alarming counts; primary/neutral for non-alarming ones. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Scales the dot/pill on the spacing scale (count pill: sm 16px, md 18px, lg 20px at the default density). |
| overlay | boolean | false | Pin to the top-end corner of the nearest relative host (an icon button) — one placement for every caller instead of hand-tuned absolute offsets. |

## Variants

- **tone**: destructive, primary, neutral
- **size**: sm, md, lg
- **overlay**: true, false

## Tokens used

`destructive`, `destructive-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`

## Accessibility

- The badge is aria-hidden: a count rendered on a control is not associated with it, so the host needs an accessible name that includes the count — "Notifications, 3 unread" — or a screen-reader user hears "Notifications, button" and never learns there is anything new. Pass aria-hidden={false} only for a standalone badge whose number is the information.
- A dot carries no number and no words: on its own it tells a sighted user only that something changed, and tells everyone else nothing. Pair it with a label that says what is new, and never make its colour the only difference between two states.

## Related

- Components: Badge, StatusDot

## Examples

### Dot + counts

```tsx
import { NotificationBadge, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={3}><NotificationBadge dot /><NotificationBadge count={3} /><NotificationBadge count={128} /></Row>
```

### Overlay on an icon button

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, NotificationBadge } from "@sableui/react"

<Button variant="secondary" size="icon" aria-label="Notifications, 5 unread" className="relative"><Icon name="bell" /><NotificationBadge count={5} overlay /></Button>
```

# NumberField

**Status:** stable

Numeric input with decrement/increment steppers over Base UI NumberField — keyboard arrows, scroll, scrub-to-change, min/max clamping, locale formatting, and form integration. Styled like Input; drops straight into a Field.

**Keywords:** number field, numeric input, stepper, form

## Usage

Use NumberField for numeric values that benefit from validation, min/max bounds, or step controls.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for quantities, thresholds, percentages, and other real numeric values.
- Do: Set sensible min, max, and step behavior when the domain has bounds.
- Don't: Do not use NumberField for identifiers such as phone numbers, ZIP codes, or credit card numbers.
- Don't: Do not use it in a property grid with steppers left on. Its two 32px stepper buttons (36px each with their inset) put a ~110px floor on a control that needs ~44px there — pass steppers={false}, or use ScrubField.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| min | number | — | Lower bound. Clamps typing, arrows, scroll and scrub alike, so the value cannot leave the range by any route. |
| max | number | — | Upper bound, clamped on every input route the same way as `min`. |
| value / defaultValue | number | — | Controlled / uncontrolled numeric value. |
| onValueChange | (value: number \| null, event) => void | — | Fired when the value changes (null when cleared). |
| step / smallStep / largeStep | number | — | Increment amount; smallStep applies with the meta key, largeStep with shift. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Locale formatting (currency, percent, units, …). |
| steppers | boolean | true | Show the decrement / increment buttons. Turn off in a dense property grid — the two 32px stepper buttons (36px with their inset) put a ~110px floor on the control; without them the value left-aligns. |
| disabled / readOnly / required / name / id | — | — | Standard form-control props. Base UI applies id + required to the input, so it labels and validates correctly. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Decrement / Increment are labelled buttons (Decrease / Increase); the input is a spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max from Base UI.
- Routes aria-describedby / aria-invalid onto the input, so a Field's helper + error are announced for it.

## Related

- Components: Input, Slider

## Examples

### Bounded

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<NumberField defaultValue={1} min={0} max={99} />
```

### In a field

```tsx
import { Field, NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Quantity"><NumberField min={1} defaultValue={1} /></Field>
```

### Currency

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<NumberField defaultValue={9.99} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} />
```

# OtpField

**Status:** stable

One-time-code entry over Base UI's OTP Field — one slot per character, SMS autofill on the first slot, paste fills every slot, and only one tab stop for the whole code.

**Keywords:** otp, one-time code, one-time password, verification code, 2fa, two-factor, mfa, pin, passcode, input otp

## Usage

Use OtpField for a short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else — an SMS or email verification code, an authenticator app, a device pairing PIN. The slots show how long the code is and where the user is in it, which a plain Input cannot.

### Best practices

- Do: Set `length` to the exact length the server sends, and verify in `onValueComplete` (or with `autoSubmit` inside a form). Most users paste or autofill the whole code at once, so the moment of completion is the natural submit.
- Do: Label it through a `Field` ("Verification code") and say where the code was sent in the description. The first slot takes the field's name; the rest are announced by position.
- Do: Use `groupSize` for codes of 6 or more so the user can check the code in chunks against the message they are reading from.
- Don't: Do not use OtpField for a password, an arbitrary-length PIN, or anything the user types from memory. Slots promise a fixed length; use Input with `type="password"` and `autocomplete="current-password"` instead.
- Don't: Do not intercept paste or clear the field on a wrong code before the user has seen the error. Blocking paste breaks SMS autofill and password managers, and wiping the slots erases the evidence of which digit was wrong.
- Don't: Do not swap it for NumberField because the code is digits. A code is an identifier, not a quantity: NumberField strips leading zeros and offers steppers that make no sense here.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | yes | A role=group that holds the value, carries the field label and description, and reports completion. |
| Slot | yes | One input per character. The first carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and accepts the whole code. |
| Group gap | no | A decorative dash inserted every `groupSize` slots; hidden from assistive tech. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| length | number | 6 | Number of character slots. Completion fires when every slot is filled. |
| groupSize | number | — | Insert a visual gap every N slots (3 renders 123 – 456). The value stays one contiguous string. |
| value / defaultValue | string | — | Controlled / uncontrolled code. |
| onValueChange | (value: string, details) => void | — | Fires on every edit. `details.reason` is input-change, input-clear, input-paste or keyboard. |
| onValueComplete | (value: string, details) => void | — | Fires once every slot is filled — the place to verify the code. Also fires when a complete code is pasted over a complete value. |
| onValueInvalid | (attempted: string, details) => void | — | Fires when typed or pasted text contains characters `validationType` rejects, so you can explain the rejection rather than letting it vanish. |
| validationType | "numeric" \| "alpha" \| "alphanumeric" \| "none" | "numeric" | Which characters a slot accepts. Also picks the virtual keyboard (numeric → number pad). |
| autoSubmit | boolean | false | Submit the owning form when the code becomes complete. |
| mask | boolean | false | Render slots as password inputs. Only for codes that are secret on screen, such as a card PIN. |
| getSlotLabel | (index: number, length: number) => string | Character N of L | Accessible name for slots after the first. Override to localize. |
| aria-invalid | boolean | — | Marks every slot invalid (destructive border). `<Field error>` sets it for you. |
| disabled / readOnly / required / name / id / form | — | — | Standard form-control props. `id` lands on the first slot, so `<Field>` and `<label htmlFor>` name the field. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-strong`, `primary`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A code field is part of the form it sits in and appears with it. Animating it in would delay the one thing the user arrived to do — paste the code they just copied.
- **response** · Slot · `motion-interactive` — Focus moves between slots on every keystroke. The eased ring and border are what let the eye follow the cursor across six identical boxes instead of hunting for it after each digit.
- **transition** · Slot · `motion-interactive` — A filled slot strengthens its border, so a pasted code visibly lands in every slot at once. Easing it reads as the code arriving rather than the field flickering.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — Verifying the code is the form's work, not the field's. Show it on the submit Button's `loading` state, where the user expects the answer to appear.

## Accessibility

- The root is a role=group named by the field label; the first slot shares the label through `id`/`htmlFor`, and later slots are announced by position ("Character 2 of 6").
- Only one slot is in the tab order. Arrow keys, Home/End and Backspace move between slots; Tab leaves the whole field.
- The first slot carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and the numeric virtual keyboard, so iOS and Android offer the SMS code above the keyboard.
- Slots render at 20px (`text-mono-lg`), above the 16px floor that stops iOS Safari zooming on focus.

## Related

- Components: Input, Form, NumberField

## Examples

### Six digits

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code"><OtpField length={6} onValueComplete={verify} /></Field>
```

### In a field, grouped

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code" description="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} /></Field>
```

### With an error

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code" error="That code has expired. Request a new code and try again."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} defaultValue="482913" /></Field>
```

### Alphanumeric

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Pairing code"><OtpField length={8} groupSize={4} validationType="alphanumeric" /></Field>
```

# OverflowMenu

**Status:** stable

An overflow ellipsis icon button that opens a Menu. Composes our Menu + Button + Icon — pass MenuItems as children and it wires the ghost icon trigger, accessible label, and portal-rendered content. All keyboard, focus, and dismissal behavior comes through Menu.

**Keywords:** dots menu, more actions, ellipsis, kebab

## Usage

Use OverflowMenu for compact overflow actions when the primary action is already visible elsewhere.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for secondary commands that belong to a row, card, or toolbar item.
- Do: Keep labels explicit so the icon-only trigger does not obscure the command meaning.
- Don't: Do not hide the most important or most frequent action inside OverflowMenu.
- Don't: Do not use it as the only affordance on a touch surface. It is revealed on hover in most layouts, and hover does not exist on touch — pair it with a visible action or make it always-visible there.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | The menu rows — MenuItem / MenuSeparator / MenuGroup, etc. Rendered inside MenuContent. |
| align | 'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' | end | Alignment of the popup along its side. Overflow menus typically right-align under the trigger; 'start' anchors the popup's left edge to the trigger instead. |
| label | string | More actions | Accessible label (aria-label) for the icon-only trigger button. |
| icon | string | ellipsis | Semantic icon name rendered in the trigger, always at the solid weight. |
| size | 'icon' \| 'icon-sm' \| 'icon-xs' | icon | The trigger's rung on the icon-button ladder. 'icon' for a card or page header; 'icon-sm' or 'icon-xs' in a list row or dense toolbar, so the trigger does not set the row height. |

## Variants

- **size**: icon, icon-sm, icon-xs

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- The icon-only trigger is labeled via aria-label (label prop, default 'More actions').
- Menu provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead via Base UI.
- Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the trigger on close.

## Related

- Components: Menu, ContextMenu

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

<OverflowMenu label="Post actions"><MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem>Share</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenuItem></OverflowMenu>
```

### With leading icons

```tsx
import { Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

<OverflowMenu><MenuItem><Icon name="check" className="text-sm" />Mark as read</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive"><Icon name="xmark" className="text-sm" />Delete</MenuItem></OverflowMenu>
```

# PageHeader

**Status:** stable

In-flow page heading block: a title row (optional back control + actions) over an optional description, with room for children (filters, tabs) below.

**Keywords:** page header, title, lede, page actions

## Usage

Use PageHeader to establish a page's title, supporting description, and primary page actions.

### Best practices

- Do: Use one PageHeader per major page or route.
- Do: Keep the title literal and put explanation in the lede or nearby content.
- Don't: Do not use PageHeader inside repeated cards, dialogs, or compact panels.
- Don't: Do not use a second PageHeader for a section of the page. It is the route's one h1; each section below it takes a SectionHeader (an h2 with the same title row, description and actions).
- Don't: Do not put it outside the Region that holds the page content. It then sits at a different measure from what it introduces, and the page reads as two documents.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | ReactNode | — | The page title (renders an <h1>). |
| description | ReactNode | — | Supporting copy beneath the title. |
| back | ReactNode | — | Leading element before the title — typically a back control on drill-in routes. Keep it a ghost icon Button (size="icon", variant="ghost", aria-label="Back") so it stays quieter than the title. A ghost back control bleeds by its inset at the start, so its glyph lines up with the content edge below (Button bleed="none" opts out). |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Trailing actions aligned to the title row's end. They drop under the title when the row runs out of room, and the title wraps rather than truncating. A ghost or link Button at either end of the group bleeds by its own padding, so its label meets the content edge (the end on the title row, the start once wrapped); filled buttons keep their edge on the line. Direct children only. |
| titleAs | "h1" \| "h2" | "h1" | The title's heading element. Keep h1 — the route's one h1. Use h2 only when something above already owns the h1: a shell that renders the route title, or a page showing a PageHeader as an example. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders the title as an <h1>; use one PageHeader per page.
- Its title renders the route's `h1`. Do not render another `h1` elsewhere on the page: heading navigation would report two documents, and the outline a screen-reader user builds from it stops matching the page.

## Related

- Components: AppHeader, SectionHeader, Breadcrumbs, Button

## Examples

### With actions

```tsx
import { Button, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageHeader title="Storage credits" description="Fund permanent storage." actions={<Button>Top up</Button>} />
```

### One per page, inside the region

```tsx
import { Button, PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// PageHeader introduces the current route: title, optional description, and the
// actions that act on THIS page.

<Region max="content">
  <PageHeader
    title="Invoices"
    description="Every charge on this account."
    actions={<Button>Export</Button>}
  />
  <p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">Page content.</p>
</Region>

// ✗ Outside the Region. The header then sits at a different measure from the
//   content it introduces, and the page reads as two documents.
// ✗ Two on one page. A second one is a section heading: a SectionHeader
//   (an h2 on text-heading-3, same title row and actions), not another PageHeader.
// ✗ Global actions in it (account, search). Those persist across routes and
//   belong in AppHeader.
```

# PageLoader

**Status:** stable

Full-screen branded loading splash: the screen fades in, the mark breathes, and an indeterminate Progress bar pulses beneath it. All motion is token-driven, so it freezes to a calm static screen when motion is off/reduced.

**Keywords:** page loader, loading, route, pending

## Usage

Use PageLoader for full-route or full-page pending states where the entire view is not ready yet.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it during route transitions, auth checks, or initial data loading.
- Do: Prefer a clear page-level message when the wait may take noticeable time.
- Don't: Do not use PageLoader for small inline waits; use Spinner, an indeterminate Progress, or Skeleton.
- Don't: Do not leave it mounted if the route's data can fail. It covers the whole viewport, so a PageLoader that never resolves is indistinguishable from a hung application — always give it a failure path.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | Brand mark / logo shown at center. Falls back to a neutral pulsing mark. |
| label | string | "Loading" | Caption beneath the mark; also the accessible label on the role=status region. |
| fullscreen | boolean | true | Cover the viewport (fixed) vs fill the nearest positioned parent (absolute). |
| hideBar | boolean | false | Hide the indeterminate Progress bar under the mark. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`, `secondary`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- role=status with an aria-label (the label prop) announces the loading state politely.
- Decorative mark and bar are aria-hidden.
- Motion respects the policy: under off/reduced the pulses hold their first frame (static).

## Related

- Components: Spinner, Skeleton, Progress

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageLoader label="Loading Studio" />
```

### With a logo

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageLoader label="Loading"><img src="/logo.svg" alt="" className="h-10 w-auto" /></PageLoader>
```

### Contained (fills parent)

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="relative h-80"><PageLoader fullscreen={false} hideBar /></div>
```

# Pagination

**Status:** stable

Page navigation built from our own Button + Icon (no Base UI). A <nav aria-label='Pagination'> with prev/next icon buttons that disable at the bounds and numbered page buttons; the current page is a secondary button marked aria-current. Collapses to first/last/current plus a sibling window, bridging skipped runs with an ellipsis.

**Keywords:** pagination, pager, pages, table, results, navigation, next, previous

## Usage

Use Pagination when a result set is split into discrete pages and the user needs predictable movement through them. Pair it with DataTable, list results, or server-paged views; use a load-more Button or infinite scroll when page numbers are not meaningful.

### Best practices

- Do: Keep page state controlled by the parent route or data layer so URL, filters, and result fetches stay in sync.
- Do: Use a specific label when multiple pagers appear on a page, such as "Collector pages".
- Do: Reset to page 1 when filters or search terms materially change the result set.
- Don't: Use Pagination for tiny lists where all items fit comfortably on one page.
- Don't: Hide disabled previous/next buttons at the bounds; disabled controls make the current position clearer.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nav | yes | The labelled pagination landmark. |
| Previous/next | yes | Icon buttons for adjacent page movement, disabled at the bounds. |
| Page buttons | yes | Numbered buttons with aria-current on the active page. |
| Ellipsis | no | Non-interactive marker for skipped page ranges. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | number | — | The active page (1-based). Clamped into the valid range. |
| total | number | — | Total number of pages. |
| onPageChange | (page: number) => void | — | Called with the next page when a control is activated. No-op for out-of-range or unchanged values. |
| siblingCount | number | 1 | Page buttons shown on each side of the current page before the list collapses into ellipses. First and last pages are always shown. |
| label | string | Pagination | Accessible label applied to the surrounding nav element. |
| className | string | — | Extra classes merged onto the nav. |

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Renders a landmark <nav> with aria-label so assistive tech can jump to the pager.
- The current page button carries aria-current='page'.
- Prev/next buttons are real <button>s with aria-label and become disabled at the bounds.
- Ellipsis slots are aria-hidden — they convey no navigable target.

## Related

- Components: DataTable, Table, Button
- Patterns: ListDetailPage, DashboardPage

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
<Pagination page={page} total={10} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Many pages (ellipsis)

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(8)
<Pagination page={page} total={20} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Table results footer

```tsx
import { DataTable, Pagination, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={2}><DataTable data={rows} columns={columns} rowKey={(row) => row.id} /><Pagination label="Collector pages" page={page} total={12} onPageChange={setPage} /></Stack>
```

### Server query state

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(searchParams.page ?? 1)
<Pagination page={page} total={pageCount} onPageChange={(next) => { setPage(next); loadPage(next) }} />
```

# PanelGroup

**Status:** stable

A row of docked chrome panels around a flexible centre, with draggable and keyboard-resizable edges and optional persisted widths.

**Keywords:** panel, panels, resize, resizable, splitter, docked, workspace, tool, chrome, inspector, layout

## Usage

Use PanelGroup for the body of a tool workspace: fixed-width Panels docked left and/or right, a flexible Panel in the middle for the canvas, and a PanelResizer between them. Panels scroll internally and the group never scrolls. This is the workspace-register counterpart to SplitPane, which only switches between side-by-side and stacked at a breakpoint and cannot be resized.

### Best practices

- Do: Give every docked Panel a fixed width and leave the centre Panel width-less so it absorbs the remaining space.
- Do: Drive the width with usePanelWidth and pass a storageKey, so a user's layout survives a reload. Spread its bounds onto the PanelResizer rather than repeating min and max by hand.
- Do: Label every Panel — they are landmarks, and 'Layers' or 'Properties' is what a screen-reader user navigates by.
- Don't: Let the group scroll. Only panels and the canvas scroll; a scrolling group means the shell lost its height constraint.
- Don't: Use it for page content columns — that's Grid or Columns. PanelGroup is chrome, and it sits outside the content grid.
- Don't: Omit PanelResizer to save effort and then let users live with a fixed panel. If a panel holds a tree or a property grid, its width is a preference.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PanelGroup | yes | The flex row. Sets min-h-0/min-w-0 so children can actually shrink and scroll. |
| Panel | yes | One column. Fixed-width when `width` is set, flexible otherwise. Scrolls internally. |
| PanelResizer | no | The draggable edge between two panels: a 1px hairline with a wider hit area, operable by pointer and keyboard. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Panel | { label: string; width?: number; scroll?: boolean } | A docked or flexible column. `label` names the landmark; omit `width` for the flexible centre. `scroll` defaults to true — set it false for a header + scrolling body + pinned footer, so the footer doesn't scroll away with the list. When you own the layout, give the header and footer shrink-0 and the middle min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto. overflow-y-auto only activates if every flex ancestor can shrink: a single missing min-h-0 anywhere up the chain makes the panel grow instead of scroll, and nothing reports it. |
| PanelResizer | { side: 'left' \| 'right'; width: number; onWidthChange: (n: number) => void; label: string; min?: number; max?: number; step?: number } | The draggable edge. `side` says which side the resized panel is on, so the drag delta's sign is right. |
| usePanelWidth | (defaultWidth: number, options?: { storageKey?: string; min?: number; max?: number }) => readonly [number, (n: number) => void, { min: number; max: number }] | Controlled width for a Panel, clamped and optionally persisted to localStorage (only when `storageKey` is passed). Read through useSyncExternalStore, so there is no server/client hydration mismatch and no setState in an effect; do not hand-roll a localStorage read during render or a write from an effect. Without `storageKey` the width is kept in memory per hook instance. The third element is the `{ min, max }` it clamps to: spread it onto the paired PanelResizer so the separator's aria-valuemin/max and Home/End match the real clamp. |

## Tokens used

`primary`, `panel`, `hairline`, `hairline-strong`

## Accessibility

- PanelResizer is a role=separator with aria-orientation, aria-valuenow/min/max, and is focusable — a pointer-only resizer is a keyboard trap.
- Arrow keys resize by `step`; Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum.
- Each Panel renders an <aside> with an accessible name from `label`, so panels are navigable landmarks.

## Related

- Components: PanelSection, ScrubField, SplitPane, Sidebar, AppShell

## Examples

### Tool body with a resizable left panel

```tsx
import { Panel, PanelGroup, PanelResizer, PanelSection, PropertyRow, Switch, usePanelWidth } from "@sableui/react"

function Body() {
  const [leftWidth, setLeftWidth, leftBounds] = usePanelWidth(240, { storageKey: "app:panel:left", min: 180, max: 360 })
  return (
    <PanelGroup>
      <Panel label="Layers" width={leftWidth}>
        <PanelSection title="Layers">
          <PropertyRow label="Background">
            <Switch checked />
          </PropertyRow>
        </PanelSection>
      </Panel>
      <PanelResizer side="left" width={leftWidth} onWidthChange={setLeftWidth} label="Resize layers panel" {...leftBounds} />
      <Panel label="Canvas">
        <div className="grid h-full place-items-center bg-canvas text-ui-body text-muted-foreground">Canvas</div>
      </Panel>
    </PanelGroup>
  )
}
```

### Both edges resizable

```tsx
import { Panel, PanelGroup, PanelResizer, PanelSection, PropertyPair, ScrubField, usePanelWidth } from "@sableui/react"

function Body() {
  const [left, setLeft, leftBounds] = usePanelWidth(240, { storageKey: "app:left" })
  const [right, setRight, rightBounds] = usePanelWidth(256, { storageKey: "app:right" })
  return (
    <PanelGroup>
      <Panel label="Layers" width={left} />
      <PanelResizer side="left" width={left} onWidthChange={setLeft} label="Resize layers panel" {...leftBounds} />
      <Panel label="Canvas" />
      <PanelResizer side="right" width={right} onWidthChange={setRight} label="Resize properties panel" {...rightBounds} />
      <Panel label="Properties" width={right}>
        <PanelSection title="Blending">
          <PropertyPair>
            <ScrubField label="Opacity" icon="grid" suffix="%" value={100} min={0} max={100} />
            <ScrubField label="Blur" value={0} min={0} max={64} suffix="px" />
          </PropertyPair>
        </PanelSection>
      </Panel>
    </PanelGroup>
  )
}
```

### Fixed panel, no resizer

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, Panel, PanelGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelGroup>
  <Panel label="Tools" width={56}>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 p-1">
      <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Toggle grid"><Icon name="grid" /></Button>
      <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Hide"><Icon name="eye" /></Button>
    </div>
  </Panel>
  <Panel label="Canvas" />
</PanelGroup>
```

# PanelSection

**Status:** stable

A flush group of property rows inside a docked panel — eyebrow header, hairline separator, rows beneath. The workspace register's answer to Card, which does not belong in a panel.

**Keywords:** panel, section, inspector, properties, property grid, workspace, tool, chrome, sidebar

## Usage

Use PanelSection to group properties inside an inspector or docked panel, with PropertyRow for one label-plus-control line and PropertyPair for two controls side by side. This is the workspace register's grouping primitive: it separates with a hairline and nothing else, because a Card inside a 240px panel spends its border and inset on nothing and pushes every row inward.

### Best practices

- Do: Group related properties under a short functional title — Blending, Layout, Fill — the way a tool inspector names its sections.
- Do: Reach for PropertyPair before giving each property its own full-width row; pairing halves the vertical cost in a narrow panel.
- Do: Put a section-scoped control (a visibility toggle, an add action) in the action slot rather than inventing a second header row.
- Don't: Wrap panel content in Card. Cards are page-register furniture; in a panel they read as a page pasted into chrome.
- Don't: Repeat the panel's own title as the section title. If the header above already names the selection, title the section by what it controls (Parameters, Blending).
- Don't: Hand-roll a property line (`<div className="flex justify-between"><span>Opacity</span><Slider /></div>`). Use PropertyRow for every label-plus-control line: when each property type invents its own arrangement, a panel of fifteen properties ends up with fifteen layouts.
- Don't: Use PropertyRow for page forms — use Field, which carries label/description/error semantics. PropertyRow is a dense chrome row, not a form control.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header | yes | The section title in the UI section tier, with an optional trailing action. |
| PropertyRow | no | One property: label left, control right. `stacked` moves the control to its own line for full-width controls. |
| PropertyPair | no | Two controls side by side, with optional captions above each. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PropertyRow | { label: ReactNode; htmlFor?: string; hint?: string; stacked?: boolean; scrub?: { value, onValueChange, step?, min?, max?, onGestureStart?, onGestureEnd?, disabled? } } | One property line. `hint` becomes the label's hover explanation; `stacked` puts the control on its own line. `scrub` makes the property NAME a drag handle for its value — the Figma/Framer/Paper convention, and the answer for a numeric row with no honest glyph to put in a ScrubField (a schema-generated `levels` or `seed`, where a `#` would be noise pretending to be meaning). Opt-in and additive: a row without it is unchanged. The label stays a real `<label htmlFor>` — a 2px jitter threshold keeps a click a click, and the click synthesised after a real drag is swallowed so a scrub does not also select the field's text. |
| PropertyPair | { labels?: [ReactNode, ReactNode] } | Two controls side by side in a 2-up grid, with optional captions above each. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | ReactNode | — | Section name, rendered as the header in the UI section tier. |
| action | ReactNode | — | Optional trailing control in the header — a visibility toggle, an add action. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `hairline`

## Accessibility

- PropertyRow renders a real <label>; pass htmlFor with the control's id so clicking the label focuses it.
- The section title is an h3, so panels contribute a real heading outline rather than styled divs.
- `hint` is exposed as the label's title attribute — keep the essential meaning in the label itself, since title text is not reliably announced.
- A `scrub` label does not replace keyboard editing and must not be the only way to set the value: the drag is a pointer affordance, so the control it names still has to accept typing and arrow keys. It also keeps its `htmlFor` behaviour, which is the reason the gesture arms on a 2px threshold rather than on pointerdown.

## Related

- Components: Workspace, PanelGroup, ScrubField, StatusBar, Field, Card

## Examples

### Blending section, 2-up

```tsx
import { PanelSection, PropertyPair, ScrubField, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection title="Blending">
  <PropertyPair>
    <ScrubField label="Opacity" value={100} min={0} max={100} suffix="%" />
    <Select value="normal">
      <SelectTrigger size="xs" />
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="normal">Normal</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="multiply">Multiply</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </PropertyPair>
</PanelSection>
```

### Rows with a stacked slider

```tsx
import { PanelSection, PropertyRow, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, Slider, Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection title="Parameters">
  <PropertyRow label="Block size" hint="Block edge length in reference pixels." stacked>
    <Slider value={32} min={4} max={256} />
  </PropertyRow>
  <PropertyRow label="Direction">
    <Select value="both">
      <SelectTrigger size="xs" />
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="both">Both</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="horizontal">Horizontal</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </PropertyRow>
  <PropertyRow label="Reverse">
    <Switch checked={false} />
  </PropertyRow>
</PanelSection>
```

### Section with a header action

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, PanelSection, PropertyRow, ScrubField } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection
  title="Blending"
  action={
    <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Hide layer">
      <Icon name="eye" />
    </Button>
  }
>
  <PropertyRow label="Opacity">
    <ScrubField label="Opacity" value={60} min={0} max={100} suffix="%" />
  </PropertyRow>
</PanelSection>
```

# Phone

**Status:** stable

A current smartphone frame at iPhone proportions: a dark body with a titanium band, thin bezels, an island, an optional status bar and a scrollable screen.

**Keywords:** phone, device mockup, mobile preview, frame

## Usage

Use Phone to frame a mobile product preview when the device context is useful.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for mobile UI demos, screenshots, and responsive previews.
- Do: Keep the framed content legible and avoid stuffing full desktop layouts into the phone frame.
- Don't: Do not use Phone as a generic panel, card, or production app shell.
- Don't: Do not use it to test responsive behaviour. The frame is a fixed aspect box, not a viewport, so media queries inside key off the real window.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | Content rendered inside the scrollable screen region. |
| statusBar | boolean | true | Draw a status bar (time, signal, battery) across the top of the screen. Turn it off to frame a screenshot that already has one. |
| systemChrome | boolean | true | Draw the camera pill and home indicator. Turn it off when the content draws its own system chrome, such as an iOS prototype framed by PhoneFrame from @sableui/react/ios/preview. |
| className | string | — | Additional classes merged onto the outer wrapper (set the width here; the screen keeps its proportions). |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Purely presentational frame; the screen region scrolls when content overflows. Add headings/landmarks in the content as needed.
- The frame's chrome (status bar, camera, buttons) is aria-hidden, so the content inside carries the entire accessible meaning. A screenshot with no alt text makes the whole mockup announce as nothing at all.

## Related

- Components: Browser

## Examples

### Framing a mobile layout

```tsx
import { Phone } from "@sableui/react"

<Phone><div className="p-4"><h2 className="text-title-lg">Activity</h2><p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">3 new collects today.</p></div></Phone>
```

### Mockup, not a responsive preview

```tsx
import { Phone } from "@sableui/react"

// Phone is DECORATIVE framing for a mobile screenshot on a marketing surface.

<Phone>
  <img src="/screenshots/mobile.png" alt="The mobile app" />
</Phone>

// ✗ Using it to test responsive layout. The frame is a fixed aspect box, not a
//   viewport — media queries inside it key off the real window, so what you see
//   is not what a phone renders. Resize the browser, or use device emulation.
// ✗ Wrapping live, interactive app UI (forms, buttons that act). Same as Browser: the frame says "picture of
//   software", so real controls inside it read as a screenshot that moves. Static composed content is fine.
//   The exception is a clickable iOS prototype: PhoneFrame (@sableui/react/ios/preview)
//   frames a whole phone-sized document in an iframe, where the frame is the device.
```

# PieChart

**Status:** beta

Parts of a whole as slices: a pie or donut, concentric rings for several measures, a total in the hole, slice labels inside or out, and an active slice that pulls outward. Slices sweep in clockwise as the chart scrolls into view.

**Keywords:** chart, pie, donut, doughnut, share, proportion, breakdown, parts, whole

## Usage

Use PieChart for a share of one total across two to six categories — traffic sources, a budget split, survey answers. A donut leaves room for the total in the middle (`centerLabel`). With more categories, or to compare values precisely, use BarChart; for a breakdown inside a stat card, SegmentedBar is lighter.

### Best practices

- Do: Put the total, or the headline slice, in a donut's centerLabel.
- Do: Configure slice names, tones and icons with categories, keyed by each slice's value in the data.
- Don't: Use more than six slices — merge the tail into "Other" or use BarChart.
- Don't: Use it for data-heavy views — streaming or real-time data, thousands of points, zoom and brushing, trading charts. Those belong on a charting library (Recharts, visx, ECharts); Sable's charts are for dashboards, landing pages and decks.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | Record<string, unknown>[] | — | One row per slice. |
| index | string | — | The datum field naming each slice. |
| valueKey | string \| string[] | — | The datum field holding each slice's amount — or several fields, drawn as concentric rings, outer first. |
| label | string | — | What the chart shows. Its accessible name and the caption of the data table assistive tech reads. |
| categories | Record<string, { label?: string; tone?: ChartTone; color?: string; icon?: string }> | — | Labels, tones and icons per slice, keyed by the slice's name. Unlisted slices take the tones in order. |
| className | string | "h-64" | Sizes the chart. Set a height. |
| donut | boolean \| number | false | Cut out the middle: `true` for a ring at 60% of the radius, or a ratio (0–0.9). |
| centerLabel | { value: string; label?: string } | — | A value and caption in the hole of a donut. |
| separator | boolean | true | A hairline in the surface colour between slices. |
| labels | "none" \| "outside" \| "inside" | "none" | Label each slice outside the pie or inside it. |
| labelContent | "value" \| "percent" \| "name" | "value" | What a slice label says. |
| legend | boolean | true unless slices are labelled | Show the legend. |
| tooltip | boolean \| { indicator?: "dot" \| "line" \| "dashed" \| "none"; hideLabel?: boolean; labelFormatter?: (label, datum) => ReactNode; showTotal?: boolean } | true | Show a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, or configure it: the row marker, hiding the heading, rewriting it, adding a Total row. |
| valueFormatter | (value: number) => string | — | Format values everywhere (axis, labels, tooltip, table) — units like "$12,480". Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere. |
| locale | string | runtime locale | BCP 47 locale for default number and date formatting. |
| animate | boolean | true | Sweep the slices in clockwise when the chart scrolls into view. |
| activeIndex | number \| null | — | The highlighted row (controlled); `null` for none. |
| defaultActiveIndex | number \| null | — | The row highlighted at first — a tooltip already open before anyone hovers. |
| onActiveIndexChange | (index: number \| null) => void | — | Called as the pointer or keyboard moves between rows. |

## Tokens used

`tone-edition`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-standard`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `foreground`, `background`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Slices · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Once on screen the slices are revealed by a mask that sweeps clockwise from 12 o'clock — the whole is read as it fills. On the motion tokens; reduced motion shows the finished chart.
- **response** · Active slice · _no motion_ — The hovered slice pulls outward and the rest dim at once; the geometry change itself eases (see transition).
- **transition** · Slices · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Geometry eases from the old shape to the new one through a CSS `d` transition on the motion tokens (no recipe animates path geometry); browsers without `d` transitions update in place.
- **activity** · PieChart · _no motion_ — A chart has no indeterminate state; show a Skeleton while the data loads.

## Accessibility

- The drawing is aria-hidden; the same numbers are in a visually hidden data table (captioned by `label`) that the chart is aria-describedby, so assistive tech reads values, not shapes.
- With a tooltip, the chart is one tab stop (role=group, aria-roledescription="chart"): arrow keys, Home and End step through the data, Escape clears, and each step is announced in a polite live region.
- Colour is never the only key: series are named in the legend, tooltip and table.

## Related

- Components: SegmentedBar, RadialChart, BarChart, Card

## Examples

### Donut with a total

```tsx
import { PieChart } from "@sableui/react"

const sources = [
	{ source: "Search", visitors: 275 },
	{ source: "Direct", visitors: 200 },
	{ source: "Social", visitors: 187 },
	{ source: "Email", visitors: 90 },
]

<PieChart
	label="Visitors by source"
	data={sources}
	index="source"
	valueKey="visitors"
	donut
	centerLabel={{ value: "752", label: "Visitors" }}
/>
```

### Labelled slices

```tsx
import { PieChart } from "@sableui/react"

<PieChart
	label="Share of visitors by source"
	data={sources}
	index="source"
	valueKey="visitors"
	labels="outside"
	labelContent="percent"
	categories={{ Search: { tone: "primary" }, Email: { tone: "neutral" } }}
/>
```

# Pill

**Status:** stable

A chip someone clicks: a filter, a tag choice, an option in a row. Always a button with aria-pressed. appearance="solid" (filters; selected lifts onto the primary surface) or "outline" (quiet chips that annotate content, like reactions); size md or sm. A static label is a Badge.

**Keywords:** pill, chip, filter, tag, toggle chip, category

## Usage

Use Pill for a row of filters or choices a person clicks to narrow or toggle what they see. For a label that only describes something, use Badge.

### Best practices

- Do: Use short text that names the filter or choice.
- Do: Reflect the current choice with selected, so the active filter reads at a glance.
- Don't: Do not use Pill as a static label. A pressable-looking chip that does nothing is the most common cause of dead clicks in a filter row — that is a Badge.
- Don't: Do not use Pill for primary actions or important system status.
- Don't: Do not restyle a Pill with border or background classes to get a quieter chip. That is appearance="outline" (and size="sm" for a small one); an override is a look that exists nowhere else in the system.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| selected | boolean | false | Marks the pill as chosen. Solid lifts onto the primary surface; outline takes a primary tint and soft primary edge. Sets aria-pressed. |
| appearance | "solid" \| "outline" | "solid" | solid for a filter row; outline for quiet chips that annotate other content (a reaction under a message, a tag on a card), where a filled chip would compete with what it annotates. |
| size | "md" \| "sm" | "md" | md sits on the density ladder's xs control height (28px); sm is 24px, for chips under or inside other content. |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Optional leading glyph (e.g. <Icon name="lock" />), rendered before the children with the base gap. |

## Variants

- **appearance**: solid, outline
- **size**: md, sm
- **selected**: true, false

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `card`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <button type="button"> for focus and keyboard activation.
- Selected state is exposed via aria-pressed.

## Related

- Components: Badge, ToggleGroup

## Examples

### Filter row

```tsx
import { Pill, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Pill selected onClick={() => {}}>All</Pill><Pill onClick={() => {}}>Editions</Pill><Pill onClick={() => {}}>Collectibles</Pill></Row>
```

### Outline, small (reactions)

```tsx
import { Pill, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Pill appearance="outline" size="sm" selected onClick={() => {}}>🎉 3</Pill><Pill appearance="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => {}}>👀</Pill></Row>
```

### With icon

```tsx
import { Icon, Pill } from "@sableui/react"

<Pill icon={<Icon name="lock" />} onClick={() => {}}>Locked</Pill>
```

# Popover

**Status:** stable

Click-triggered overlay over Base UI Popover (focus management, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal). Holds interactive content; 18rem-wide surface.

**Keywords:** popover, floating panel, anchored, disclosure

## Usage

Use Popover for anchored secondary content that needs more room than a tooltip but less commitment than a dialog.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for small pickers, summaries, or contextual controls tied to a trigger.
- Do: Keep focus behavior and dismissal predictable.
- Don't: Do not use Popover for blocking confirmations, long forms, or critical information.
- Don't: Do not put a form that can fail validation inside one. A popover dismisses on outside click, which discards what the user typed with no warning — that is a Dialog.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PopoverTrigger | yes | The element that anchors and opens the popover. |
| PopoverContent | yes | The floating content surface. |
| PopoverTitle | no | An optional heading for the content. |
| PopoverDescription | no | Optional supporting copy. |
| PopoverClose | no | An explicit close control when helpful. |
| PopoverArrow | no | An optional arrow pointing to the trigger. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PopoverTrigger | Base UI Trigger props + render | The anchor element. Use render={<Button/>} to compose with another component. |
| PopoverContent | Base UI Popup props + side: "top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-*" + align: "start" \| "center" \| "end" + sideOffset: number + anchor: Element \| Ref \| (() => Element) \| VirtualElement + className | Portals + positions + paints the popup. side picks which side of the trigger to render against (auto-flips on collision; defaults to "bottom"); align sets alignment along that side (defaults to "center"); sideOffset is the gap in px (defaults to 8). anchor positions against a different element/ref/getter than the trigger — Base UI 1.5 has no separate Anchor part, so pass it here to decouple the open-location from the trigger. |
| PopoverTitle | Base UI Title props + className | Accessible heading; Base UI wires aria-labelledby to the popup. |
| PopoverDescription | Base UI Description props + className | Supplementary copy; Base UI wires aria-describedby to the popup. |
| PopoverClose | Base UI Close props + render | A button that closes the popover. Use render={<Button/>} to compose. |
| PopoverArrow | Base UI Arrow props + className | Optional pointer connecting the popup to its trigger. Place inside PopoverContent. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Popover (Root) | Base UI Popover.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal) | — | Groups the trigger and content. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border-floating`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI manages focus into and out of the popup, traps focus when modal, and restores focus to the trigger on close.
- Opens on trigger press (click/Enter/Space); dismisses on Esc and outside press.
- PopoverTitle/PopoverDescription wire aria-labelledby/aria-describedby on the popup.
- Enters and exits on the motion-pop recipe (Base UI starting/ending-style attributes), so it follows the motion policy.

## Related

- Components: Tooltip, ContextCard, Dialog

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Popover><PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Details</Button>} /><PopoverContent><PopoverTitle>Edition details</PopoverTitle><PopoverDescription>A limited run of 100, stored permanently on Arweave.</PopoverDescription></PopoverContent></Popover>
```

### With close

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Popover><PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Open</Button>} /><PopoverContent><PopoverTitle>Heads up</PopoverTitle><PopoverDescription>Collecting mints a compressed NFT to your wallet.</PopoverDescription><PopoverClose render={<Button size="sm">Got it</Button>} /></PopoverContent></Popover>
```

# Progress

**Status:** stable

Linear progress bar over Base UI Progress — value 0–100 drives the fill; omit value (or pass null) for an indeterminate, pulsing bar.

**Keywords:** progress, task progress, meter, loading

## Usage

Use Progress to communicate determinate or indeterminate completion for a task or process.

### Best practices

- Do: Use determinate values when progress can be measured.
- Do: Pair the visual indicator with text when users need context or exact values.
- Don't: Do not use Progress as a decorative divider or status color bar.
- Don't: Do not use a determinate Progress for an unknown duration. A bar that sits at 90% is worse than a Spinner, because it makes a promise about time that you cannot keep.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ProgressTrack | yes | The background track that defines the range. |
| ProgressIndicator | yes | The filled or animated progress indicator. |
| ProgressLabel | no | A text label for the progress task. |
| ProgressValue | no | A readable value such as 45 percent. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ProgressTrack | Base UI Track props + className | The rail. Rendered automatically when Progress has no children; renders a ProgressIndicator child by default. Takes `size` (inherited from Progress) for its thickness — use that rather than a className height. |
| ProgressIndicator | Base UI Indicator props + className | The fill. Width is set by Base UI from the value; spans full width and pulses while indeterminate. |
| ProgressLabel | Base UI Label props + className | Accessible label; wires aria-labelledby on the Root. |
| ProgressValue | Base UI Value props + className | Formatted value readout. Accepts a render-function child for custom formatting. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| null | null | Current value between min and max. null (or omitted) renders the indeterminate state. |
| min | number | 0 | The minimum value of the range. |
| max | number | 100 | The maximum value of the range. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Formatting options for ProgressValue (e.g. style: 'percent', or a currency). |
| getAriaValueText | (formatted, value) => string | — | Returns a human-readable text alternative for aria-valuenow. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Bar thickness, on the same three rails as Meter so the two match on one page. ProgressTrack inherits it. |

## Variants

- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `primary`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A progress bar appears because work started. Staging its entrance delays the one piece of information the reader is waiting for.
- **response** · Root · _no motion_ — It reports; it does not accept input. A bar that reacted to the pointer would read as a Slider, which is a control the reader can drag.
- **transition** · ProgressIndicator · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Fill width eases between values on the motion tokens (no recipe animates width), so the bar reads as filling rather than as a series of unrelated widths. It matters most where progress arrives in coarse jumps — four chunked upload callbacks look like a glitching bar without it.
- **activity** · ProgressIndicator · `motion-pulse` — Indeterminate (value null) has no width to animate, so the pulse carries the whole signal that work is still happening. Without it the indeterminate state is a static bar — indistinguishable from a stalled determinate one.

## Accessibility

- Base UI sets role=progressbar with aria-valuenow / aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax and reports status to screen readers.
- Indeterminate state (value null) omits aria-valuenow per the ARIA spec.
- Pair ProgressLabel with the bar for a visible, associated name; ProgressValue exposes the formatted value.

## Related

- Components: Spinner, Skeleton

## Examples

### Determinate

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress value={64} aria-label="Upload" />
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress aria-label="Preparing export" />
```

### With label and value

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressTrack, ProgressValue } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress value={40}><div className="mb-2 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1"><ProgressLabel>Uploading</ProgressLabel><ProgressValue /></div><ProgressTrack /></Progress>
```

# RadarChart

**Status:** beta

Several measures compared around a centre: one polygon per series over a polygon or circular web, filled or outline only, with optional dots, a radius scale and a tinted web. Polygons grow from the centre as the chart scrolls into view.

**Keywords:** chart, radar, spider, web, profile, skills, comparison, polar

## Usage

Use RadarChart to compare the shape of a profile across five to eight dimensions — skills, product scores, a cycle of months — for one to three series. The shape is the message; for exact values or more than three series, BarChart is easier to read.

### Best practices

- Do: Keep every spoke on the same scale and direction (more is better on all of them).
- Do: Use filled={false} when two polygons overlap heavily, so both outlines stay visible.
- Don't: Use fewer than five spokes — three or four make a triangle or square that says little; use BarChart.
- Don't: Use it for data-heavy views — streaming or real-time data, thousands of points, zoom and brushing, trading charts. Those belong on a charting library (Recharts, visx, ECharts); Sable's charts are for dashboards, landing pages and decks.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | Record<string, unknown>[] | — | One row per spoke. |
| index | string | — | The datum field naming each spoke. |
| series | { key: string; label: string; tone?: ChartTone; color?: string; icon?: string }[] | — | The measures to plot: the datum field, its name in the legend/tooltip/table, and its colour (a tone by role, or any CSS colour). Omitted, series take the chart palette in order: --chart-1 … --chart-8, validated for colour-blind separation in light and dark; a theme may override the set. |
| label | string | — | What the chart shows. Its accessible name and the caption of the data table assistive tech reads. |
| className | string | "h-72" | Sizes the chart. Set a height. |
| grid | "polygon" \| "circle" \| "none" | "polygon" | The web behind the polygons. |
| gridFill | boolean | false | Tint the web's outer area. |
| filled | boolean | true | Fill each polygon; `false` draws outlines only. |
| dots | boolean | false | Mark every vertex with a dot. |
| radiusAxis | boolean | false | Print the ring values along the top spoke. |
| legend | boolean | true when there is more than one series | Show the legend. |
| tooltip | boolean \| { indicator?: "dot" \| "line" \| "dashed" \| "none"; hideLabel?: boolean; labelFormatter?: (label, datum) => ReactNode; showTotal?: boolean } | true | Show a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, or configure it: the row marker, hiding the heading, rewriting it, adding a Total row. |
| valueFormatter | (value: number) => string | — | Format values everywhere (axis, labels, tooltip, table) — units like "$12,480". Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere. |
| locale | string | runtime locale | BCP 47 locale for default number and date formatting. |
| animate | boolean | true | Grow the polygons from the centre when the chart scrolls into view. |
| activeIndex | number \| null | — | The highlighted row (controlled); `null` for none. |
| defaultActiveIndex | number \| null | — | The row highlighted at first — a tooltip already open before anyone hovers. |
| onActiveIndexChange | (index: number \| null) => void | — | Called as the pointer or keyboard moves between rows. |

## Tokens used

`tone-edition`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-standard`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `foreground`, `background`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Polygon · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Once on screen each polygon grows from the centre and fades in, series staggered, on the emphasized easing. On the motion tokens; reduced motion shows the finished chart.
- **response** · Active spoke · _no motion_ — The hovered spoke's vertices and label highlight at once.
- **transition** · Polygon · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Geometry eases from the old shape to the new one through a CSS `d` transition on the motion tokens (no recipe animates path geometry); browsers without `d` transitions update in place.
- **activity** · RadarChart · _no motion_ — A chart has no indeterminate state; show a Skeleton while the data loads.

## Accessibility

- The drawing is aria-hidden; the same numbers are in a visually hidden data table (captioned by `label`) that the chart is aria-describedby, so assistive tech reads values, not shapes.
- With a tooltip, the chart is one tab stop (role=group, aria-roledescription="chart"): arrow keys, Home and End step through the data, Escape clears, and each step is announced in a polite live region.
- Colour is never the only key: series are named in the legend, tooltip and table.

## Related

- Components: BarChart, LineChart, Card

## Examples

### Two profiles

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from "@sableui/react"

const scores = [
	{ skill: "Speed", a: 86, b: 65 },
	{ skill: "Quality", a: 72, b: 90 },
	{ skill: "Support", a: 64, b: 80 },
	{ skill: "Price", a: 90, b: 55 },
	{ skill: "Docs", a: 70, b: 85 },
	{ skill: "Ecosystem", a: 60, b: 75 },
]

<RadarChart
	label="Product scores compared"
	data={scores}
	index="skill"
	series={[
		{ key: "a", label: "Atlas" },
		{ key: "b", label: "Beacon" },
	]}
/>
```

### Circular web, outlines only

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from "@sableui/react"

<RadarChart
	label="Atlas scores"
	data={scores}
	index="skill"
	series={[{ key: "a", label: "Atlas" }]}
	grid="circle"
	gridFill
	filled={false}
	dots
/>
```

# RadialChart

**Status:** beta

Progress or share as rings: one ring per row against a muted track, a full circle or a gauge (`sweep`), one ring split between rows (`stacked`), ring labels and a value in the middle. Rings draw round as the chart scrolls into view.

**Keywords:** chart, radial, ring, gauge, progress, goal, score, activity rings, donut

## Usage

Use RadialChart for progress toward goals (several rings), a single score or usage gauge (`sweep={180}` with `centerLabel`), or a split of one total along a gauge (`stacked`). For one reading in a form or settings row, Meter's ring shape is lighter.

### Best practices

- Do: Set max to the goal, so a full ring means "done".
- Do: Pair a gauge with centerLabel stating the value in words or units.
- Don't: Compare more than four rings — inner rings are shorter for the same value, which misleads; use BarChart.
- Don't: Use it for data-heavy views — streaming or real-time data, thousands of points, zoom and brushing, trading charts. Those belong on a charting library (Recharts, visx, ECharts); Sable's charts are for dashboards, landing pages and decks.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | Record<string, unknown>[] | — | One row per ring, outermost first. |
| index | string | — | The datum field naming each ring. |
| valueKey | string | — | The datum field holding each ring's amount. |
| label | string | — | What the chart shows. Its accessible name and the caption of the data table assistive tech reads. |
| categories | Record<string, { label?: string; tone?: ChartTone; color?: string; icon?: string }> | — | Labels, tones and icons per ring, keyed by the ring's name. |
| className | string | "h-64" | Sizes the chart. Set a height. |
| max | number | the largest value (stacked: the total; labelled: the largest value ÷ 0.75, leaving room for the labels) | The value a full ring stands for. |
| sweep | number | 360 | How far round a full ring runs, in degrees: 360 for a circle, 180 for a gauge. |
| stacked | boolean | false | Split ONE ring between the rows instead of a ring each. |
| track | boolean | true | Draw each ring's full track behind it. |
| labels | boolean | false | Name each ring at its start. |
| centerLabel | { value: string; label?: string } | — | A value and caption in the middle. |
| legend | boolean | true unless rings are labelled | Show the legend. |
| tooltip | boolean \| { indicator?: "dot" \| "line" \| "dashed" \| "none"; hideLabel?: boolean; labelFormatter?: (label, datum) => ReactNode; showTotal?: boolean } | true | Show a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, or configure it: the row marker, hiding the heading, rewriting it, adding a Total row. |
| valueFormatter | (value: number) => string | — | Format values everywhere (axis, labels, tooltip, table) — units like "$12,480". Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere. |
| locale | string | runtime locale | BCP 47 locale for default number and date formatting. |
| animate | boolean | true | Draw the rings round from their start when the chart scrolls into view. |
| activeIndex | number \| null | — | The highlighted row (controlled); `null` for none. |
| defaultActiveIndex | number \| null | — | The row highlighted at first — a tooltip already open before anyone hovers. |
| onActiveIndexChange | (index: number \| null) => void | — | Called as the pointer or keyboard moves between rows. |

## Tokens used

`tone-edition`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-standard`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `foreground`, `background`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Ring · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Once on screen each ring draws round from its start (stroke-dashoffset on a round-capped arc), staggered outside in. On the motion tokens; reduced motion shows the finished chart.
- **response** · Active ring · _no motion_ — The hovered ring stays full strength and the others dim at once.
- **transition** · Ring · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Geometry eases from the old shape to the new one through a CSS `d` transition on the motion tokens (no recipe animates path geometry); browsers without `d` transitions update in place.
- **activity** · RadialChart · _no motion_ — A chart has no indeterminate state; show a Skeleton while the data loads.

## Accessibility

- The drawing is aria-hidden; the same numbers are in a visually hidden data table (captioned by `label`) that the chart is aria-describedby, so assistive tech reads values, not shapes.
- With a tooltip, the chart is one tab stop (role=group, aria-roledescription="chart"): arrow keys, Home and End step through the data, Escape clears, and each step is announced in a polite live region.
- Colour is never the only key: series are named in the legend, tooltip and table.

## Related

- Components: Meter, PieChart, Progress, Card

## Examples

### Goal rings

```tsx
import { RadialChart } from "@sableui/react"

<RadialChart
	label="Weekly goals"
	data={[
		{ goal: "Move", progress: 82 },
		{ goal: "Exercise", progress: 64 },
		{ goal: "Stand", progress: 91 },
	]}
	index="goal"
	valueKey="progress"
	max={100}
	labels
/>
```

### Gauge with a value

```tsx
import { RadialChart } from "@sableui/react"

<RadialChart
	label="Plan usage"
	data={[{ plan: "Used", gb: 7.2 }]}
	index="plan"
	valueKey="gb"
	max={10}
	sweep={180}
	centerLabel={{ value: "7.2 GB", label: "of 10 GB" }}
	legend={false}
/>
```

# Radio

**Status:** stable

Single-select control over Base UI RadioGroup + Radio (roving focus, arrow-key nav, ARIA radiogroup wiring, form integration). RadioGroup + Radio.

**Keywords:** radio, radio group, single choice, form control

## Usage

Use Radio when a user must choose exactly one option from a visible set.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it when all options should be visible for comparison.
- Do: Keep option labels mutually exclusive and easy to understand.
- Don't: Do not use Radio for independent toggles or multiple selection; use Checkbox or Switch.
- Don't: Do not use a radio group with only one option, and do not omit the Fieldset. Without the fieldset the options share no accessible name, so a screen reader reads the choices with no question attached.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | yes | The grouped set that manages one selected value. |
| Radio | yes | One selectable option in the group. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | Base UI RadioGroup props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange, name, disabled, readOnly, required) + className | The group container that wraps Radio items and shares selection state across them. Controlled via value + onValueChange; uncontrolled via defaultValue. Lays its Radio items out in a vertical stack. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Radio | Base UI Radio.Root props (value, disabled, readOnly, required) + className | — | A single radio button. value pairs it with the group's selected value. Renders a native button with radio semantics, the ring and an inner Indicator dot. A custom non-button render must also set nativeButton={false}. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `primary`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the radiogroup/radio roles, aria-checked, hidden native inputs, and roving tabindex.
- Arrow keys move and select between items; Space selects the focused item; Tab enters/leaves the group.
- Checked state styling reads from the data-[checked] attribute; disabled items from the disabled state.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring on the focused item. Wrap each Radio in <Field label orientation="horizontal"> so the label names it, is part of the hit target, sits on the first line, and dims with it when disabled — do not hand-build a <label> row.

## Related

- Components: Checkbox, RadioCard, Field, Fieldset, Select

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Post type</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<RadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
			<Field label="Standard" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="standard" /></Field>
			<Field label="Edition" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="edition" /></Field>
		</RadioGroup>
	</FieldsetContent>
</Fieldset>
```

### With a disabled option

```tsx
import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Post type</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<RadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
			<Field label="Standard" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="standard" /></Field>
			<Field label="Edition" orientation="horizontal" disabled><Radio value="edition" /></Field>
		</RadioGroup>
	</FieldsetContent>
</Fieldset>
```
